Instead, I often identify with activities outside of academia to give my mind the rest it needs to stay sharp and focused. I feel most comfortable when I am out in the woods setting up a tripod for the perfect photograph to add to my growing portfolio or when I am at the beach soaking in my weekly dose of sunlight. It's such a therapeutic sensation to be connected to the outdoors and it is this mentality that keeps me healthy all around. But apart from my love of the outdoors, I spent the last 8 years practicing classical Indian dance and have been honored as one of the youngest students in the world to receive a Bachelor of Dance (Bharatanatyam) from the Art Society of Mumbai. To date, this is my proudest accomplishment. Dance is not only a part of my heritage, but it is an exquisite form of self-expression and a rich form of cultural narrative.

essays.promptLabel: Topic that makes you lose track of time
essays.prompt: Describe a topic, idea, or concept you find so engaging that it makes you lose all track of time. Why does it captivate you? What or who do you turn to when you want to learn more?
essays.essay:
From a young age, I was captivated by the realm of computers, surrounded by the influences of my parents who worked in the software industry. I vividly recall moments of exhilaration as they revealed the mysteries behind Google searches, YouTube videos, and text messaging. These moments ignited a curiosity within me, one that eventually blossomed into an unwavering passion for Computer Science.

Starting my journey of programming, I learned Python and Java while also developing simple projects. As I advanced my knowledge in these languages, I began to devote my focus to competitive programming, specifically USACO. Competitive programming truly tested my critical thinking skills by forcing me to create solutions that were “out-of-the-box.” An unforgettable night marked my qualification for the silver division. I had to solve four challenging problems to advance to the next division. I scribbled, sketched, and refined my algorithms numerous times on paper, trying to find a valid solution. I couldn't simply brute force a solution, rather I needed to create the most efficient algorithm. With minutes to spare, I submitted my code and watched the green checks appear sequentially, each one increasing my happiness levels. In that moment, as the delight traveled through my veins, I realized that my passion for problem solving was key in persuading me to pursue Computer Science.

As I continued to progress in competitive programming, I yearned for a transition where I could create my own applications. This aspiration led me to discover full-stack development, where I joined Revoteen, a social media startup with over ten thousand users. My excellent work as an intern allowed me to transition to an employee and remain on the team for the acquisition phase.

Working at Revoteen was phenomenal as I learned new technologies and was able to work to create new features on the webpage. I remember when I was tasked with developing a chat feature for user interaction. I was excited because this was my first major task at the company, so I wanted to do my best. I woke up in the morning and opened up my code editor to start creating the API. As I continued to work on the feature, I noticed an issue with the requests not being properly processed. Using my problem-solving skills, I traversed through each line of code, meticulously debugging and experimenting with different approaches to fix the error.

After multiple hours of strenuous work, trying to fix the bug, I realized the error originated from a deprecated component that I had used. After creating an alternative component that was far more efficient, a wave of joy surged through me as I saw the chat message sent successfully on the website. It is these moments, when time seems to be irrelevant and the pursuit of a valid solution overcomes my every thought, that lead me to be enthralled by the beauty of programming. In this specific scenario, I was able to utilize my critical thinking to solve the problem, but there are other instances where the solution is more intricate and complex. In those times, I turn to my favorite YouTube channel, Fireship. His videos have guided me through the most difficult problems as he explains each technology and framework in such a way that I can debug my own errors.

My experiences have shaped my journey and solidified my dedication to Computer Science. From collaborating with companies to creating remarkable projects, from participating in arduous competitions to mastering new technologies, these undertakings have cultivated my problem-solving, teamwork, and programming skills. My passion for coding has not only instilled a desire to pursue it at a higher level, but it has also molded me into a resourceful, innovative, and intelligent individual. When I program, I can tune out all of the distractions. It's just me and the code. Programming, to me, is a form of art–a realm where your imagination is the only limit. This is why I adore it.

essays.promptLabel: Topic that makes you lose track of time
essays.prompt: Describe a topic, idea, or concept you find so engaging that it makes you lose all track of time. Why does it captivate you? What or who do you turn to when you want to learn more?
essays.essay:
I fondly remember my eighth-grade Python debut. Clicking the green run button, I watched gracefully as the numbers seven through nineteen were printed on the screen. It was magical, and I couldn't resist hitting the button repeatedly, grinning as the numbers danced across the command prompt.

It was astounding to think that I, a mere middle schooler, wrote a set of instructions for such a complex system. It felt surreal, and I couldn't contain my excitement. I quickly grabbed my machine and raced for the master bedroom, where I found my dad crafting his own elegant code for work. His display was a vibrant canvas of colorful lines, far more intricate than mine. I tapped on his shoulder and quietly presented my for-loop code. His reaction was reserved, and he said, “Next time, add another loop,” but I knew deep inside he was brimming with pride.

Since that interaction, I've embraced the world of tech. My Palenight-themed VSCode editor always adorned my monitor, and Fireship's YouTube channel kept me company. I settled into my quiet room, relishing the solitude and watching the sky change from blue to black each day. The only noises I heard were the clicks from my Macbook keyboard and the hungry growls from my stomach. It didn't matter, though—I was full of code.

Fast forward a few years, I landed an internship at Revoteen, a vibrant social media startup that fueled my passion for computer science. I began my journey by downloading the GitHub repository, creating a Linux subsystem, and learning the nuances of Next.js.

Whenever a new task was assigned to me, I eagerly embraced it. With Airpods in and my favorite TV show, “All American,” playing, I was ready. As I listened to the intense dialogue from the show, my fingers bashed the keyboard in a furious metronome of coding. Toggling left and right, alternating between my code window and the web application, I remained focused. With every new line of digital poetry, I marveled as the website reloaded in real-time, instantly converting my changes into vibrant components. The JSX file was roaring with colors, like the sea of beauty I saw on my dad's screen that day. There were method identifiers, imports, constants, and states—all the elements that would make any developer proud. These blocks joined together, weaving the web page in front of me. It was mesmerizing.

Even the errors contributed to the work of art, giving my code a distinct charm. I didn't find these bugs troublesome; they were like gasoline added to an already present flame. That flame within me wasn't dying because I was going to finish this feature. Adding “console.log” statements to every line to debug the issue wasn't tedious or annoying—it was fulfilling. Each log was one step closer to solving the problem. When my efforts paid off after correcting my erroneous code, I felt a sense of joy as I deleted each “console.log” one by one. At last, the file was clean and complete.

Restarting the terminal and committing my changes gave me genuine satisfaction as I saw each file added to the staging area. After typing “git push,” I witnessed these files being concurrently uploaded to the remote repository. I opened the pull request page on GitHub. My code was labeled “commit 95dc5dd.” I clicked the rectangular, green merge button. I anxiously waited as my code was being tested. 1/10 test cases passed. Then 3/10. Then 9/10. After a few seconds, the test case indicator proudly displayed a green check mark, indicating my success.

These moments where I can sit in my gaming chair, put on a show, and create something that benefits others are the reason I adore programming. When I program, I tune out all of the distractions. It's just me and the digital canvas. Coding, to me, is a form of art–a realm where your imagination is the only limit.

essays.prompt: Duke University seeks a talented, engaged student body that embodies the wide range of human experience; we believe that the diversity of our students makes our community stronger. If you'd like to share a perspective you bring or experiences you've had to help us understand you better - perhaps related to a community you belong to, your sexual orientation or gender identity, or your family or cultural background - we encourage you to do so. (250 word limit)
essays.essay:
One checking of Duke's website informing me about its emphasis on diversity/inclusion most certainly helps into cementing how it is the best place for a girl like me to further my dreams of practicing medicine. It is quite an exciting time for women in the field, and Duke's male-to-female ratio in every department is quite an inspiring feat for a campus.

Although I was born in the United States, my parents have always tried to raise me within the supplementary confines of my Indian ethnicity. This amalgamation of two cultures have led me into exploring not just the sciences but also the liberal arts where I turned into practicing and preserving the flair of my rich South-Asian culture side-by-side with my alignment to American lifestyle.

Aside from many notable activities which centered mostly in the field of medicine-related research and hospital work, one might be surprised with how equally supporting my peers had been when it came to how I relate my individuality and creative streaks. I was immediately entranced when I was first exposed to our arts that I took 8 years of Indian classical dance and Indian classical singing. This experience allowed me to learn about what it means to be multicultural, and how our many equal societies further America's democratic virtues.

At Duke, I aspire to do just the same - taking with me my determination of learning about new cultures and local customs while sharing my personal core principles of curiosity and harmonic, diplomatic nature.

essays.prompt: Tell us about an experience in the past year or two that reflects your imagination, creativity, or intellect. (250 words)
essays.essay:
My nonprofit Overstress began as a medium to address the adverse mental health effects of the Covid pandemic. Instead of tackling this issue with old methods, my cofounder and I worked to imbue creativity into our process. At the time, I was enamored with the idea of upcycling. As a tennis player, the most glaring waste I encountered was discarded tennis balls. Could this be the solution we were looking for?

Immediately, I began scouring my local area for anything we could leverage. After calling various landscape companies around my area, a few agreed to use landscape chippers to shred the discarded tennis balls to be repurposed. After attempting to use a landscaper (and failing spectacularly), I looked online and reached out to another nonprofit - Recycleballs. There, they used massive machines to mince tennis balls into a simple resin. They agreed to work with us, and in the following weeks, we collected hundreds of tennis balls which were then converted into a fluffy substance we utilized to create squishy stress balls.

At Duke, I'd hope to continue injecting creativity to find solutions. With an undergraduate class that is uniquely engaged, I could bring over my stress balls on a far greater scale than at home. Or, I could once again channel the creativity of upcycling to find new ways to help the Blue Devil community - perhaps turning discarded student notes into school flyers for game days. At Duke, the opportunities are endless, and I can't wait to make my mark.

essays.prompt: We recognize that not fully "fitting in" a community or place can sometimes be difficult. Duke values the effort, resilience, and independence that may require. Feel free to share with us circumstances where something about you is different and how that's influenced your experiences or identity. (250 words)
essays.essay:
As the son of a Turkish mother and Dutch father, yet living in America, my life feels like a conundrum. Born on American soil, there's no doubt I'm American, except that until preschool I only responded to a mix of Turkish and Dutch. Travelling to Turkey and the Netherlands over 14 times each, there's no doubt I'm an international native, except I've never lived outside the US. Quite simply, I'm an outsider.

While I'll never have both feet in one community, I'm okay with that. Rather than wallow in what I can't change, I've strived to build bridges between the international and American aspects of my identity. When I worked with Kobac general trading in Somalia, I helped standardize their English application for Innowwide EU. When I interned at EY Istanbul, I made global friends by talking about eccentric interests I explore at home ranging from tennis to pokemon cards.

Over the years, I've continued to grow outside the labels that define me. While travelling abroad has always been about visiting family, since high school I've utilized this opportunity to explore internships. In the future, I aim to continue to use this gift of travel to inspire meaningful change. I still have much to learn, but with Duke's collaborative International Guide program or even by hosting informal food exchanges, I hope to be the bridge-builder who unites my fellow students. Regardless of whether I am Turkish, Dutch, or American, I'll continue to do what I do best: bring people together.

essays.prompt: If you are applying to the Trinity College of Arts and Sciences as a first year applicant, please discuss why you consider Duke a good match for you. Is there something particular about Duke that attracts you? (Please limit your response to no more than 250 words.)
essays.essay:
With the luxury of Duke University's surroundings, Trinity College of Arts and Sciences' global recognition of its research facilities, the access to groundbreaking technological advances and medicinal research, and North Carolina's fast-paced urban lifestyle - I find myself already readying into adapting into the next thrilling experience of my life.

Duke's motto, "Eruditio et Religio" (Knowledge and Faith), resonates well within me. As a budding physician, I have always dedicated time into proper research and learning opportunities. But I have also always tried to remind myself that all the things we do in life must be in the good service of humanity as a whole. I've had some time put in as a volunteer in a Veterans Affairs hospital where I've experienced the cultural and generational gaps with those who are my age and those who fought for our country, and saw first-hand how both science and faith worked hand-in-hand in keeping the veterans' will to live comfortably and peacefully adjusting back into society.

As I have always been a curious person who found being challenged by new surroundings exhilarating, I am always prepared to advance my understanding of neuroscience and psychology in a place whose foremost focus is academic excellence. I have no doubt Duke is also the perfect place for me to find and expound on strategic plans when it comes to future career decisions. And I hope I will be allowed to find new meaningful experiences and add color to the campus's already-vibrant surroundings.

essays.prompt: What is your sense of Duke as a university and a community, and why do you consider it a good match for you? If there's something in particular about our offerings that attracts you, feel free to share that as well. (250 word limit)
essays.essay:
On the night of February 6, 2023, a devastating 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the Turkey-Syrian border, leaving thousands of families shattered. My heart sank. Among them were my friends, a community of Turkish and Syrian children that I became a part of through weekly online English lessons. Now they needed my help.

Yet, unsure of what to do, I called out to my school for help. Here, I saw the power of an engaged community as the leadership team collaborated with me to host a fundraiser for the disaster. Together, we set up donation jars, raised class competitions, and even hosted pizza events to collect money. In the following weeks, I saw hundreds of students actively engage, doing so much to help people they had never met before. This experience moved me.

Following that event, I strived to be more engaged in my community. Whether through small acts like staying 5 minutes overtime in peer tutoring or larger ones like leading a tennis teaching organization to aid seniors in my community, I've made it my duty to help others. And yet, nowhere else is there as strong a school connection as at Duke. The Duke community rallies together, shows up to every event, and engages meaningfully both at home and abroad like in their record-breaking sports events or incredible Duke Engage program. Above all, in the unfortunate situation that a disaster like this occurs again, I know that at Duke there will be endless people ready to help.

essays.promptLabel: A creative work made for you
essays.prompt: Which book, character, song, monologue, or other creative work (fiction or non-fiction) seems made for you? Why? (150 words)
essays.essay: The song "Time Adventure" by Rebecca Sugar intertwines with my childhood to the deepest parts. It was officially released when my favorite show of all time (Adventure Time) came to an end. The lyrics "will happen, happening, happened" changed the way I thought about my every move. I discovered that there is no need to dwell on past mistakes, and instead focus on the present. I discovered that although I know there are things to come in the future, I can approach it when the time comes. Even when things go south, I did what I did and maybe it was fate for me to end up on a different path in life than how I intended. That is my version of will happen, happening, happened.

essays.prompt: What academic areas are you interested in exploring at Emory University and why? (200 words)
essays.essay:
What started as a curiosity has grown into a deep interest in learning about the framework that influences how cities and roads are developed. Before long, zoning laws had become my endless supply of dopamine. In my spare time watching videos and reading urban planning documents, I learned that what may seem like hundreds of rules are really the fabrics that build the tapestry of a city.

Going to Japan last summer, I was intrigued by their mere 12 zones compared to the over 100 we have in North America! These zoning arrangements in Japan were genius in that each one builds on top of the other to foster urban growth. This explains why a shop serving sizzling takoyaki can be right next to a single-family home and why a business district can be a stone's throw away from a school. By contrast, the U.S relies on Euclidean zoning, which creates exclusive zones that make racial divide and economic struggle more prominent in some places than others.

If I had more space to share, I'd share a small journal worth of insights, but I'll save that for my peers at Emory! Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got more streets to explore.

essays.prompt: Emory University has a strong commitment to building community. Tell us about a community you have been part of where your participation helped to change or shape the community for the better. (150 words)
essays.essay:
On February 6, 2023, a 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck the Southeast Turkey and Syrian border, leaving thousands of families shattered. My heart sank. Among them were my friends, a community I joined through weekly English lessons. Now they needed my help.

Immediately, I launched a fundraiser for impacted Turkish and Syrian children and gathered first-hand stories from affected families. By sharing these stories, slowly more and more people took action. With my school's supportive leadership program, we set up pizza competitions, school newsletter stories, and donation jars across campus, raising $2,200.

In the end, seeing my school come together for an issue that didn't directly affect them was inspiring, and I hope to continue building bridges between my communities in the future. Most of all, I knew our efforts wouldn't restore all the damage, but I was proud to be of help - to have supported my friends.

essays.prompt: In a scholarly community, differing ideas often collide before they converge. How do you personally navigate disagreement in a way that promotes progress and deepens meaningful dialogue? (150 words)
essays.essay:
My philosophy for navigating disagreement is objectivity over emotion. While I was interning at Global SVF, my team disagreed on which nonprofit to support. I initially advocated for Youth Finance USA because its mission resonated with my personal interests, while my colleague supported NFTE.

Instead of arguing, I proposed that we should step back and look at our organizations using our proposed criteria. Looking through the data, we realized that objective metrics deepened our discussion, transforming disagreement into a collaborative search for the best solution. This helped me realize that my perspective had been shaped by my emotions and that NFTE's broader reach aligned better with our mission.

Ultimately, this disagreement taught me that objectivity in disagreements can lead to meaningful discussions. Since then, I have continued practicing this, analyzing the facts instead of letting my emotions take over, something I hope to continue at Emory's diverse and debate-driven community.

essays.prompt: What academic areas are you interested in exploring at Emory University and why?
essays.essay:
Business to me, specifically Investment Banking and High Finance, have often been portrayed as these cut throat careers, where all people care about is their job. No care for others, just themselves. As a kid, I've been raised to put people first and money second, to pursue a version of finance that values integrity and human impact as much as performance and profit.

At Emory, I am drawn to the opportunity to major in Finance at Goizueta while complementing it with a minor in Ethics. Through experiences like consulting for small businesses and working with nonprofit organizations, I've seen how financial decisions shape livelihoods, not just balance sheets.

I am eager to build on this foundation through coursework such as Financial Accounting, Corporate Finance, and Ethics and Leadership, where I can better understand how financial strategy and moral responsibility intersect. Programs like the Goizueta IMPACT initiative and partnerships with the Small Business Development Center particularly excite me, as they mirror the hands-on, community-centered work I've already pursued.

By combining rigorous financial training with ethical reflection, I hope to develop the judgment necessary to make decisions that serve both markets and people. Emory's commitment to purposeful leadership offers the ideal environment to grow into a finance professional who measures success not only by returns, but by the communities strengthened along the way.

essays.prompt: As a top tier research university, George Washington is committed to providing opportunities for practical application of theoretical knowledge and hands-on experiences in your field of interest. Please discuss the ways in which GW's academic approach appeals to you and how that approach will strengthen your ability to succeed as a future physician. (250 words)
essays.essay:
As an aspiring physician, I am confident that George Washington University is the best place for me to acquire all the knowledge and experience I need in the next years of my life. With the respectable SMHS strategic plan, GWU's dedication to improving healthcare and bridging the gap between healthcare professionals' and students' access to the latest medical advances, and real-world opportunities immediately offered during the onset of the studies, I could see myself being able to make humble but valuable input not just in the field of neuroscience but also into our ever growing social and educational climate.

With GWU's esteemed reputation and its faculty's access and interactions with world leaders, me and my future classmates will be able to further advocate the simple worries we may have had with our current healthcare strategies with a higher chance of being actually heard. As a responsible American, I feel that it is my civic duty to be part of the larger discourse when it comes to the application of technology and funding of research, advancing later discoveries that may unfortunately be overlooked by those who did not come from the same socio-economic background.

There is also, of course, the higher chances of us being connected with the best future employers where we could apply our passions alongside all the things we'll learn from GWU, giving me the chance to make a larger impact to society as well as the confidence I could one day make the GWU family proud.

essays.prompt: Briefly discuss the significance to you of the school or summer activity in which you have been most involved.
essays.essay:
This past summer, I had the opportunity to intern at Global SVF, a venture capital firm where I focused on researching and investing in non-profit organizations with growth potential. This experience reinforced my vision of working as a private analyst at a top firm like Bain, KKR, or Blackstone.

At Global SVF, I gained valuable negotiation skills through executive-level meetings where our firm negotiated with businesses to secure funding opportunities for local non-profits. I learned about the complex nature of tax write-offs for businesses donating funds to non-profits, the concept of capital allocation to maintain a healthy portfolio, and research methods to measure a non-profit's financial health when deciding which organizations to fund.

As an intern, I was given the autonomy to research and invest in my own non-profit, and to build pitch decks to support my case. It was a novel experience that was equally challenging: learning to include the appropriate financial terms and metrics, and to gather all the information into a few clean slides for executive review, was a monumental task.

In my research, I chose NFTE, an NPO that promotes entrepreneurial skills for the youth. I developed an in-depth research proposal that included 990 forms, an impact analysis, and financial metrics, and I even met with NFTE's Board, which was the highlight of this whole experience. Talking to their Board taught me more than just the good and the bad about the non-profit, but the powerful story behind their founding and the values. I learned about their strategy for scaling from a small, non-profit to a nationally recognized organization that's helped 1.5 million entrepreneurs start their own ventures.

I hope to use this experience as knowledge and insight in the nonprofits that I am a part of, to help them grow and impact more youth around the world, just like how NFTE has done.

essays.prompt: Please elaborate on any special talents or skills you would like to highlight.
essays.essay:
Planning effectively has been the cornerstone of my success.

When planning anything, I prioritize my tasks from most to least impactful, then break each task into smaller chunks. This strategy enables me to multitask effectively, allowing me to clearly track my progress one step at a time without becoming overwhelmed.

I've demonstrated this ability in my day-to-day at school, managing my workload all while balancing a rigorous activities schedule, and I've also been able to use this skill effectively as the Officer of Operations at a youth marketing nonprofit.

At the nonprofit, we help local businesses grow through social media management. I rely on my planning skills to stay organized and ensure our posts are sent on time. To facilitate this process, I coordinate weekly meetings with our members and business owners to ensure we're all aligned on the same plan and to make revisions and updates to the campaigns as needed. I also work directly with members, guiding them and making time to deliberate on any roadblocks that are preventing smooth operations.

Through effective planning, I've led a group of members in developing a strong social presence for four local businesses, increasing their revenue substantially.

That's why I think my ability to plan effectively has been a key factor in my success today.

essays.prompt: Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business provides graduates with essential global, ethical, analytical, financial, and diverse perspectives on the economies of our nation and the world. Describe your primary motivations for studying business at Georgetown University.
essays.essay:
"Have we got our property back?"
"Why do these people keep trying to steal our land"
(In Marathi, of course).

Coming from India, America was supposed to be this new world with a fresh start. But for my parents it was like they were still there, battling court cases on the phone against people who were well aware that the land wasn't theirs. Living through moments where people invested time and effort in the wrong actions taught my parents the lasting value of doing the right thing.

This trait has seeped on to me, with my parents teaching me the value of doing the right thing, even when no one is watching. I'll continue to live by these values no matter how far I go. In business, investment banking and finance have always been portrayed as highly competitive fields motivated by a culture of performance over ethics. I disagree with that notion and I plan to pursue finance with empathy and genuine intentions, highlighting my core values just as much as performance and returns.

This perspective is what draws me to Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business. McDonough's approach to business education reflects what my parents taught me growing up. Georgetown's Jesuit principle of cura personalis, care for the whole person, resonates deeply with how I view leadership in business. I want to acquire skills that help others and not just for my own benefit.

At McDonough, I plan to pursue a major in Finance with a minor in Tech, Ethics and Society, where I can build a strong analytical foundation while grounding my studies in ethics and global awareness. I'll take advantage of courses such as Introduction to Financial Accounting and Corporate Finance to learn financial analysis, assess capital structures, and evaluate investment decisions. Through Financial Markets and Institutions, I hope to understand how capital flows, regulation, and technological innovation shape global markets.

Beyond developing a strong analytical foundation, ethics-focused courses will teach me to examine how emerging technologies, data use and algorithmic decision-making influences fairness, transparency, and accountability in business. Together, an education at McDonough will prepare me to navigate finance with quantitative skill, and ethical judgment in a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

Beyond the classroom, I am excited by McDonough's emphasis on experiential learning and socially conscious finance. Through student organizations such as the McDonough Student Investment Fund and Net Impact, I hope to apply financial theory to real-world challenges with peers who share a commitment to responsible and sensible leadership. These experiences will sharpen my technical skills while remaining accountable to the broader impact of my work, whether investing capital as an advisor, consulting for organizations as a business and financial expert, or shaping long-term vision for corporations as a strategist.

Georgetown's location in Washington, D.C. further distinguishes McDonough as the ideal place for me to study business. The proximity to policymakers, global institutions, and nonprofit organizations offers a unique lens into how finance intersects with regulation, diplomacy, and social change. Having witnessed how legal systems and power structures can be exploited, I am deeply interested in understanding how ethical business practices can restore trust and promote fairness within economic systems. Georgetown's integration of business with policy and global affairs offers an unmatched environment to develop that understanding.

Ultimately, I want to pursue a career in finance where success is measured not only by returns, but by responsibility. McDonough's emphasis on ethical foundations and analytical rigor will prepare me to enter competitive financial fields without compromising my values. Just as my parents taught me to do the right thing even when no one is watching, I want to leave Georgetown prepared to lead with integrity, using finance not merely as a tool for profit, but as a force for principled and lasting impact.

essays.promptLabel: Why this major at Georgia Tech
essays.prompt: Why do you want to study your chosen major specifically at Georgia Tech? (300 words)
essays.essay:
For a while now, thoughts of using my full-stack programming skills to create a revolutionary application that benefits countless individuals have been in the back of my mind. This summer when I visited Georgia Tech, these thoughts resurfaced and made me realize that my dream can become a reality at this university.

Aside from the temptation of the Chick-fil-A at the John Lewis Community Center, I was astonished by the campus. The moment I entered the Klaus Computer Building, my jaw dropped. I looked around to see 3D printers and engineering equipment in the various laboratories. My surroundings pulled me in, and I got lost in the idea of using these tools to develop a multitude of projects.

I was equally amazed by Georgia Tech's active role in facilitating growth beyond the classroom through services that connect students with renowned companies like Coca-Cola and Delta. The prospect of interning at these establishments further motivates my decision to pursue computer science at this school.

What truly caught my attention was Georgia Tech's commitment to nurturing young minds and empowering students to apply their skills in real-world settings. The InVenture Challenge appealed to me since it resembled a hackathon. I have been participating in hackathons since the start of high school, and creating solutions to societal problems provides me with an overwhelming sense of accomplishment.

Georgia Tech will allow me to pursue an enriching journey of self-discovery. Courses like Computing for Engineers will teach me how to design algorithms which are crucial skills for the development process. The university's vast resources, coupled with my zeal to learn, will propel me to excel as a software professional. I know that Georgia Tech will help me achieve my dreams—its focused curriculum and cordial student community is unmatched.

essays.prompt: An LMU education forms ethical leaders compelled to tackle the world's most pressing challenges. How do your personal experiences and educational goals align with this mission?
essays.essay:
If I had a dollar for every instance I walked into my house with a new bruise, scrape, or scratch, I would be able to instantly pay for my tuition with extra savings. With every injury I was scolded by my mother. "You are too rowdy for a girl, you mustn't be messy." However, the lessons I learned with every fall or fault or splinter molded me into the toughest fighter.

Every injury comes with a story, like the time I forgot how to brake on a bike or the time I jumped off the swings and onto the tanbark. Good to know I wouldn't be doing those things again. However, there was a recurring thought that came with every scolding from my mother. What else can I do? What accomplishments could I achieve? These very thoughts stay present with my character to this day.

What I eventually understood is that with opportunity comes sacrifice. Of course, most of these opportunities given to me do not produce bruises on my knees, but they have a con that can be just as painful. Once I started to explore hobbies on my own, I was hit with a sense of fear with every step. I was anxious about progressing; it wasn't like the swings on the playground or the brakes on the bike, I was growing up. But the more I did on my own the more I realized fear made everything possible. I got into game design, the arts, coding, and even longboarding. Most of these hobbies were also disapproved of by my traditional Korean family, but I hold these hobbies close to my heart because I had to give up opportunities.

The world's most pressing challenges are not to be solved so simply. They're dubbed "the world's most pressing challenges" for a reason, however my question still remains. What accomplishments could I achieve? What exactly is the limit? That is what I strive to discover. With every fall, I grew more and more adventurous. There is a problem waiting just for me to combat. I aim to develop a deeper understanding of real-world issues, and I hope LMU will foster such an environment for me to explore these issues. This includes climate change, social injustices, and more complex challenges. My values align with this mission, as I am ready to face it all. Sure, these problems don't come with physical splinters and sharp edges, but they are difficult to swallow and will need a lot more than just one person to tackle it all. I'd be honored to contribute to the fight against such issues. I'll swing in with a strong mindset and an adventurous perspective. Then, I will be able to see just where the sky ends.

essays.prompt: In a world where disconnection seems to often prevail, we are looking for students who embody the qualities of bridge builders—students who can connect people, groups, and ideas to span divides, foster understanding, and promote collaboration within a dynamic, interconnected, and vibrant global academic community. Please consider one or more of the following: What personal experiences or challenges have shaped you as a bridge builder? How have you been a bridge builder in your school, community, or personal life? What specific actions have you taken to build bridges between diverse groups, ideas, or cultures? How do you envision being a bridge builder during your time at our university and beyond? (250 words)
essays.essay:
At my breakfast table, Turkish cheeses meet Dutch bread, creating cultural harmony. Born to a Turkish mother and a Dutch father in America, I've always been surrounded by different cultures. Instead of choosing one side however, I've learned to bridge these cultures to form an identity that's uniquely mine.

This perspective shaped my response when the devastating Turkey-Syria earthquakes struck a community close to my heart. I rallied my school's support in a fundraiser to aid the children I taught English to in that area – uniting communities of people to help make a difference. Together, we set up donation jars, raised class competitions, and even hosted pizza events to collect money. Yet, this effort wasn't just about the donation, it was about encouraging the feeling of empathy for others, turning international headlines into a shared experience within my communities at home.

At NYU, I'll build on these experiences as a bridge builder. I imagine hosting cultural nights and potlucks to share foods and traditions with my fellow students, and I'd be proud to share my parents' delicious hometown recipes. Additionally, I'll volunteer with NYU SPS International Club to foster connections with global students and organize informal community events to unite people of different backgrounds. Here, we could talk freely about important topics ranging from politics to history and equally-important topics ranging from Pokémon cards to anime cosplay. At NYU, whether through a community service event or a shared meal, I hope to do what I do best: bring people together.

essays.prompt: We are looking for peacemakers, changemakers, global citizens, boundary breakers, creatives and innovators - Choose one quote from the following and let us know why it inspires you; or share a short quote and person not on our list who inspires you, and include why. Quote chosen: "You have the right to want things to change."
essays.essay:
The desire to change is inevitable, it's part of the nature of mankind. It is what makes us human. You felt it, I felt it. However, the change I want I know I can make. My burning question is: are video games detrimental? If so, why do people believe that? The mind is hard to shift once it's locked in, but change is constant. There is no harm reaching for the stars.

Not long ago, I researched that game development doesn't have to be just video games for iPad kids. In recent times, game design has shifted into the medical field. The use of video games in a high-stress environment has proved to be a therapeutic way to recover. However, there are still a vast amount of individuals who believe that this form of entertainment, therapy, and comfort taints their minds and leads them to a darker path. However, I have the skills to show people the true colors of video games.

I hope that by diving into the deeper elements and concepts of the development of games, I too can assist in the creation of therapeutic games. Games not only for those in need but for everyone and anyone. Just like what Gusteau said in the hit movie Ratatouille, "Anyone can cook." Yes, I agree. Anyone can cook, not just food but brew a new approach to the possibilities of video games. That is my change.

essays.prompt: Think about a time when your curiosity led you to not just learn, but to act. How did you learn more, and what tangible steps did you take as a result of what you learned? What insights about yourself, others, or the world did you take away from this process of learning and doing? (600 words)
essays.essay:
It was a gloomy Sunday. I was driving in South Carolina, coming back from my friend's house. I saw a strip mall with 8 local businesses, all side by side, a bakery, a laundromat, a barbershop, and a few others, each with its own story and struggle. On the ride home, I kept thinking about all these local businesses had to do just to stay afloat. After I got home, I did some research and found out about all of the things that go into running just one business, from suppliers to paying workers, managing marketing, inventory, and customer relationships. Every decision, from choosing where to advertise to deciding how much product to order, can impact their survival. The deeper I looked, the more I realized how interconnected everything is: a single supply chain issue can affect dozens of people, and a dip in sales can mean cutting employees' hours. It made me appreciate not just the effort behind entrepreneurship, but also the resilience and creativity it demands.

To really see how difficult this was, I started my own mini business my freshman year. Back then, I really enjoyed gardening and spent a lot of time keeping our lawn in tip-top shape. So I thought the perfect business to start was a lawn mowing business. It seemed simple at first; all I had to do was knock on some doors and ask them if I could cut their grass. But after getting those first initial customers, I hit a wall. I had to market myself on a dozen social media apps, from Nextdoor to even Facebook (I felt ashamed using this app - I thought it was only for old people). While doing all of this, I had to still cut lawns and keep in touch with my customers. Even for a business model as simple as this, I learned how hard entrepreneurship really is.

With my new experience, I strived to bridge that gap for other new business owners. So I joined the Charlotte Youth Marketing Association. As the Officer of Operations, I had the opportunity to work with Velvet, a local boba and ice cream shop. The owners were first-time business owners, and they were massively in-depth and struggling to stay afloat. To solve this, we optimized their ads and social media posts so that they are posted at peak times and reach their target audience. We also fixed internal money leakages that were going on, with the overstocked inventory issue, oversized menu, and overstaffing. With lots of continuous hard work and more help, this business was able to turn a profit and renovate, turning it into one of Charlotte's go-to options for many for Boba and especially rolled Ice cream.

Through this process and these experiences, I recognized that curiosity isn't just about "wondering" or pondering about what happened; it's about having the drive to understand something so deeply that you are forced to take a chance and strive to make a difference. Before, I saw businesses as money-making machines, but now I see them as living systems that rely on human connection and constant adaptation. I learned that real problem-solving isn't just answering the question; it requires empathy by understanding what the business owner is going through. From the stress of every late payment to the excitement of seeing a new customer, even a local one. Working with business owners taught me how much of an impact small, but thoughtful changes can have. Not just on profits, but on people's lives. It made me think of these more analytically, but also through a more compassionate lens. I now approach challenges by looking beyond the surface, searching for the invisible forces that shape outcomes. Most importantly, I discovered that curiosity paired with action can create real, measurable change in my community.

essays.prompt: Explain why you selected the first choice academic program above and why you are interested in studying this at NC State. (250 words)
essays.essay:
There are 2 careers I'm split in pursuing, all under the umbrella of finance. I want to either go into Business analyst at a large firm, or try and break into investment banking, both extremely competitive fields. To turn this interest into actionable skills, I want to pursue a Business Administration major with a concentration in Business Analytics at NC State.

Courses like BUS 459, BUS 440, and BUS 422 will provide me hands-on training in predictive analytics, data-driven decision-making, and advanced financial management, equipping me with the quantitative and strategic skills essential for a career in business analytics. NC State's AI initiative will help me streamline these skills and learn how to use AI as a tool in this field.

Beyond the classroom, I'm excited to engage with NC State's analytics-focused community. Joining the Business Analytics Club would allow me to apply classroom concepts to real projects and participate in case competitions, while the Poole Consulting Club offers opportunities to tackle real-world business challenges using data-driven solutions. Additionally, programs like the Business Analytics Honors Program would let me work directly with companies on consulting-style projects, giving me practical experience that bridges analytics theory and professional application.

Now, to put everything I've learned into action, NC State's strong corporate partnerships with top companies like SAS, Deloitte, and IBM would give me direct access to internships and networking opportunities, making the transition from classroom to career much more efficient. Coupled with the hands-on experience from the Business Analytics program and clubs, these connections would allow me to apply my skills to real-world business challenges and prepare for competitive roles as a business analyst.

essays.prompt: Explain why you selected the second choice academic program above and why you are interested in studying this at NC State. (250 words)
essays.essay:
Although I hope to pursue a career as a Business Analyst, I find myself torn between that path and the fast-paced world of Investment Banking. A major in Business Administration with a concentration in Finance provides me with a strong foundation for that career.

NC State's courses like BUS 340, BUS 420, and BUS 426 would provide a strong foundation in corporate finance, valuation, and investment theory, essential tools for understanding how companies raise and allocate capital. Through these classes, I'd gain practical experience in analyzing balance sheets, assessing risk, and building financial models, all of which are critical skills in investment banking.

Outside the classroom, I'm especially drawn to the Student Managed Investment Fund and the Wealth Management Initiative. Managing real assets and working with financial mentors would give me hands-on experience in portfolio analysis, risk assessment, and client strategy, skills directly aligned with the analytical and relationship-driven nature of investment banking. I'd also join Beta Alpha Psi, where I can live with like-minded people and connect with top finance and accounting students while building relationships with firms through professional events and leadership opportunities.

Finally, NC State's strong ties to industry leaders like Wells Fargo, Deloitte, and Fidelity make it the perfect environment to develop both technical and professional skills. With these opportunities, I know NC State will give me the foundation and connections to turn my interest in finance into a thriving career on Wall Street.

essays.prompt: We want to be sure we're considering your application in the context of your personal experiences: What aspects of your background, your identity, or your school, community, and/or household settings have most shaped how you see yourself engaging in Northwestern's community, be it academically, extracurricularly, culturally, politically, socially, or otherwise? (fewer than 300 words)
essays.essay:
As the only child of two East Asian immigrant parents, my duty was set at birth. On my life-long journey to become the perfect son, I've had many hiccups, but I never gave up. Approaching my father was sometimes difficult; his expectations were realistic, but they were above the norm. In third grade, after advancing in Kumon, I asked my dad for help with double-digit multiplication only to receive a long lecture about how I needed to try harder.

Contemplating quitting, I studied and made progress. I returned to my father, holding the same worksheet with perfect marks, but was disappointed once again. Rather than praise, a dismissive nod sent me back to my room feeling gutted. This pattern persisted, and in high school, a flame of indignation pushed me to search for approval. So I turned to the only metric of achievements I knew. I accomplished straight A's, excelled in AP courses (earning top scores on the exams), and assumed leadership roles in community service clubs.

Although I've realized my foolishness throughout the journey to prove my self worth, I discovered my ability to persevere and have since fallen in love with my work. Discovering a passion in medicine and community service, I want to work alongside Northwestern's Community Health Corps to learn CPR, first aid skills, AED operation, and more. With this information, I can then help educate others within the Evanston community by teaching these skills, answering health related questions, or connecting individuals to professional resources.

Since discovering my calling as a physician in progress, I have made up with my dad. He has pushed me to work hard and subsequently help others, two values that are promoted by Northwestern and two values that I will live by forever on.

essays.prompt: We want to be sure we're considering your application in the context of your personal experiences: What aspects of your background (your identity, your school setting, your community, your household, etc.) have most shaped how you see yourself engaging in Northwestern's community, be it academically, extracurricularly, culturally, politically, socially, or otherwise? (300 words)
essays.essay:
I have always measured my growth by how much I help others grow. Whether it was guiding members at 4-H meetings or helping elementary schoolers improve their soccer skills, I found purpose not just in participation, but in mentorship. Those early experiences shaped how I see myself engaging in any community: as someone who builds systems that allow people to succeed.

That mindset came fully to life through my role as Officer of Operations at the Charlotte Youth Marketing Association (CYMA). On our first call with local business Velvet, I crunched the numbers and discovered an alarmingly high customer acquisition cost at $4, an unsustainable figure for a small, low-margin business. Partnering with the owner, we cut costs immediately. We sourced ingredients locally to reduce supply costs, streamlined the menu to minimize inventory waste, and restructured their digital marketing strategy. By launching targeted Instagram, Yelp, and Facebook ads tied to happy-hour promotions and holiday deals, we increased foot traffic while lowering marketing spend. The impact extended beyond the business itself; every customer who walked into Velvet benefited from a stronger, more sustainable local establishment, even before its later renovation.

At Northwestern, I see myself continuing this work through Form & Function Marketing and Consult Your Community (CYC). Both organizations embody the kind of impact-driven consulting that motivates me: applying analytical thinking to solve real problems for real people. Through Form & Function, I would contribute my experience designing professional marketing campaigns while mentoring newer members. Through CYC, I am drawn to the opportunity to apply consulting frameworks to nonprofits and mission-driven organizations, aligning operational efficiency with social good.

My experience at CYMA - leading teams, refining strategy, and teaching peers - prepares me to contribute meaningfully to both groups. More importantly, it reflects how I see myself at Northwestern: as someone who learns by doing, leads by teaching, and strengthens communities by helping others grow.

essays.prompt: Community and belonging matter at Northwestern. Tell us about one or more communities, networks, or student groups you see yourself connecting with on campus.
essays.essay:
I envision myself becoming an active member of the Personal Finance Student Association. Its mission of promoting financial literacy aligns closely with my passions and experiences. During my time with Youth Finance USA, I had the opportunity to teach financial literacy to elementary and middle school students, which gave me valuable insight into effective teaching strategies. At Northwestern University, I aim to leverage this experience to expand the organization's reach, not only by engaging with university students but also by partnering with local high schools, middle schools, and elementary schools to broaden its impact on financial education.

I could also see myself being a member of Form & Function Marketing. Its mission of creating professional campaigns that drive business impact aligns with what I do right now at Charlotte Youth Marketing Association (CYMA). As the officer of operations at CYMA I develop posts for small businesses and assign groups of students posts that they have to develop, which I then touch up and post. At Form & Function Marketing I could continue doing this hobby and create posts that have a much greater impact than at CYMA. My skills and experience teaching gained at CYMA would help me develop professional grade posts and teach newer members with less experience how to develop posts. This would ultimately allow me to have a huge impact on the small businesses that we develop posts for and the students with less experience in marketing.

essays.prompt: Northwestern's location is special: on the shore of Lake Michigan, steps from downtown Evanston, just a few miles from Chicago. What aspects of our location are most compelling to you, and why?
essays.essay:
Good work-life balance is what signifies a great college experience to me. Northwestern's prime location gives that perfect balance.

To live life a little, Northwestern's short distance from Sky Zone makes it the perfect outlet after a demanding week. I still remember going to Sky Zone for the first time in 4th grade, jumping on every trampoline, diving head first into foam pits. Even now, I visit Sky Zone regularly to relive the childhood joys. Knowing it's so close to Northwestern makes it feel like home.

Just as important as knowing when to unwind is having spaces to help channel my energy back into work. I can't wait to do my work at Patisserie Coralie, a French bakery nearby. While I'm not a coffee addict, this shop has one of my favorite drinks, a French Soda, and my go-to almond croissant. These simple joys of life are what will keep me grounded and motivated through college.

As I'm sure there's a lot more that Northwestern and its vicinity has to offer, I'm determined to explore every week, finding hidden gems around the city that I can share with friends and family back at home.

essays.promptLabel: What would you paint on The Rock
essays.prompt: Painting "The Rock" is a tradition at Northwestern that invites all forms of expression - students promote campus events or extracurricular groups, support social or activist causes, show their Wildcat spirit (what we call "Purple Pride"), celebrate their culture, and more. What would you paint on The Rock, and why?
essays.essay:
Kaju-Katli, that's what I would paint on "The Rock". This Indian delicacy, made from cashews, sugar, and cardamom powder, holds a special place in my heart.

As a child, Kaju-Katli was a part of every meal. It was often the reason I finished everything on my plate. However, as I grew older, it became less of an everyday indulgence and more of a rare treat, reserved for special occasions like Diwali and Ganesh Puja.

Kaju-Katli taught me to appreciate the simple joys food can bring. The sugar in Kaju-Katli represents the sweet moments in life, the happy times, the times when eating this treat brings immense joy, letting me forget my worries and live in the moment. Finally, the cardamom powder, delicately sprinkled into the dough after the other ingredients, represents the spread of culture.

Sharing Kaju-Katli with loved ones and friends, lighting up their day (unless they're allergic to nuts), is what makes this treat so special. It allows for everyone around me to feel the same joy I felt as a kid and still feel today. That's why I would paint Kaju-Katli on "The Rock."

essays.promptLabel: What would you paint on The Rock
essays.prompt: Painting 'The Rock' is one of Northwestern's oldest traditions. If you had the chance, what would you paint on The Rock and why? (prompt not stated verbatim in the document; inferred from the essay's reference to painting 'The Rock')
essays.essay:
A dragon fruit. Beautiful, stunning, colorful. It represents my Chinese heritage and those Saturday morning strolls around my city's Chinatown markets, where prices are written on cardboard signs labeling the value of different vegetables, herbs, and of course dragon fruit. However, it is more than that.

It represents my dad's quirky passion for his dragon fruit farm. Containing more than a dozen different species, it possesses globally sourced plants. Each fruit it produces is unique and can often disturb those who crave the traditional fruit. Nonconforming, however, my father harbors exploration despite criticism. The dragon fruit encapsulates his unpredictable, spontaneous, and entertaining individualism.

On the other hand, the dragon fruit embodies my mom's grounded personality. The dragon fruit reminds me that each product bore from our yard is carefully cut and prepared by my mom. She is the backbone of our three person family and a lifesaver. From teaching me to load the laundry to retelling her immigration tales, the dragon fruit brings her independent nature to campus.

So when asked what I would paint on 'The Rock,' my love for my Chinese heritage and the two opposing characters that raised me will shine perfectly through a dragon fruit.

essays.prompt: In 300 words or less, help us understand what aspects of Northwestern appeal most to you, and how you'll make use of specific resources and opportunities here.
essays.essay:
When I told my mother I wanted to be a Wildcat, she stared at me as if to say, "But that's many states away." Although she was, at first, worried about the move, I immediately eased her concerns when I told her about the many reasons why the competitive Northwestern University has always been my number one college campus choice.

With the luxury of NU's surroundings; its progressive, left-leaning socio-political climate; proper tools and research facilities; access to groundbreaking technological advances and medicinal research; and Evanston's fast-paced urban lifestyle - I find myself preparing into the next thrilling experience of my life. NU's quarter system, specifically, is also a great way to maximize learning within shorter periods of time, challenging all undergraduates to perform even better.

As I have always been a curious girl (and an aspiring physician) who found being challenged by new surroundings exhilarating, I'm always prepared to advance my understanding of neuroscience and psychology in a place which foremost focus is academic excellence.

One checking of NU's website informing me about its emphasis on diversity/inclusion most certainly helps, too. The safe and beautiful environment, the many student housing blocks, the prospect of joining great academic clubs and networking with the postgraduates while being at the center of innovation - these were just a few of the things that convince me that NU is the place where I could really excel at.

NU simply boasts all the things where I could further my interests in medicine, scientific research, and healthcare work. I have no doubt NU is also the perfect place for me to find and expound on strategic plans when it comes to future career decisions. And I hope I will be allowed to find new meaningful experiences and add color to the campus's already-vibrant surroundings.

essays.prompt: Quirks, idiosyncrasies, peculiarities. They help differentiate us. What is one of yours? (133 words)
essays.essay: I've always been a frustratingly indecisive person, and that also applies when I paint my nails. Whenever I decide to paint my nails, it takes me at least ten minutes just to decide what I want to do, and then sometimes it takes me another ten minutes to decide if that's what I honestly, genuinely want to do. A quirk I have is painting my nails with different colors, whether it's a pattern on one hand versus the other hand or alternating colors one after the other. I think it's fun and unique, while it also eases the indecisiveness that goes on in my brain. I think my favorite combination is an alternating pattern of black and white, just because it looks really trippy when I look at my hands as a whole.

essays.prompt: Occidental's central mission emphasizes the value of community amidst diversity. What do you value in a community and how do you see your perspectives and life experiences enhancing it?
essays.essay:
In a community, I value people who support one another, listen openly, and work towards a shared goal. As a leader in different communities, such as Kumon and various school clubs, I've experienced different kinds of communities and how people work together in them. These experiences taught me that strong communities aren't always built on similarities, but on compassion, respect, and togetherness.

My perspective on community is influenced by moments when I didn't feel included. I've been in groups where my ideas were overlooked, people were divided and overly competitive. Those experiences showed me the value of making people within a community feel seen and heard. When I stepped up as a leader for my communities, I brought quiet students into the discussion, checked on people who seemed left out, and created an environment that made everyone feel comfortable.

At Occidental, I hope to strengthen the sense of togetherness at a school that brings different cultures and walks of life into one space. My approach to community starts with listening first and encouraging my peers to bond through collaboration and shared interests. Specifically, I want to help create or join clubs on campus and host events where students and friends can participate and have a great time, especially cultural events where we can all share and learn a thing or two from each other's cultures.

essays.prompt: Why are you applying to Occidental? What are your intellectual curiosities and why do you think Occidental is the right place for you to pursue them? (200 words)
essays.essay: I was recommended Occidental by a family member who visited the campus and told me of how great it is, which was how I first heard of the school and became enraptured once doing some more extra research. I've always liked Southern California, whether it was for visiting colleges or going to Disneyland, so I really enjoy the location Occidental is in. I also took note of how small the class sizes are and speaking from personal experience with moderately large class sizes at my high school I'd appreciate a smaller class. It allows for better communication with professors as well as other students. I want to major in Sociology and I even took a glance at Occidental's course list and the sociology of law and youth culture in United States Society are courses that caught my attention when I skimmed the list, but there are a lot of other classes that I'm interested in learning more about. Occidental has a wide variety of classes to choose from when it comes to Sociology and I think that's a big reason why it's an excellent place for me to study.

essays.prompt: Pepperdine is a Christian university where all are welcomed and encouraged to challenge each other in the pursuit of truth. Students, faculty, and staff members from all backgrounds participate in conversations of faith inside and outside of the classroom. Considering that Pepperdine is a Christian university, why are you interested in attending and how would you contribute to conversations of faith on campus?
essays.essay:
When I first learned about Pepperdine's unique identity - a Christian university rooted in both faith and academic rigor - I was immediately excited to apply. Though I do not identify as deeply religious, I have long been drawn to values such as compassion, integrity, and a commitment to serving others - principles that resonate with the Christian foundation Pepperdine upholds. My interest in Pepperdine stems from a desire to grow intellectually, morally, and spiritually, where lessons of faith intertwine with the study of law, allowing me to develop new perspectives.

I imagine walking through Pepperdine's campus in the early morning, the wind carrying the sound of light conversation through the air. The setting is soothing - a place where deep, intentional conversations feel not only possible but welcomed. I can imagine taking part in discussions that stretch beyond textbooks and legal theory, reaching into questions of purpose, belief, and how we serve others through our work. That kind of educational setting draws me most to Pepperdine: one that encourages the pursuit of truth and justice through both scholarship and faith.

Through my upbringing, I carry a deep respect for faith traditions and a sincere interest in learning from others who believe differently than I do. My values are rooted in humanism, with an emphasis on empathy, active listening, and the dignity of every person. These values mirror many Christian teachings, and I see this collaboration as a starting point for meaningful dialogue on campus. I don't view differences as divisions - I see them as opportunities to grow, to challenge assumptions, and to foster understanding through respectful conversation.

Beyond lectures and lessons, I hope to contribute to conversations of faith by asking thoughtful questions and sharing my own experiences with others. I want to be part of a community where people are not afraid to express belief or explore the unknown. My goal is not to argue, but to connect - to help create a space where faith is not something that separates people, but something that brings them together in the shared pursuit of truth, justice, and compassion.

My ideas of sharing faith come from experience. I have led clubs and sports teams, and I have learned that all voices must be heard and valued. Everyone's perspective is important; each can teach open-mindedness and compassion for all backgrounds. I loved asking my club members for suggestions to improve the group and ensure that the community worked together rather than relying on a select few. I will do the same with the Pepperdine community and follow the same principles I did with my past groups.

My interest in Pepperdine is not just academic - it blooms from a love of community and inclusivity. I want to be part of a university where students from all corners of the earth are invited to ask questions in pursuit of something bigger than themselves.

essays.prompt: Imagine having a 1 a.m. debate/discussion with your peers in college about an issue you care about. What is that issue, and what is the discussion? (300 words)
essays.essay: I can imagine the issue we would be having, absolutely delirious, at one a.m. is about whether or not socks with sandals is an acceptable thing to wear outside of the house. I support socks with sandals in public, but only if they are funky socks matched with Birkenstocks or Crocs, because if you're going to reveal your socks you might as well make them fun to look at. The other side who are fully against socks with sandals would probably say that it's a gross look when one could honestly just wear sneakers. To that, I would say that sometimes sneakers take too long to put on, because you have to slip your foot in and shake it in for a while if it's laced up too tight and then bend all the way down to tie the laces. It isn't worth the effort if you're just going out for errands. Although, I do agree that socks with sandals look awful if it's white tube socks with flip flops, because then you have to wedge the band in between your toes when you're wearing socks that don't permit that to happen. The opposing side would go against that and say they could just take their socks off and then just wear the sandals. In turn I would say, but what if it's too cold to go barefoot then you need to wear socks? Then I think that they would go back to their sneakers argument, and I would say that sometimes laziness triumphs style. Then we would all walk to class the next day in socks and sandals.

essays.prompt: Share your favorite quote, and tell us what it means to you. The quote can be from an author, leader, musical artist, family member or other source - famous or not. (Your response should be 200-250 words not including your quote.)
essays.essay:
"I think that one of these days," he said, "you're going to have to find out where you want to go. And then you've got to start going there. But immediately. You can't afford to lose a minute. Not you."

This quote was from The Catcher in the Rye, written by J.D. Salinger. I picked this book to do for a project my sophomore year and I wasn't expecting for this story to hit such a soft spot with me, since it was one of the first classics I'd read of my own volition, and at the time I thought classics were overrated. I think this was one of those times where you read a book at the exact right time so it affects you differently, and you can't explain why. I could barely understand the book on my own, but that's what I loved about it. That's how I felt most of the time I was in high school, although I don't want to try and give into that terrible angsty teenage trope. This quote in particular is something I always recite during ice breakers when the teacher asks what your favorite quote is. It's because, as I get older people are more inclined to ask about college and my future, especially now that I'm a senior, and honestly it feels like my whole life has been leading up to these few months. Everything feels fast. I like to hear this quote whenever things seem overwhelming, because it reminds me that this is my life and I get to decide when and where things happen, and not on anyone else's timeline.

essays.prompt: How will opportunities at Purdue support your interests, both in and out of the classroom? (Respond in 250 words or fewer.)
essays.essay:
I was the kid who served mud pies to my dad when I was younger. He would always take a plastic fork and "eat" my delicious pastry of dirt, grass, and weeds. This simple expression of my creativity evolved into me diving into the arts. Little did I know my artistic skills would soon intertwine with the involvement of STEM, and I hope that pursuing this route will lead me to the doorstep of Purdue University.

The diverse selection of STEM programs supported by Purdue caught my attention. What intrigued me the most was the research projects offered. Not only did it capture the core concepts of anything STEM-related, but the projects included a collaborative environment that brings together people from all sorts of fields and backgrounds. This also includes those in the art departments who bring creativity to the table. Two of my biggest interests blended into one big pie. In addition to the projects provided, the art galleries at Purdue University excited me to my core. I have yet to go to an art gallery that strings technology and art into an assortment of pieces.

Digital art to interactive media, both are shaped by the human hand. I hope that I too may dig my hands into this diversified approach and mold a future for myself that supports both the artistic and calculated sides of me. Though I will not be feeding anyone mud pies, I hope that by joining the dedicated community of Purdue, I will be able to feed people a pie of arts and technology.

essays.promptLabel: Reasons for pursuing your alternate major
essays.prompt: Briefly discuss your reasons for pursuing the alternate major you have selected. (Respond in 250 words or fewer.)
essays.essay:
Not only is gaming a hobby, but the intricacies and the craft of game development pique my interest. Turning what was once a harmful addiction into a full bloom passion has been my greatest accomplishment and I yearn to pursue this path. It's not just a form of entertainment, it was the fuel that drove me to explore new skills.

Not long ago, I had researched that game development doesn't have to be just video games for iPad kids. In recent times, game design has shifted into the medical field. No, this isn't like those surgical games you find on sketchy websites. But the use of video games in a high stress environment has proved video games to be a therapeutic way to recover. Video stimulation simulators have been designed to assist those recovering from muscle-damaging injuries. Video games are also present within other fields, like daycares and educational institutes.

I hope that by diving into the deeper elements and concepts of the development of games, I too can assist in the creation of therapeutic games. Games not only for those in need, but for everyone and anyone. Just like what Gusteau said in the hit movie Ratatouille, "Anyone can cook." Yes, I agree. Anyone can cook, not just food but brew a new approach to the possibilities of video games.

essays.prompt: Briefly discuss your reasons for pursuing the major you have selected. (Respond in 250 words or fewer.)
essays.essay:
The advancements of machine learning stem from the core concepts of statistics. It piqued my interest; who knew sets of numbers could be the roots of a whole new realm of possibilities? By taking this route, I can be a passionate agent of this mission to intertwine the complexities of statistics with theories of machine learning. But what does this mission mean? Well, it means progression, growth, advancement and efficiency.

Machine learning provides datasets that cannot be done by human hands. And that all boils down to statistics, the foundation of what machine learning is. From analyzing the simplest of data to being the backbone of autonomous cars, the possibilities stretch over a vast horizon. Yet this wide sky contains issues yet to be tackled. However, I hope by exploring the Statistics department of Purdue, I can see where the sky and land meet as statistics and machine learning join as one. That is my target.

In hopes of exploring statistics, I will dedicate my energy to the ongoing development of technology. I see no end in the constant reforming of technology. These solutions are good, but they aren't the best. We can keep improving, and I will be a part of this movement.

essays.prompt: There is a breadth of intellectual opportunities here at Rice. Further explain your intended major and other areas of academic focus you may explore. (150 word limit)
essays.essay: As an aspiring physician, I am confident that Rice University is the perfect place for me to acquire all the knowledge and experience I need in the next years of my life majoring in Neuroscience. As for my readiness to succeed in my chosen major, I would take the professionalism I gained during my time in the Summer Research Intensives at the Markstein Cancer Research Lab, the groundwork I've laid as a Research Officer and Neuroscience Specialist Student in the Neuroscience Club at my high school, and the many months I spent shadowing family doctors in my hometown. I have no doubt Rice is the perfect place to find and expand some of my strategic plans for future activities while enrolled in the BSDM program and furthering my interests in medicine, scientific research, and healthcare work. I'm also looking forward to taking several electives in psychology, sociology, and humanities.

essays.prompt: What aspects of the Rice undergraduate experience excite you and led you to apply? (150 word limit)
essays.essay: Right now, I can tell you with all honesty how I am looking forward to the residential college system, as I am very much excited in developing lasting friendships while getting the best education. Rice's faculty-to-student ratio is very impressive, and the fact that Rice is being constantly praised with its access to top-tier research assures me and my future batchmates that we will be getting more than sufficient attention and hands-on experience, readying us best for the future.
