There is also the entire Texan adventure, the great food, and the safe environment where diversity and inclusion are highly prioritized. With all the 2020 prospies coming in from different states and socio-economic background, Rice presents itself as a highly capable breeding ground of ideas that dares not limit its own narrative. I hope I will be allowed to find new meaningful experiences and add color to the campus's already-vibrant surroundings.

essays.prompt: Please discuss why you are interested in becoming a physician. (200 words)
essays.essay: I have always planned on being a physician (more particularly, a neuroscientist) since I was a child. I remember being 8 years old and picking up a random Children's Learning book from my mother's library and being completely fascinated with the way each nerve is beautifully mapped in the illustrations and how much information I could consume within a few minutes of skimming the book had excited me more than, say, sports or computers. (Both of which I practice on my spare time but had never truly been my main academic focus.) In my early teenage years, I tried to learn more through numerous exclusive internship programs as well as shadowing family doctors. Where I am from, medicinal applications and healthcare laws have always been the center of the news, but it always sounded alienating to many people who are not on good social standings. I dream to one day be a good physician by working the extra mile on both scientific and scholastic levels, that I may one day be part of a great team that advances our understanding of it, and also because I want healthcare to be as accessible as possible to everyone who needs it.

essays.prompt: At Santa Clara University, we value our diverse and inclusive community. Our campus learning environment is enriched by the lived experiences of people from different backgrounds. What people, places, events, or circumstances have shaped the individual you are today and how you could contribute to our community? (150-300 words)
essays.essay:
"She is keeping up academically, however she lacks the social skills expected of this grade. Have you considered falling back a year?" were the words that were muttered to my parents as the 4th week of kindergarten approached me. Four-year-old me didn't understand, nor did she care. Pretending to be a dinosaur and playing with legos by herself kept her well occupied. The other kids didn't pay her much attention either since she couldn't speak English very well.

I soon found myself in a vibrant colored classroom titled the "Rainbow Room." The classroom incorporated art into social situations. Every day during school, I'd spend an hour there and I was immediately drawn to the energy and tools incorporated. Not only did I learn the way to approach others, I learned that I had found a hobby that will stick with me for life.

Once I was able to leave the Rainbow Room, I started exploring the arts. To say that art has a huge impact on my life would be an understatement. Not only did it inspire me to take advanced art classes, but it drove me to join the art club in high school as well.

Through the art club, I was involved in a project to decorate a local city center, which helped raise $2,000 for our program. To top it off, I was also promoted as Secretary where I helped grow the club.

The path I took from the Rainbow Room to being the Secretary has been a long yet knowledgeable journey. At SCU, I hope to spread my love of arts with the diverse communities built here, and though it's not the vibrant Rainbow Room, it harbors the same creative energy that I'm searching for. And if there's legos, count me in.

essays.prompt: At Santa Clara University, we push our students to be creative, be challenged, and be the solution. Think about an ethical dilemma that you care about that our society is currently facing. This can be something happening in your local community or more globally. How can an SCU education help you prepare for and address this challenge? (150-300 words)
essays.essay:
The essential part of the success of human life involves the most basic compounds of nutrition. We can also call it food. However, the food we consume today does not have the same properties as the food we had a century ago. Genetic engineering has been present in the food industry since the 1950s, but this processing of food has raised significant concerns over many years. As a fellow food consumer, the thought that the thing I'm currently putting in my mouth has been fondled with does not sit well with me.

Through the process of genetic engineering in food, traits and nutrients have been modified to benefit society. However, many cons arise with this new set of technology. Not only does this modify the genetic traits of nature, but many health risks arise with the changes. I am a moody person and food has always been the comfort tool to my advantage. But the thought that there are too many cons that come with the flavor-blasting sustenance seeps into the mind and the enjoyment of food declines. I hope that by enrolling in SCU's engineering curriculum, I may combat these fears and turn the cons into sweet pros.

The engineering program provided by SCU captured my eye. With the endless research opportunities I was immediately hooked to the hopes that with SCU's Jesuit background, I can explore my yearning to assist the food industry from a scientific point of view. The accelerated programs offered by SCU will allow me to step foot into labs, and prepare me for a long-lasting battle of genetic modification in food. Though food modification will likely be present forever, I hope that in this lifetime I may serve the world a culinary relief in a lab coat, not a chef's hat.

essays.prompt: Please describe what aspects of your life experiences, interests and character would help you make a distinctive contribution as an undergraduate to Stanford University.
essays.essay:
"It's got to be Federer, no one else has his style" I declared.
"Fair, but for me, It's Nadal - his grit is just something else" a coworker responded.
When I first joined my internship at Ernst and Young, I had no idea I would be debating on who the tennis GOAT is. In fact, I was too busy rehearsing my pronunciations of "ş" and "ç" and doing everything in my power to fit in with my native Turkish peers.

Then I met an older coworker, who I learned was once a top 1000 tennis player. We spent hours discussing the rise of Jannik Sinner and relishing over our favorite tournament: Indian Wells. Soon, I felt my passions speaking louder than my mispronounced words. For the rest of my internship, I focused on seeking out these connections. I bonded with my co-worker who spent his free time traversing the world on Microsoft Flight simulator and geeked out with another who was enamored with anime cosplaying.

While my time at EY certainly taught me how to navigate an excel sheet and summarize a presentation, the most important thing I realized was that when words fail to communicate, passions will. At Stanford, I can't wait to see how these passions will evolve. I know that sometimes the walls between people feel insurmountable - but I am confident that we have more that unites us than separates us. Volunteering at English in Action, helping out with International karaoke night, and hosting informal potlucks as we talk about our homes away from home can be a way to close the gap between international students and US natives. At the end of the day, we are all just human.

essays.prompt: Please describe what aspects of your life experiences, interests and character would help you make a distinctive contribution as an undergraduate to Stanford University.
essays.essay:
“There is something more terrible than a hell of suffering - a hell of injustice.”
Victor Hugo, Les Misérables

Justice has never been abstract. It is the difference between suffering that is unavoidable and suffering that is imposed by misjudgment, mistakes, or malice. Victor Hugo's words align with my idea of injustice; it is not just pain, but rather pain that did not have to exist. To me, justice begins with the humility to recognize when harm could have been prevented.

Fairness has never been clear in the pursuit of justice, nor have rules ever been successful in capturing the truth of human reality. During discussions and debates, I find myself asking not only what the law permits, but what justice would require. Often, they overlap; laws were created to ensure justice. But, rarely, justice shies away from the law's shadow as it prevails over all. I want to help justice become what it truly stands for; to interpret it correctly to create the perfect balance between justice and injustice.

At Stanford, my dream of serving on the Supreme Court would allow me to connect with others who have similar ambitions to mine. With like-minded peers, we would be able to collaborate and help each other reach our goals. I aim to create deep conversation and spark new ideas that foster an environment where our perspectives branch outward, rooted in shared ambition and growing in all different directions, echoing the diversity and spirit of the Stanford Tree.

essays.prompt: Please describe what aspects of your life experiences, interests and character would help you make a distinctive contribution as an undergraduate to Stanford University.
essays.essay:
It started when I decided to help my community by building websites for local businesses during the pandemic. I became a better web developer through this initiative, but it was more than that. I was able to seize the opportunity to use my technological prowess to positively impact the community. I gained both an entrepreneurial and technological mindset that I hope to bring to Stanford.

Beyond these websites, I won countless hackathons and coding competitions, where I developed working solutions to real-world problems. These awards were proof that I can turn ideas into tangible applications that address issues in the world. It was here that my confidence and skills as a programmer grew.

But my goal was deeper than this. I see Stanford as a university where technology is more than a tool—it's a force for positive change. I want to create a community with the bright minds at this university who also share my vision for a positive transformation in the world. It would be a collaborative space where works of engineering, both hardware and software, will genuinely connect and uplift other people. With the skills that I have acquired in programming, entrepreneurship, and real-world development, I'm ready to start this community where we come together and unite to create products that truly matter to the world.

I bring more than skills; I bring a new perspective—a vision. A vision of making the globe a better place. I want to achieve this vision at Stanford.

essays.prompt: The Stanford community is deeply curious and driven to learn in and out of the classroom. Reflect on an idea or experience that makes you genuinely excited about learning.
essays.essay:
It's 2:00 a.m., I should be sleeping, but I'm still wide awake, cruising the world through Google street view. As I toured the canals of Amsterdam and the street vendors of Mexico, I can't help but wonder: why are the streets so different?

What started as a curiosity has grown into a deep interest in learning about the framework that influences how cities and roads are developed. Before long, zoning laws had become my endless supply of dopamine. In my spare time watching videos on the toilet and reading urban planning documents, I learned that what may seem like hundreds of rules are really the fabrics that build the tapestry of a city.

Going to Japan last summer, I was intrigued by their mere 12 zones compared to the over 100 we have in North America! These zoning arrangements in Japan were genius in that each one builds on top of the other to foster urban growth. This explains why a shop serving sizzling takoyaki can be right next to a single-family home and why a business district can be a stone's throw away from a school. By contrast, the U.S relies on Euclidean zoning, which creates exclusive zones that make racial divide and economic struggle more prominent in some places than others.

If I had more space to share, I'd share a small journal worth of insights, but I'll save that for my peers at Stanford! Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got more streets to explore.

essays.prompt: The Stanford community is deeply curious and driven to learn in and out of the classroom. Reflect on an idea or experience that makes you genuinely excited about learning.
essays.essay:
When I was in elementary school, I always looked forward to the next field trip. These excursions to science centers, historical buildings, and foreign grounds transformed education into something I could see, touch, and feel. These days have inspired my curiosity and love for learning.

One of my favorite destinations to date is the Exploratorium in San Francisco. The industrial building, the bright lights, the towering decorations, and all the buttons and levers that made unexpected things happen made me genuinely enjoy learning. Especially exciting were the shows and science lectures that they held, helping students like me connect science to the real world and bringing books to life in ways I could never imagine.

These trips changed my perception of learning – it can be fun through exhibits, presentations, and movies. These different avenues of learning made ideas click in a way classrooms couldn't. More importantly, the excitement of leaving the classroom for a day helped me associate learning with a fun excursion rather than the monotony of the indoors.

I believe it's essential to change up the pace and environment of learning for students. This doesn't just teach information, it builds enthusiasm for discovery and helps students learn to love learning rather than fighting it. Field trips showed me that learning can be playful and adventurous, yet deeply educational. The belief that learning is more powerful when it engages both curiosity and joy is a mindset that I carry with me today whenever I approach new ideas.

essays.promptLabel: Idea or experience that excites you about learning
essays.prompt: The Stanford community is deeply curious and driven to learn in and out of the classroom. Reflect on an idea or experience that makes you genuinely excited about learning. (250 words)
essays.essay:
My fascination for autonomous robots is a journey that lights up my curiosity and truly drives my passion for learning. Being part of an FTC robotics team, I found myself captivated by the idea that a robot could participate in a tournament fully autonomously and outperform any human-controlled robot.

Motivated to accomplish this goal, I was excited to wake up every day and learn about the various components required to make this possible. The pathing library that I wanted to create consisted of slightly unfamiliar concepts such as feedback loops, universal localization, odometry, and more. Reading through the research papers was exhilarating because I knew that these concepts extended beyond theoretical understanding.

What really got me excited wasn't the theoretical understanding; it's the end vision I see as I grasp these concepts. I can vividly picture myself writing code and seeing the robot's wheels turn in perfect harmony to weave through a set of paths. More than that, I envision myself creating advanced systems that are present in Amazon or Tesla robots. After all, robotics is a universal field—the concepts that I learn here will apply to all other robots but on a much larger scale.

Learning is the key to innovation. I live by the saying “knowledge is power” because it truly is. Learning has become a necessity because of the rapid technological evolutions. It's the fact that my knowledge can lead to a beautiful creation that gets me excited to learn as much as I can.

essays.prompt: Virtually all of Stanford's undergraduates live on campus. Write a note to your future roommate that reveals something about you or that will help your roommate—and us—get to know you better.
essays.essay:
Dear roommate,

I can't wait to meet you! I already know - this is going to be an epic year. Picture it: between hikes in Santa Cruz, learning to longboard around campus, and hitting up late-night food vendors in Palo Alto, we'll make Stanford the ultimate playground. But first, let me bring a taste of Turkish delights to our room. I've got my mom's recipes memorized and her fervor of cooking in my blood. And, I'll teach you the proper way to drink Turkish coffee – we'll need a couple of those for late night studies.

At Stanford, we'll push each other to try new experiences wherever possible. Maybe that's joining school clubs we've never heard of, training for a half-marathon, trying out a battle of Jugger on the Stanford quad, seeing what the rave of drive-in theaters is about, or trying shipments of exotic fruits; whatever it is, I'm down to make the best of the time that we have here.

And before I forget to mention this, if you hear me speaking a mix of Turkish, Dutch, and English, don't be alarmed. It's just me video calling my family because I'll miss them and I can't wait for you to meet them so it'll all make sense why I'm who I am.

So here's to learning together, being each other's support system, and chasing our graduation caps together. Once a roommate, always co-pilot in life's greatest journeys. Let's make it the best years of our lives!

Sincerely,

essays.prompt: Virtually all of Stanford's undergraduates live on campus. Write a note to your future roommate that reveals something about you or that will help your roommate—and us—get to know you better.
essays.essay:
Dear roommate,

I hate my alarm clock.

But every morning, like a broken record, I let it ring and with a heavy head, heart, and hand, I snooze it, knowing it'll be the same way in five minutes. I hope you don't mind when it rings - if we can deal with my alarm clock, I think we'll be able to deal with anything as roommates.

Now, important things aside, I'm interested in the law, reading, and cars. I'm always down for a talk about anything. Human interaction is one of my favorite ways to disconnect from all the distractions around me and just focus on the people I care about. I also love hanging out in general - my battery recharges with a good time outside. On the walls, you might see a collection of polaroids of my friends and family, as well as letters from loved ones; I'm a pretty sentimental person.

Being at such a beautiful campus, I can't wait for us to spend time outside, like under the trees studying, watching sports in the student lounges, or just exploring the campus to find all the touristy spots that are picture worthy. Off campus, I'd like to explore the surrounding cities – grab a bite, check out the local shops and vendors, and maybe even take a trip to explore further out. Anyways, I can't wait to meet you in person and get through the alarm clocks one day at a time.

Your roommate,

essays.prompt: Virtually all of Stanford's undergraduates live on campus. Write a note to your future roommate that reveals something about you or that will help your roommate – and us – get to know you better.
essays.essay:
Hello!

I'm supposed to write this letter for you to know me better, so here we go!

Let's start off with TV shows. Breaking Bad, Lupin, Reacher, and The Boys are just a few of my favorites. I'm different from most people because I'm the type to rewatch a show more than 20 times (literally). Why? Well, it's because instead of listening to music, listening to the voices of familiar characters helps me concentrate a lot more. Maybe we can binge a show together.

But I also enjoy movies. One of my favorites is Ford v Ferrari which gets me really excited about cars. Oh, do I admire cars. The roar of the v8, the sound of a turbo charging, and the modified exhaust systems are like a symphony to me. Symphony—I should probably mention that I love to play the piano. Been playing since I was five years old. That's probably why I try to find music in anything. Music is truly a wonder. It's my way of expressing my emotions and communicating with my soul.

Back to cars though. I love to watch Paganis and Koenigseggs travel elegantly down the road. They are beautiful works of engineering. Since I love engineering so much, I really want to build my own project car one day. Don't worry I'm not going to assemble an engine in our dorm room, but that would be kinda cool right—us working on a car together.

I can't wait to meet you!

Cheers,

essays.prompt: Briefly elaborate on one of your extracurricular activities, a job you hold, or responsibilities you have for your family. (Stanford short answer, ~50 words)
essays.essay: When starting my mental health nonprofit Overstress, I was enamored with the idea of upcycling. As a tennis player, the most glaring waste I encountered was tennis balls. Experimenting with landscape chippers and eventually partnering with another nonprofit, I was able to turn shredded tennis balls into squishy stress relievers.

essays.promptLabel: Elaborate on an extracurricular, job, or family responsibility
essays.prompt: Briefly elaborate on one of your extracurricular activities, a job you hold, or responsibilities you have for your family. (50 word limit)
essays.essay: A job I hold is at a Kumon center, tutoring kids after school. I find it has helped me be responsible, as I always have to manage my time well and show up to work on time. It has also helped me develop teaching skills.

essays.promptLabel: Elaborate on an extracurricular, job, or family responsibility
essays.prompt: Briefly elaborate on one of your extracurricular activities, a job you hold, or responsibilities you have for your family. (50 word limit)
essays.essay: I help my mom, who prefers staying at home, with household tasks and grocery shopping. She lacks confidence to drive, so I drive her wherever she needs to go. My dad works long hours which leads me to take care of my brother's transportation to various activities and school.

essays.prompt: List five things that are important to you. (Stanford short answer)
essays.essay:
The sigh of relief.
My signature handshake with my brother.
The ready position to prepare myself for a tennis ball - and the other challenges life throws at me.
The stack of Pokemon cards that my parents have long been begging me to get rid of.
Hugs.

essays.promptLabel: Five things that are important to you
essays.prompt: List five things that are important to you. (50 word limit)
essays.essay: My family is crucial and supports me through everything. My computer is my lifeline, storing valuable data. I prioritize physical health, specifically the gym, to avoid medical issues. Chicken, my favorite food, goes with any dish. Money is my main ambition, and fuels my passion above all else.

essays.promptLabel: Historical moment you wish you could have witnessed
essays.prompt: What historical moment or event do you wish you could have witnessed? (50 word limit)
essays.essay: I want to witness Ford's victory at the 1966 Le Mans because beyond speed, the GT40 MK II is a pure work of engineering. This historic race accentuates my love for the design innovation and high-performance feats of the Ford team. It also proves that with dedication, anything is possible.

essays.promptLabel: Historical moment you wish you had witnessed
essays.prompt: What historical moment or event do you wish you could have witnessed? (Stanford short answer, ~50 words)
essays.essay: Albert Einstein's greatest accomplishment. No, not when he discovered the theory of general relativity. Instead, I am interested in something much more important: his weekly sleep routine. The man routinely got more than 10 hours a night! I must find out how. After all, sleep is the most important investment.

essays.promptLabel: How you spent your last two summers
essays.prompt: How did you spend your last two summers? (50 word limit)
essays.essay: I traveled to India with my relatives, where I discovered my roots by partaking in traditional practices, eating cultural dishes, and contributing to household chores. I visited a town in Georgia where I cherished moments with close friends and family. I also dedicated time to advancing my programming skills through side projects.

essays.promptLabel: How you spent your last two summers
essays.prompt: How did you spend your last two summers? (Stanford short answer, ~50 words)

essays.essay: Trouble making eye contact is not just a problem with phones. Rather, we need to break apart the exclusive suburbs, the disconnect between countries, and the dividing hills that separate people. We have designed our lives so that people are apart; in reality we need to be together.

essays.prompt: Please describe why you are interested in attending UNC Charlotte. Your statement lets us get to know you beyond your academic credentials. Your response will distinguish you from other qualified candidates within the applicant pool. (250 words)
essays.essay:
As a finance major at the UNCC I hope to break past the generic corporate finance, but specialize in something deeper like investment banking or private equity, where I can see myself having a real impact for a company. Going to UNCC is the perfect first step to reaching that goal.

Firstly, Charlotte is the second biggest banking city in the US and UNCC being only a 19 minute drive from there makes it perfect for someone like me, who likes to network and meet new people. In a competitive field like private equity, networking is essential for building the relationships that open doors to interviews and opportunities.

Secondly, The Belk College of Business offers a large range of courses, such as Financial Markets and Institutions and Investment Analysis that align perfectly with my goal of entering the private equity field. I’m particularly drawn to the opportunity to learn from professors like Dr. Han and Dr. Karahan, whose research in corporate finance and investment management embodies the analytical rigor and real-world perspective I aim to develop.

Thirdly, UNCC programs/clubs like the Financial Management Association and Niner Venture fund allow me to work with students who have the same passions as me. These organizations will give me a platform to apply what I learn in class, collaborate on projects, and grow as both a leader and a problem solver.

Together, these three pillars make UNC Charlotte a powerful three pronged spear, one designed to cut through the challenges of a highly competitive industry.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
“Your work is impressive! You understood the problem statement and documented the solutions well. Great job!” I did it. I landed my first internship after persistently cold-emailing multiple companies.

This journey leading up to my internship offer began in my freshman year. Since we were all in quarantine, completely bored out of our minds, this was a catalyst for my exploration into new hobbies. This urge to try new things also came shortly after I lost basketball due to an injury, which for better or for worse, led me to programming.

After completing a few certifications on Coursera and applying these skills to coding puzzles in LeetCode, I knew I had to try something more practical. So, I created my first website with a friend for a club we wanted to start.

Luckily for us, sophomore year started our first year of in-person high school. A long-awaited return to school was announced with the inauguration of our Web Development Club. I wanted others to experience the same fire that had built up in me. Since then, we have hosted four of our hackathons with above 100 participants. Not only did we get fantastic feedback, but we also got a lot of support from sponsors like Wolfram Alpha, Art of Problem Solving, and other academic services who offered prizes to the winners of the hackathons.

All of this teaching experience from the club, knowledge from online courses, and work in computer science earned me my first internship in the summer of 2023 at Photon Commerce, a start-up focused on integrating AI into finance documentation. Under the tutelage of their Engineering Lead, I previewed their APIs, took part in stand-in meetings, and provided enhancements for their programs to sophisticate their data collection from financial documents.

The transformative power of computer science to solve almost any problem has profoundly impacted my life. It has shaped me into an avid learner, a capable leader, and a collaborative team member. As I delve deeper into this subject, I find myself captivated by its complexity and potential.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
From a young age, I was captivated by the realm of computers, surrounded by the influences of my parents who worked in the software industry. I vividly recall moments of exhilaration as they revealed what occurred behind the scenes when I watched my first Youtube video. This early exposure planted a seed of curiosity within me, ultimately leading me to discover my true passion for Computer Science.

During the pandemic, I seized the opportunity to advance my programming skills by learning Python and Java, gaining competent skills in programming and logic building. I participated in hackathons and coding competitions such as USACO, which further developed my problem-solving skills. My inquisitive nature led me to explore further, supporting local businesses with website redesigns, taking college courses on UI and network design, and creating various projects to apply my skills. The limitless potential of Computer Science enthralled me, so I persisted in deepening my passion by learning technologies and tackling complex projects.

My determination unveiled new opportunities at a very young age. I furthered my skills in full stack development by joining a startup called Revoteen, a thriving social media platform for teenagers with over ten thousand users. My impressive performance as an intern earned me a permanent position. Working with Revoteen from early stages to its acquisition phase has been amazing, providing valuable insights into technologies such as Next.js (a JavaScript web development framework) and Firebase (a Google Cloud backend cloud computing service). More importantly, Revoteen taught me how to apply my programming skills in the real world, fostering collaboration with a talented team, and building production-quality code.

My experiences inside and outside the classroom have influenced my academic achievement and solidified my decision to major in Computer Science. Working with companies, building awesome projects, participating in difficult competitions, and learning new technologies have cultivated my problem-solving, teamwork, and programming skills. My passion for coding has instilled in me a desire to pursue Computer Science at a higher level. It has molded me into a resourceful, innovative, and intelligent individual. I find programming to be a work of art–its potential to create is only limited by your imagination. This is why I adore it.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
When being asked to write about which subjects I've always held great interest and adeptness in, I have always been quick to feet and fingers in expressing just how much my liking towards biology had been my driving force. Always rivaling my fervor towards other subjects, such as chemistry and the natural sciences, this leaning towards studying medicine and the actual physicality and anatomy of the human brain had expressed itself through countless activities, fellowships, and internship programs that I could easily state, without hesitation, how there had been no clearer path for my future other than getting a degree in neuroscience.

After not much convincing, my professional experience with the field officially started in 2015, when I became a research officer in the Neuroscience Club at my high school where I managed basic tasks such as coordinating activities for club members, helping in creation of many presentation slides, and aiding club members with questions regarding the field. After a year of full commitment, I then became the student representative for Society for Neuroscience Speaker events where we mingled with actual specialists. This was a proper springboard for me to start interacting with doctors, researchers, and other professionals from different backgrounds. I am proud to say that I am still involved with the two mentioned positions.

Studious and competitive as I ever were, I applied and successfully got into numerous research internship programs the minute they became available. In 2017, I got the opportunity to be at the Summer Research Intensives at the University of Massachusetts where I got to work in the Markstein Cancer Research Lab where the focus was on the effects of chemotherapeutic drugs on different types of cancer in the gut of fruit flies. The next summers, I landed consecutive internship summer programs at the University of California Santa Cruz. We first worked with Latinx fourth and fifth graders as part of the Youth Participatory Action Research program and Psychological Research and Action Team. We then went into analyzing mice brains to further understand the neural stem cell differentiation as it relates to ALS and Autism.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
I used to believe the common consensus of my classmates: math education beyond elementary level had few applications in real life. However, my perception of math has since changed. It’s not about what you learn, it’s the way math makes you think.

Math is a tool I use to navigate the world around me. In third grade, I learned to think quickly by rehearsing my multiplication tables. In middle school, I explored my creativity by solving math riddles unconventionally. Now in AP Statistics, I sharpen my analytical skill and logical reasoning when designing population studies. Acquiring these skills has its challenges, but I’ve learned to overcome them by developing the right mentality.

Part of the requirement for enrolling in my AP Calculus class involved taking a Stanford online course called “How To Learn Math”. Though it did not teach calculus concepts, the course focused on something of much greater value: maintaining a growth mindset. If one believes they have the capability to improve, then they can, because intelligence is not fixed. With grit and persistence, anyone can achieve the highest levels of math. I was inspired, and wanted to share my knowledge with other students in need of support.

I established “Successful Solutions”, a tutoring club at my high school for students in all levels of math. Along with the tutors I recruited, I work one-on-one with students, making sure they fully understand each step to solving a problem before moving on to the next. By drawing visual aids on the whiteboard such as graphs and number lines, I help students to better comprehend the material.

Several students who attend my club meetings are deaf and hard of hearing. The process of communicating with them through sign language interpreters allows me to develop greater compassion and patience in my teaching. I watch students gain confidence as they overcome challenges, find solutions, and acquire skill sets. The rewarding feeling after each meeting fills my heart with satisfaction and shows me how empowering math can be.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
I’ve been asking questions my entire life. At age six, I recall sitting in my room terrified at the prospect of eternity. At twelve, I remember gazing at Jupiter and its four largest moons through my eight-inch Dobsonian. At fifteen, I remember hearing the words of Richard Feynman for the first time.

I had been trapped in the endless cycle of YouTube’s deceiving algorithm, and I expected it was going to be another unproductive day on the train ride home from the lab; however, a video titled, “Physics is Fun to Imagine” by Feynman, caught my attention. Interested, I clicked on it and was introduced to a world that I never imagined would have such an impact on me.

Soon enough, complex questions arose out of everyday occurrences. Questions like, “Why does time only move forwards and not backwards?” or “Why does a bicycle stand upright?” were commonplace. Often, I didn’t have the answers to these problems, but physics changed that. Physics, in combination with mathematics, has given me the opportunity to intuitively come to conclusions about the universe, but with scientific proof.

Furthermore, I’ve found that I am most drawn to theoretical physics as I can visualize experiments in my head, and I have a great desire to learn about the phenomena that aren’t discovered experimentally. My desire for this understanding culminated in the purchase of various physics books, but none have superseded the absolute brilliance of “The Feynman Lectures on Physics.” Essentially, the lectures bridged the separation between my intuition and complete understanding with a combination of mathematics and a rigorous introduction to physics.

This introduction, coupled with my IB Physics HL Course, has granted me a solid base from which I can begin my physics career, but I find that my true desire comes not from learning by others, but by creating new knowledge myself. In the words of Newton, I wish “to see a little further by standing on the shoulders of giants” to cultivate an innovative, scientific life where I can propagate new ideas to create a better future for myself and others.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
Fire has always terrified me. I never understood how flames could move so unpredictably, consuming everything in their path. The faint voices singing “Happy Birthday” to me were drowned out by the hypnotizing flame on the candle of my cake that seemed to be alive. Oddly enough, learning about the chemical reaction of combustion turned my fear into fascination for chemistry.

When I first entered chemistry sophomore year, I expected it to be like any other class, unaware I was about to discover an entirely new world of atoms and molecules.

Chemistry changed how I viewed everything. I began to wonder about the interactions of subatomic particles in even the simplest objects, like the pencil sitting on my desk. I was mesmerized by how I was surrounded by so many complex reactions occurring at every single second, yet I could see none of it. As I poured mixtures in the lab, I felt challenged, yet intrigued by how chemistry blended problem-solving and creativity in ways I hadn’t expected.

I enrolled in AP Chemistry my junior year, where I discovered my passion for crystallography. How crystals catch the light perfectly and come in various shapes and colors are what make them alluring to the naked eye; however, I find their beauty in the meticulously ordered structure of atoms repeated multiple times, forming a crystal lattice. Captivated by their stunning composition, I conducted research to grow crystals at home.

With a few household materials and a small notebook to keep my observations, I grew many types of crystals; my favorite was a clear alum crystal that resembled a diamond. Crystal growing is a time taking process, and I experienced lots of trial and error and didn’t always understand what was happening. Experimenting with batteries to extract a chemical paste inside certainly involved many setbacks, but the end result was a beautiful pink sulfate crystal. I delved deeper into my curiosities, allowing me to test the limits of my knowledge. Chemistry ignited a spark within me that drives me to want to know more, and I am excited to continue exploring its wonders.

essays.prompt: Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.
essays.essay:
"Bloomberg reports Gamestop Corp (GME) up 688%". That's what I viewed economics as for the longest time: money moving and stocks going up and down.

That perspective changed in junior year when my microeconomics teacher stated "Economics isn't about money". That's what sparked my curiosity.

While my microeconomics teacher was brilliant in the way he broke down complex topics into simple concepts, it was macroeconomics that swept me off my feet. There was something incredibly engaging about how large-scale decisions, like tariffs or interest rates, can ripple across entire economies. It felt like a behind-the-scenes look at how the world works, and it made me understand how interconnected economics was to other disciplines. On top of that, learning foundational concepts like modeling money market graphs gave me a clear lens into how money really moves in relation to interest rates.

This inspired me to explore economics further in my local community. I started cold-emailing professors at multiple universities about direct research work that I could contribute to because I didn't get accepted into a few research programs I applied to. Surprisingly, after lots of rejections, the Economics Department Chair at a local university gave me a shot.

Together, we researched sports economics, specifically analyzing how sporting events have impacted hotel revenues in my city over the past decade. We also factored in key drivers like pre and post pandemic trends to normalize the data and after collecting over a decade's worth of data, I used GRETL to run regression models to identify patterns and correlations. Through this, we found a statistically significant positive correlation between sporting events and hotel revenues, with average increases ranging from 30-40% on event days. The largest increase was seen for our local pro football team's games, and even higher during their playoff games. Our research is critical because local governments can leverage these findings to support more sporting events, ultimately promoting tourism and small businesses in my city.

This project transformed economics from something theoretical to living. It showed me that behind every data point lies a story about people, choices and communities.

essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
On the night of February 6, 2023, a devastating 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck Southeast Turkey and the Syrian border, leaving thousands of families shattered.

My heart sank as I followed the live updates. All I could think about were the children near the quake's epicenter whom I had taught English to just a year earlier. We formed a special bond learning from each other, and they affectionately called me their big brother.

Now they needed their big brother's help. I launched a fundraiser for impacted Turkish and Syrian children and created presentations for classrooms that I had visited to share stories about the earthquake's impact on families. Despite my efforts, I quickly realized I couldn't do it alone, so I turned to my community for help.

I reached out to my school's leadership program and presented my plan to the board to enlist their support. To make this campaign more impactful, I asked my mom to help gather firsthand stories from affected families. These stories became the focus of my presentation and were featured in our daily school newsletter, inspiring my peers to take action. I then worked with leadership to set up donation jars in classrooms and incentivized participation by offering a pizza reward for the class that raised the most. By the end of two weeks, our collective efforts were a success. We raised over $2,200, which we donated to trusted organizations that provided aid for affected families.

This experience reinforced my belief in the power of a community. By rallying my peers in leadership to take action, I saw how a shared vision can create meaningful changes around the world. I learned the importance of addressing issues I care about, as doing so can encourage others to do the same within their communities. Like how the students I once taught inspired me to step up, in turn, I inspired leadership to do the same. In the end, I knew our efforts wouldn't restore all the damage and lost lives, but we're proud to be of help – to have supported my friends.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
My creative side is expressed in the form of problem solving.

For me, solving problems is like a peculiar form of art - it's a testament of my intellectual abilities and a representation of my fun personality. On second thought, problem solving comes naturally to me because I am a person that enjoys do-it-yourself projects, which uses creative ways to help save money, boost productivity, and create entertainment for ordinary problems.

Take for example the time when I converted all the old cassette holders in my home into phone stands and picture frames. Or the time I built a multi-story dog house with the cardboard and styrofoam from the packaging of a television set. Or even the time when I built a makeshift heater using candles and empty clay pots in the garden. That's just a glimpse into all the little quirky projects that I put my free time into.

But if the previous projects were at all impressive, my latest venture tops everything. I am in the midst of making a water filter for a large fish tank in my home. After years of replacing faulty tank filters and changing out the water weekly, it was time to put some thought into saving my time and money. I convinced my parents to help me and so far, they have been tremendously helpful.

The inspiration behind this idea is actually from an episode of Bear Grylls' "Man vs. Wild" outdoor survival show. He created an effective filter using a bottle and layering rocks, charcoal, sand and grass. I replicated his methods but strapped multiple bottles together to increase the water capacity and the speed of filtration.

Sure enough, the filter worked like a charm, but there were occasional leaks from overflowing. My plan is to add hollow bamboo at the base of the filter to channel the leakage into a separate turtle tank to conserve water or perhaps use pvc pipes to collect the water for flowering plants. Either way, I have another fun project to look forward to and another project to exercise my creative thoughts.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
Aside from my interest in the sciences, I've also always been passionate with performance arts. I've always known that I was a performer since I was just a mere toddler. Being born in the United States, I was surrounded by people who had my features but the media itself were quite lacking, back then, with Indian portrayals. (Which is different now, but we still only have a handful of people like Mindy Kaling and Kal Penn as pop culture representation, aside from popularized Bollywood productions.) As a full American with Indian ethnicity, I have sought performing to feel closer to my South-Asian roots, which made me deviate (in a good way) from the clichéd portrayals. This led me into honing my skills in classical Indian dance and singing.

The former, where I have had 8 years of training for, and have even received my four-year bachelor of dance degree (Bharatanatyam) from the Art Society of Mumbai, located in India. I've also received the Carnatic Chamber Concert Competition Recognition after 10 years of education and training in the very art of Indian classical singing, and have performed at numerous community events where the mixed background and diplomatic relations is the highlight.

Finding the right balance in self-expression and focusing on the sciences has never been easy as, with the numerous practices, both my mind and body were pushed to their limits but it had all been extremely rewarding experiences. Through endless training, I've learned how not just to focus on abstract goals but also in the actuality of having to tirelessly pursue them, not just for the sake of accomplishment or glory but also for the very input of the produce and how I could advocate for furthering the diversity in my social circles.

As America is known as the melting pot of cultures, I'm quite proud of how I've represented American-Indian culture, expressing and preserving what makes our being multicultural a cornerstone of our society. Through these numerous side-activities, I have found quality friendships and opportunities in establishing long-term goals and a deeper understanding of humanities, shared history, and the social sciences.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
Cardboard and hot glue – that's all I needed to express my creative side.

When I was young, I received a few Lego sets as gifts. I liked building them but it was an expensive hobby and usually sat there to collect dust on the shelves. But everything changed when I discovered a cheaper way to build things with just some cardboard and hot glue.

This inspired new creations that were way more fun than Legos because I was the architect of every piece. I remember the feeling of cutting the cardboard into anything I wanted, not being limited by not having certain pieces, which unlocked a lot of creativity for a seven year old me.

My first project was a bird feeder. I traced and cut the pieces out and used the remaining cardboard as a base. Slowly, I glued the walls together, then added a roof gently with a few dabs of hot glue so it wouldn't be too heavy on top and fall apart. To my surprise, after leaving it on the deck outside with some bird food, I had a few visitors stop by.

While this activity gradually slowed down as I grew older and had more responsibilities at school and around the house, I still made time to build. Two years ago, I made a two-story dream garage after my grandma bought me a limited edition set of Hot Wheels from India. She knew how much I loved cars since I was young and I had to reciprocate my appreciation by picking up the glue gun and cardboard once again.

Today, while others might see building things with cardboard as a kid's activity, it's my version of creative expression. It brings back so many great childhood memories and gives me an opportunity to work on a project with my dad in his spare time. Creating what I wanted not only kept me busy in my free time and curbed the time that I spent on my phone, but it also made me a hands-on person, innovative and detail oriented – traits that I will use forever.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
Saturday morning my house is like a scene out of the Food Network. Turkish omelets, toasted sourdough, and organic jams of the variety - my parents source the best ingredients for this breakfast of champions. I, on the other hand, am responsible for plating the food, finding ways to combine staples like Dutch bread with Turkish cheese.

While arranging cultural food seems simple, it's a creative process. It's a balance of colors, nutrients, temperature, and space, all on an 11 inch plate. I like to imagine this process like an economics equation; too much quinoa and we lose demand for the sauteed potatoes, too much greens and we don't have enough space for proteins, and a shortage of olives triggers a scramble for the last piece on the pan. It's the mastery of balancing these variables on a plate that helps train my creative mind in the kitchen.

Soon, I found this creative balancing act carrying over into other facets of my life. At Impactful Tennis, I approach coaching like plating a meal – breaking complex serving and footwork into digestible parts. To improve the coaching experience, I designed coaching guides that simplify tennis into core parts: the rules, the basic technique, and training strategies. The guides are neatly labeled with digital tabs, color-coded, and organized evenly so that users can find what they need quickly. Similarly, with my nonprofit Overstress, I design daily challenges much like a balanced plate. Each activity is created with the intention of engaging a different part of the mind to help members overcome stress. To add a physical element to my design, I experimented with landscape chippers and eventually partnered with another nonprofit to transform used tennis balls into squishy stress relievers.

What started as a simple joy of plating food has taught me to use my creative potential in all parts of my life. Creativity is something that can help me elevate ordinary tasks into something more fun and engaging. In the same way I add balance to my life and passions, I hope to continue to inject creativity to further my learning in university.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side. (UC PIQ; specific prompt number inferred from content)
essays.essay:
It wasn't always so hard.

When I got my phone on my 13th birthday, I was ecstatic. It was more than just a device, it was a rite of passage into my teenage years and to an acceptable social life. I even named it the banana phone because of its yellow hue. To say I was infatuated with my phone would be an understatement.

Yet there was one key distinction. One promise. I vowed that no matter what, no matter how much I loved my phone or its silly banana name, I would never get social media.

Now, when I ask most people, they say social media inspires them, it gives them an outlook of others' lives; but what about not having social media?

Many say that social media is bad for you. Yet everyone always goes back to it, everyone always encourages it, and I needed to find a way to uphold my promise.

The simplest times were in the beginning. When people would ask me for my socials I would simply explain my situation and refuse. But I soon realized I would need to be more elaborate.

I first disabled anything that would attract me to social media on my phone. The next step was letters. I would write using sticky notes on my doors. I would incorporate little aspects into my life that kept me to my promise. I built my own in-person speaking skills. I became a master at connections to get the new information. And I now found time to journal and focus on improving myself.

Not only did not having social media grant me more time to pursue my own creative interests, I was able to express my own creativity in finding ways to exclude it from my life.

While I may not be up to speed on the newest trends, or able to see who is dating who, not having social media has let me spend more quality time with my family, go on my own adventures without worrying about others, and most importantly, find my own creativity.

Maybe it wasn't so hard after all.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
I was 6 when I became a flower expert. Not the kind that has mastered every intricate detail of a tulip or sunflower, but the kind that understands how to turn the 2D strokes on my canvas into a 3D paragon.

Starting in the 1st grade, I became a student at an Asian art school, another attempt from my parents to try to find the spark that would light an innate fire within me, much like the piano and swimming classes every weekend.

Despite this assumption, from the beginning, drawing drew me in. The brush in my hand became an outlet for my mind to run in any direction, exploring body proportions, color theory, and various brush strokes.

Every other week, at least one student had won an award or gotten accepted into an art school. I had come to realize that the kids around me were painting for a trophy, to reach some sort of achievement that would boost them to higher levels. I had considered trying as well, but recognized that the constant pressure to get better, similar to the other activities and classes in my life, would drown out my passion.

Regardless of my decision to stray away from the competitive aspect of art, I found a way to continue to enjoy and develop my skill, applying it to another facet of my life: gifting. Rather than using store-bought cards, I spent time curating handcrafted, personalized ones that reflected my sincerity. Employing my watercolor palette, I painted flowers and petals with various opacities, bringing a pop of color to the dulled-toned cardstock. With a pencil in hand, I drew portraits, cartoons, patterns and embellishments, filling the empty space with character. It became clear that my skill was not bound to the number of awards I had, but by my ability to share a little part of it with those I cared for. Now, armed with a paint brush, I set off to cultivate a blossoming garden, determined to foster life into each and every card.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
While maintaining a good physical shape, a competitive mindset, and furthering my passion to travel, I still find myself attached to the comforts of my laptop and cellphone. There's good reason for my inclination towards the technology around me: I am expanding my interests beyond economics by learning to code.

Growing up in an era where forums and blogs have become popular lodgings for technology enthusiast like me, I've been influenced into the world of coding as a practical skill set for everyday problem solving. This is where I express my creativity - both in the actual writing of codes and the problem solving processes associated.

When I code, my philosophy is self-reliance. Far too often, software engineers engage in sharing proprietary lines of codes to help others take shortcuts in their own projects. For me, I use my own creativity and intuition to develop complicated codes that are multi-functional and highly efficient. Granted, coding is not a simple task, I would spend hours to create a simple function instead of using codes that are accessible to the public in various online databases. Take for example my most recent project, which is a mathematical simulator that approximates supply and demand curves based on multiple parameters. Rather than using simple C++ computer language, I opted for the more archaic and tedious R language. I even designed a live background on the website with mosaic shapes as the theme.

In choosing my major, my passion aligns with economics, and computer science as an interdisciplinary subject of interest. I find that in the space of economics and computer science, creativity is not only necessary, but essential for being outstanding. These fields demand more than just wits, memorization, and work ethic to be successful; it takes creativity, trial-and-error, and the ability to try different perspectives to find success. At university, I will continue to develop new ways to learn about economics. I will explore this subject matter in combination with my background in coding to achieve new insights into a field that necessitates creativity and innovation.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
I'm a proud aquascaping hobbyist. That's right - I'm talking about the niche craft of underwater gardening that takes terrarium building to a whole new level. Yes, I'm one of those people that spend weeks gathering aesthetic pieces of driftwood and rocks in plastic boxes, days ideating and sketching designs of a mini-environment, and hours positioning, sculpting, and gluing a masterpiece of an aquarium. These are the passion projects that reflect my blossoming creativity and the appreciation that I have for the environment.

For me, aquascaping is an escape. Not the kind of escape that temporarily freezes time so that college finals, job interviews, and utility bills can remain distant so that I can enjoy my young adult life, but the kind that almost feels like a mini dive session off the coast of some islands surrounded by the clearest blue waters. It's an indescribable feeling of watching my own artwork come alive at the end of a project, when the lights are strategically angled to accentuate the sandy waterfall that's surrounded by greenery that I meticulously trimmed and planted. I can't say the feeling is as pleasant in the process of gluing things that keep falling apart, or rocks that seem to have feet of their own, but it's all worth it in the end.

In the dim of the night, as I carefully introduce the algae, the cute apple snails, and the glowing tetras, the liveliness of the aquascape exposes my quiet excitement. It's a burst of satisfaction that can only be compared to the thrill of a young child seeing the Monterey Bay Aquarium for the first time. This is why I love aquascaping. It's not just an outlet for creativity, but an engine for creative growth. The more I stare at the life multiplying in these mini worlds that I've created, the more hungry I become for the next project. My brain becomes a pool of creative thoughts and the artist in me is screaming at the highest pitch. Now, back to cleaning this tank and trimming these overly grown lily pads.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
To me, computer science perfectly encapsulated the beauty of creativity. In studying this science, I have found real world issues that could be solved through innovative thinking and computer technology. Just like painting a portrait or carving a statue, computer science allows me to express my creative side and has given me the tools to learn at a faster pace and at a deeper level. It is one of the most gratifying and enjoyable outlets that I have found for my creative instincts.

The more I study computer science, the more I learn how to harness my skills and convert them into real solutions to challenging problems. In the process, I have had many accomplishments, such as creating a dietary tracking app and a website for uploading my photographic portfolio, but I've also had a fair share of mistakes, such as attempting to create a mobile application in the wrong computer language. Nonetheless, the last two years have been a productive period of learning as I took aid from professors, classmates, and an online community of technology experts. As I now know, creativity does not mean indulging in every idea or impulse - rather, I have learned that my creativity in computer science is inspired through planning, assessing what's not available to the public, and adding my personal touch to the visual elements.

Fortunately, my creative outlets are not only limited to computers. I also take pride in being a creative artist of sorts. My parents tell me that at a young age, my teachers recognized my knack for painting and sculpting. They often joke this ability was passed on from my grandfather who had a short stint in selling handmade, painted clay pottery in his youth. It's an interesting thought, but I know that much of this ability is a product of my vivid imagination and my practice in graphics arts since I first learned about photoshopping. So, in the end, I guess that my background in computers ultimately contributes to my creativity and I couldn't be more excited to study computer science at the University of California.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side. (UC PIQ; specific prompt number inferred from content)
essays.essay:
Snap, twist, I weave my fingers through his in a fluid motion. That is, until a sudden grip of tension - my palm had caught on to my brother's as the friction of two avid Handshakers collided to a halt. "Dang it! Let's try one more time."

I was a Freshman when my family went to my Dad's hometown in the Netherlands. However, my brother and I couldn't always have the attention for sprawling little houses and cobbled roads - we were kids, and we demanded excitement. Three years younger than I, my brother's smile was filled with gaps like missing pieces of a puzzle and wavy hair that wouldn't quite form into curls. I was much the same. But nevertheless, we were up to the challenge: to create our own ultimate handshake.

Step 1: The base.

The first part of any good handshake, and any good idea is the foundation. Handshakes can be overwhelming - that's why we started with a firm clasp of our hands. An excited elderly man I met on the street once told me that when you go for a handshake, "You grip firmly, look the person right in the eye, and say I want a high paying job with little work." Heeding his advice, we got to work.

Step 2: Flesh it out.

Now that you have the base, inject complexities into your work. Finger motions, maybe a loop. A new team member, a finished business model.

Step 3: Add some flair.

Revise, contemplate, and share. Ignite the creativity from the recesses of the mind. Experiment with arm movements, full-body motions, and don't forget to end with a "snap." Now you have the final product - a handshake, a nonprofit business, a new idea for an internship.

Extra Step: Have some fun.

My parents and a few passersby suddenly turned their heads as they heard a resounding "Clap" - an open toothed smile erupted on my brother's face. "We nailed it."

I embed this process into my life. It has become the blueprint to new ideas. And every time I see my brother, I make sure to give him a handshake.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced. (Standard UC PIQ prompt; inferred from content, not printed in the document.)
essays.essay:
“You need to let go.” My mother said, trying to shake my arm off as I violently cried into her coat. We were at the gates of hell. In thick bold lettering presented my doom. “Preschool.” It was a challenge I was not willing to face. My mother finally managed to rip me off from her arm and toss me into the room of kids. There, I experienced my first time outside my box. My safe, comfort box.

English has always been a subject I resented because I’ve been so unfamiliar with it. Yet I still rejected that idea even when it was apparent that I struggled. As the studious, asian girl, I needed to work things out on my own, that’s how I liked it, right? High school rolls in, I turn in my first essay, and I receive the worst grade I’ve ever seen. Then the SAT rolls by, I take it, and my English score drops. The bus finally hits me full force. It was then it dawned on me, I can’t keep sitting here and let myself rot in my box. I needed to step out and I knew.

Before then, asking for help to me was like proving to the world that I’m dependent and weak. I couldn’t bear the shame. After seeing how poor I was doing in English however, I knew I needed to step out. I started to come to extra classes for support. There, I connected with students who were able to give me feedback, and slowly I gained the courage to talk to teachers. That’s when I peaked. I aced the next essay and increased my SAT English score by 80.

Healthy, dependable bonds were created with my teachers and English no longer frightened me. That comfort zone never really helped me nor others. Now, I can confidently recognize when I need to make changes, and it motivates me to try new things. With that, I am ready to fit into any environment. I’m ready to face my next challenge.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
“Today, we will write an analytical essay on the influence of the Romantic Era on contemporary writing”.

This was senior year of high school. I spent two long nights reading a series of poems by the great Ernest Hemingway and I was excited to produce some of the best material for my English teacher. I was genuinely excited about the assignment because I finally came across a prompt that I felt confident about. With my pen firmly gripped and my mind fully focused, I began to write profusely an introduction that I felt was my best work. Everything went smoothly - that is until I reached the thesis. My confidence escaped me and I ended up with a final product that received a barely passing grade.

Essay writing is perhaps my greatest weakness, and I have attempted many different strategies to improve the quality of my work - such as verbalizing my ideas into a recorder, annotating my thoughts into outlines, asking for peer feedback, and using online essay checkers to determine the source of my weakness. In doing so, I learned that in every essay, my biggest problem is that I am unable to organize all my ideas in a cohesive manner and even more problematic is my lack of creativity to engage my audience in the introduction.

This year, my writing has improved significantly. With the help of a private writing tutor that is detail-oriented and unafraid to provide constructive criticism, I learned to write content-rich material, communicate my ideas effectively, and answer essay prompts. In the past, I was under the impression that good vocabulary alone would get me far, which encouraged me to use the “synonym” function on Microsoft Word religiously.

Now, having learned through trial and error, and incorporating the feedback from my tutor, I am a better writer. Certainly I haven’t mastered the craft of writing, but I continue to spend my time productively at libraries and local coffee shops with my tutor to improve on my weaknesses - specifically on constructing a thoughtful thesis, evaluating evidence properly, and synthesizing a connection between myself and the audience.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
"I survived war, kid… but this pain? Some days it feels like it's winning," said the agonized Vietnam veteran in a heavy accent and a prosthetic on his right leg.

As a volunteer at the Veterans Hospital, I spent countless hours listening to veterans share stories of their service, sacrifices, and the pain that they carry. While wheeling them to their appointments, I often wished I could ease even a fraction of their suffering. When I dropped one veteran off, he looked at me and said, "You are capable of becoming a great nurse. I believe in you." This was when I knew that healthcare was my path.

Recently, I earned one of only twelve spots in my school's Certified Nursing Assistant internship program at the Northern California Nursing Academy. This opportunity has expanded my knowledge of patient care and how every interaction varies. Throughout this internship, I learned the essential tasks of a nurse, from changing a patient with injured arms to providing modified bed baths for those with limited mobility. These simple acts of service in helping to ease a patient's worries showed me how small gestures can have a significant impact on a patient's well-being.

One lesson that left a strong impression on me was learning about the Gate Control Theory of Pain, which suggests pain signals can be blocked in the spinal cord before reaching the brain. Seeing pain through this lens helped me understand why some veterans described their pain as overwhelming and why practices like repositioning them in bed or even having a conversation could bring relief.

This internship has put me a step ahead in my healthcare career, enabling me to utilize my skills to support others sooner. In a couple of months, I look forward to starting clinicals and aim to earn my certification by the end of the program. The CNA program has become a foundational step in my education, sharing the kind of healthcare provider I'd hope to become – one that cares for others with the same faith they place in me.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
In China, I was fortunate enough to have access to academic support outside of school, but by no means was I raised in an upscale household. My parents held blue-collar jobs but made tremendous financial sacrifices - or as they say “expensive investments” - to ensure that I received the best education that they could afford. I didn't take their provision lightly and I worked harder than most of my peers.

Each Sunday, while my friends gathered at internet bars to play team-based videogames and persistently invited me without success, I met with a private tutor instead. My parents hired a tutor through a social networking group to help me with my planned transition to the U.S. This was a huge financial commitment for my family because my tutor was an American expat with decades of experience preparing Chinese students that planned to study in the U.S. That being said, his time was expensive. In fact, my father secretly took on an additional part-time job to pay for the tutoring expenses because he didn't want me to feel discouraged about the cost. Nonetheless, I was incredibly grateful and I attribute my English literacy to the help that I received.

Thinking back, I've always had a knack for learning languages. I spoke Cantonese, Mandarin, and two other Chinese dialects fluently, but English always gave me the hardest time. In middle school, I butchered English and despised it like an enemy. Maybe it's the alphabet system, or all the caveats of grammar rules, or maybe the pronunciation of letters - whatever it was, it challenged me. My tutor ultimately became my handbook for success. He provided me with all kinds of unconventional learning methods that accelerated my growth. As part of my unique regiment, I listened to radio podcasts in English, read subtitles of American films, memorized musical lyrics from hip hop classics, and wrote daily diaries just to speed up my learning curve.

Today, after 10 years since my first encounter with English, I feel accomplished. I took on English with brute force and found my way through its maze.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
I have always been conscious of how deeply competitive and how quickly evolving the academic and business atmosphere had been in Silicon Valley. Being so engrossed with my pursuits in high school - taking AP courses, getting my 4.70 GPA and 1550 in the SATs, my commitment to different science clubs and very selective programs, studying classical singing and dance - I found there to be barely enough time to actually invest in my social life as a teenager. I worried quite a bit on what I may have been missing out, if I may be so blunt. Looking for guidance from my parents and peers, my concerns were easily rectified and I got into thinking more on how I could balance enjoying my early years while also being in fruitful places of business.

From September 2018 to October 2019, I have been offered the great opportunity to shadow doctors: a family physician and a child and adult psychiatrist. Being in these environments, I got to see more than just the hectic schedules of modern-day professionals. I also got to know them as human beings who have become pivotal to my understanding of how one should operate under all the many stresses of the jobs.

Taking great inspiration from the doctors that have been instrumental in my growth as a budding professional, I've opened up to another thing which I have always wanted to try, which is travelling. Backpacking through most of the Western states and Northern Europe, I learned about the differences in culture and economic backgrounds while also getting more in touch with myself through natural, technological, and human resources. Not only had I been able to find a great way to unwind and meditate in beautiful landscapes and plan about how I could help further the advancements of sciences, I have also learned how to avoid being too burnt-out. Coming back to California in more relaxed conditions, I was able to easily catch up with whichever small things I may have missed, reconnected with my friends, and got into putting more of myself with every pursuit.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
Five years ago, I took advantage of an opportunity that completely changed the direction of my life. At first, I refused to go, but my mom signed me up for a tutoring program anyway. I was upset because I envisioned a different kind of summer – traveling, unlimited naps, watching movies. But in the end, I lost that battle and attended. That small choice became the turning point I never saw coming.

Before the program, school to me was meaningless. I was obsessed with the dream of becoming a professional eSports player, spending an embarrassing amount of time playing. My grades fell into an abyss, and I lost every bit of motivation to try. It felt like I was trying to deadlift an elephant, I was too far behind to catch up. What made it worse was seeing students around me visiting colleges, working part-time jobs, or camping out at Starbucks to study. I was never part of that picture. That's when I started to wonder: what if there was more out there for me?

This program has taught me real-life skills that school doesn't have, like how to build a resume, write professional emails, communicate better in interviews, manage my budget better, and improve my overall writing and speaking.
