But what impacted me most was when my mentor told me three words: "You have potential." Me hearing that pushed me to work harder and believe in myself. I pushed my mom to sign me up for more classes. I started to volunteer, taking school seriously, and slowly improving my grades. Most importantly, my mindset changed, I gained confidence, began talking to teachers and classmates more, managed my time better, and realized that education could give me more opportunities video games couldn't guarantee.

Looking back, I learned that I was able to pull myself out of a bad place. That summer program didn't just help me with school, but it allowed me to believe in myself, both in and out of school.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
Most people in my generation had become pigeonholed into 'just being natural' in terms of reacting to and interacting with technology, and this is the farthest thing from the truth. You hear terms like 'tech-savvy' being thrown around so often that it has become synonymous with 'tech-literate'. But everyone from my generation have always shown varying degrees of adeptness to technology. What's more is that there are thousands who become so good so quickly at their respective fields, they are held as 'geniuses'– a word which had lost its value to this age's tokenism.

I do not consider myself an accidental genius with computers. What I am is because I sought out information that had always been readily available but easy to ignore. During my years in high school, I had already been showing great interests in the field of technology and applications. While most kids my age focused on band practices, debate preparations, or content creation, I had always taken the time to learn about back-end development of websites and apps which weren't even, more than half the time, required for a passing grade. Learning how to code during free hours, to most, becomes a solitary practice; but I take it now as rewarding in building character.

My commitment to tech in itself, although still in early stages, is what keeps me going. I have also integrated usage of Adobe software, Maya, Vegas Pro, Android SDK, XAMPP, cPanel, Sublime Text 3, and FileZilla into my day-to-day. With the help of my seniors who I share the same interests in programming with, I have even produced my own WordPress child themes, which may not be that daunting a task, but is still a good springboarding experience. Moving forward in my life, I would like to take this innate interest in learning the ways of programming so that I could be one of the many people who make our day-to-day lives more seamless– or as to say, making the world a better, more convenient place to live in along with the geniuses and the frontliners.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
The most significant educational opportunity that I have taken advantage of was attending community college.

I find that two of the greatest perks in attending community college is the extended preparation time that I am granted to comfortably transition into university as well as the supportive community of TAG-bound students that have given me useful advice to ease through the transfer process.

At community college, I felt a greater degree of freedom to explore my passion for economics and business in depth - all while trying new strategies to improve my studying habits and my proficiency in mathematics. My peers and I can also attest that the faculty at community college has played a critical role in guiding students towards the right direction - regardless of major, ethnicity, or academic background. I was fortunate to have instructors that really wanted me to achieve by giving me the extra attention I needed during office hours.

In particular, my introduction to economics instructor gave me very useful advice in the admission process. He talked to me about his personal experience of trying to find his path while he was a freshman community college student at San Jose State University, and explained that this was an important time for him to grow as a learner instead of a dweller. What he taught me was that community college should not be a place where students feel discouraged and fixate on the mistakes made in the past; community college as I learned, should be a fresh slate to do away with bad habits and concentrate on learnings and developing interests. Had I not taken advantage of community college - and office hours for that matter - I may not have the optimistic outlook that I have today.

Of course, the TAG-bound community has also been fundamental to my progress. I am part of a large Facebook group where transfer students exchange important information, advice, and updates regarding the admission progress. Here, I learned about the demands of the economics major and developed a full, four year plan of my university schedule across all 9 UC's.

essays.prompt: Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.
essays.essay:
My dad once told me that he would rather be exceptional at one skill than to be half-glass full at a hundred things. "What's the use of learning how to fix half a car or knowing how to design half a home?", he questioned. I couldn't argue, only that I wasn't planning to be a brilliant mechanic or architect by any means. But I understood his point loud and clear. Knowing half of anything is good, but mastering one thing is always much more desirable.

To that thought, my dad was very adamant that I learn English - and learn it well. He wanted me to be a "proper" student in America, speaking the language without an accent like a native. He explains, the reality of being Taiwanese in America is the inherent discrimination that exists when some hear the "immigrant" tones that are soldered into the way we pronounce certain letters and words. I took him seriously because this was the doorway to an educational opportunity that I could create for myself using the resources that I had: the Internet and books.

As much as Mandarin is near and dear to my heart as a native language, English as I've come to learn is a necessity, not a want. I know that in order to achieve my goals, I must prioritize my ability to speak and write "proper" English. That being said, I took it upon myself to leverage the magnificent world of digital e-books and podcasts. The two in combination have greatly accelerated my progress in English over the years; the best $6.99 monthly subscription investment I've made so far. These educational resources provided me with an opportunity to learn about economics, start up businesses, venture capitalism, communication strategies, and self-help methodologies.

The hours of churning through this amazing content from experts in these fields and the many nights of falling asleep with Airpods stuck in my ears the next morning (super painful by the way) has finally paid off. I'm no longer the half glass full person that held me back in everything that I did.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
One day I came across a video on bullet journaling, and realized I wanted to start one.

It serves as a self-designed planner that I decorate every month and an outlet for me to destress and creatively express my artistic side. I decide a theme for every month of the year, and take a day out of the thirty days to decorate each spread aligned with its theme. I drew an ocean with diverse patterns of blue to represent February, a garden of colorful flowers for April, a lit city skyline for March, and that one day where I would plan the next month was always a day I looked forward to. It gave me the chance to put my worries aside and let the creativity flow.

It also serves as a normal planner because I'm about as forgetful as they come.

It ranged from being a test I didn't realize was coming up to completely blanking on a chore my mom had just assigned me. It's a flaw that has held me back from reaching my full potential as a student, with having to sloppily cram homework assignments in the period before, and giving up on studying for tests that I didn't know were the same day.

But once I started my bullet journal I've been able to reach my full potential.

I jot down what days I have tests, when homework is due, projects that I need to work on, and other events that impact my schedule. I got to take my time doing my homework, trying to get the answers right and not just completed. I got more involved in big projects, finishing my share of the work. I was also able to study for tests in advance and get scores I was proud of, knowing I did my best. It allowed me to become a better student overall.

This past year my bullet journal has been an important form of expression in my life, while also being a vital part of my success at school.

essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
Having a passion for business, it only makes sense that I am part of a sneaker culture that resells highly coveted shoes for high profits. However, being a reseller of sneakers is not as easy as waking up early, adding the shoes to cart, and entering payment information. It's nearly impossible to buy certain shoes without some type of loophole or lesser-known strategies - especially since stores began using a "queue" or online waiting room to lower the success of resellers.

This is where I get creative. Over the last two years, I have created two effective strategies to buy some of the most limited shoes that end up being resold for multiple times its original value. The first method takes advantage of a loophole by using a shopping bot that I developed. A bot is a program that overrides the waiting rooms of a web page and automatically purchases the item as soon as the product becomes available. To do so, I learned to code in the Perl computer language, which I spent months practicing, but was worth the effort.

As for my second strategy that I developed, I call it the "split screen" method, which involves modifying the computer graphics settings to split one monitor into 16 smaller screens. In doing so, this allows me to open 64 waiting room webpages at once, which significantly improves my chances of purchasing a shoe. The logic behind this strategy is that having one screen on my monitor would only provide enough space to open 4 waiting room webpages, however, a simple change on the graphics will give the effect of having 16 computers.

Evidently, I will go to great lengths to buy a limited shoe; after all, I have an entrepreneurial spirit that motivates me to try new business ventures. The lesson that I learned from reselling sneakers and doing so in a creative way is that creativity can often go hand-in-hand with business. This experience also demonstrates to me that being creative is not always about producing something visually pleasing - it can also come in the form of problem-solving.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Writing is my greatest skill.

I've created stories, settings, and characters ever since I was four feet tall with pigtails in my hair. And I've grown a lot since, including my love to write and this desire to publish a novel like the ones on the shelves. Eventually, by the end of my junior year I'd written, edited, published, and released my first novel, and I have to say it was some of the most stress inducing, frustrating work I've ever endured.

The other day I was cleaning out my computer of old documents, and I was able to come across the very first draft of my novel. I read over each sentence, and physically felt my body cringe at how horrible it was. It left me dumbfounded how such an embarrassing, dumpster fire of a draft turned into a perfected novel I'd gladly call my own.

The idea originated during sophomore year from reading The Catcher in the Rye all day. I'd never read anything so authentic, concerning modern day adolescence. I became obsessed with writing something that meant something to someone.

The next year was full of writing, rewriting, deleting, and rewriting again, googling advice for how to develop the middle plot, watching YouTube videos on character development, examining blog posts on how to construct the anti-hero, researching the Vietnam War, going on random name generator websites, cracking open Stephen King's writing tips book to discover why adverbs are bad, being convinced and replacing every single adverb, and so much growth as a writer.

Writing a novel teaches you a lot of lessons, from patience to motivation, but the most essential tip that ultimately led to my success, is that it's a team effort, whether you rely on strangers or peers. If I'd been dependent wholly on myself, I would've given up before I even started.

I wouldn't wish the pain of writing a novel on my worst enemy, but I've never felt such gratification as I did when I held the first physical copy of my book.

And I wouldn't trade that for the world.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
The bright spotlight cast a warm glow on the grand piano's keys. I looked to my side and saw hundreds of people at the theater ready to listen to me play. I took a deep breath as my fingers grazed the black and white keys to locate the starting position. A world of melody unraveled before my eyes as I pushed down the keys and started to play "Für Elise." This moment marked the beginning of a lifelong passion.

When I took my first piano lesson at five years old, my dad noticed the talent within me. This talent, coupled with the refuge I found in the melodies, was the reason I continued to play the piano every day. Beyond the black and white keys was an escape—a place where I could convert the paper notes into beautiful sounds. Many hours of practice and dedication allowed me to play challenging pieces such as the 3rd Movement of Beethoven's "Moonlight Sonata" and Debussy's "Clair de Lune." I even took piano exams to test my skills.

The more I played, the more the music engulfed me. I pivoted my focus from classical music to "impromptu" music. This style requires great skill and devotion as it demands me to harness my creativity by creating music in the moment. While classical music is an extension of someone else's emotions, "impromptu" music directly amplifies mine. Each new piece was a reflection of who I was at that instant.

Playing the piano taught me more than musical syntax. It revealed the depths of my patience and determination. Spending endless hours mastering each measure, and facing the frustration of misplaying a section, taught me resilience. As the years passed, my relationship with the piano became stronger. It was an extension of my soul. The music I created was an expression of my highs and lows, the wins and losses. Every time I sat on the piano bench, I felt relieved as I could release my happiness and love into the world. I discovered not only my talent but also who I am—a musician and a creative soul.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Five years ago, I stumbled across an online forum dedicated to the topic of "Jailbreaking". Unlike what this term might insinuate, jailbreaking is basically unlocking a device that allows users to customize just about everything within the phone through third-party softwares. I liked this idea a lot; it gave me the freedom to personalize my phone to my specifications, and that was enough reason for me to spend hours jailbreaking my phone.

Shortly after jailbreaking my phone, I changed the font of the virtual keyboard, modified the battery and Wi-fi symbols, and added moving animation to the home screen. This gave my phone a refreshing feel, but this was all internal changes- the outer casing of my phone was still a bland white color with scratches and dents from general wear-and-tear. With the idea of changing the outer appearance of my phone, I took my curiosity to Google and discovered an entire world of mobile customization websites that provided tutorials on exactly how to take phones apart and install all types of aftermarket parts.

Needless to say, I had a lot of fun customizing my phone. I installed a larger battery, replaced the metal casing with a more durable carbon fiber exterior, and swapped out the old LED screen with an aftermarket alternative that was more responsive. From this experience, I developed more than just an interest in customizing things - I developed a skill in it. Customizing something is complicated; it requires studying instructional manuals, following precise instructions, deconstructing the object, and putting it back together in working order.

After my phone was fully customized to my liking, I moved on to customizing my laptop, and later to my car which now has a full set of Japanese-imported headlights, a new exhaust pipe, and to top it all off, a shift knob that looks like a joystick from the old arcade systems.

For me, the appeal of customization is that there are an endless amount of possibilities for change. I like to own things that stand out - it makes for a great conversation and allows me to express my creativity and preferences.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Talents come in all shapes and sizes. For me, snowboarding highlights my physical talents like none other, and I take pride in the amount of practice that I've committed to this sport. About four years ago, I discovered my love of snowboarding by accident when my family planned a last-minute trip to the Bear Mountain Resort. I remember nagging my parents to go someplace else like Kauai in Hawaii to see the migrating humpback whales that I saw on Youtube and suggested that even Las Vegas would be more ideal for its winter festivities. But without success, we stuck to Bear Mountain.

Unlike most talent stories that start off with good sentiments, my story begins with a concussion and sprained ankles. Of course, the teenage angst in me underestimated the slippery slopes. I waived the snowboard tutorials because I thought, how hard could it be to balance on a wooden plank strapped to my feet? My second mistake: taking the aerial lifts to the intermediate elevations where I was ready to experience the thrilling acceleration. But shortly after I launched forward, I woke up with a blinding flashlight pointed directly into my pupils and a crowd of concerned adults and kids surrounded me. I wanted to springboard up and pretend I was fine, but I was too disoriented. I later learned that I fell backward midway down the slope and the back of my head thudded hard against the snow, leaving me with a mild concussion and a bruised ego.

That night, I was instructed not to sleep in case of further complications like a coma. I sat in the cabin, feeling grateful to be alive. But this incident didn't leave me afraid. It felt good to have dared myself to my physical limits, and from then on, I actually learned to snowboard in Truckee through an instructor. Since then, I've mastered countless tricky maneuvers like the fancy inverted rotations and flips to some goofy tricks called the Canadian bacon, gorilla, mule kick, and pickpocket; and of course, I learned to ride down the slopes without losing more brain cells!

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
If there's anything that I am truly proud of, it's my ability to pick up random skills that have little to no practical value. But at least the learning process is always fun.

I consider myself to be a harborer of random skills. I can ride a unicycle, spin a pen on my fingertips, create a Bob Ross-esque painting, solve a Rubik's cube, and choreograph quite the impressive dance routine to my favorite songs. It's evident that I am far from the statistical norm of the stereotyped Chinese female, but this is what makes me unique.

But perhaps my greatest skill is dishing up a perfectly cooked dry-aged ribeye steak. This is about the only real skill that is useful, especially for holiday dinners or celebratory nights that are worth putting the time and effort to make a dry-aged steak.

I first learned about dry-aged steaks about two years ago from my uncle who I consider as a food connoisseur. He is truly an artist when it comes to making dishes of all sorts. He is also my go-to source for learning new flavors of rib eye seasonings from Mediterranean, Malaysian, Korean, and the classic Japanese style.

Ever since my uncle taught me how to dry-age using a refrigerator and mountains of salt, I was hooked. I absolutely embrace the idea of dry-aging because the flavor palette is irreplicable through traditional methods of cooking steak. The richness of a dry-aged steak mimics the flavor of mushrooms and truffles - an odd but delicious flavor that makes every bite enjoyable.

In hindsight, I have developed this skill of dry-aging and cooking through trial and error. I've gained an appreciation for cooking, but more importantly, discovered another skill that makes me feel very capable.

Moving forward, I will continue to improve the many skills that I possess and grow my passion for cooking. In fact, I am beginning to teach my younger cousins how to bake sweets such as gingerbread cookies and velvet cupcakes. My hope is to broaden my expertise in general cooking and to give others a great experience.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
It's midnight - my body and mind is ready to shutdown. But before I could get comfortable, I heard a distressing cry for help from my mom. No, this was not an emergency, but a faulty cell phone signal was probably the closest thing to that. Of course, in the middle of the night, I had to diagnose a cell phone.

This is not an infomercial to sell my cell phone repairing services, but I am skilled when it comes to fixing electronics. That being said, I do not blame my parents for taking advantage of this skill that I possess when something in the house stops working.

My story behind how I developed this skill always brings back fond memories. It started with a late night essay in high school, a lot of opened tabs on my browser, then a "blue screen of death" - the frozen screen that many people with an old laptop must have experienced at least once in their lifetimes.

In short, my computer overheated and this time it was gone for good. It was during this time that I learned to build customized desktop computers. It was a very popular and an affordable alternative to buying the pre-built computers in stores. I was first introduced to this culture of tech savviness by my friend who sold customized computers as a side business. He taught me everything from the function of different components to how the pieces came together.

Building my first computer was a defining moment for me. It felt rewarding and I was immensely proud to be a girl that knew more than just the brand of a computer, but I was still a novice then. My skill developed significantly when I learned about circuitry and soldering from YouTube and technology repair forums that I found on the Internet. The combination of these two skills meant that I could do more than just build computers, but I could also fix almost any hardware problems.

Sometimes I wonder, what if my computer didn't stop working? I might have developed a skill in cramming late night essays instead.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Ever wonder what can be made with powdered gelatin, butter, cornstarch, boiling water, and a paint sprayer? Skittles. This is an absolutely random recipe that I came across while watching a segment on Bon Appetit, a YouTube channel known for recreating gourmet versions of traditional candy. This is exactly the type of content that I look forward to at the end of a long day, and precisely my source of inspiration for developing my skill in cooking.

By my parent’s standards, I am a great cook. My interest in cooking developed at a young age while watching my parents tactfully prepare customary dishes of Chinese food full of vibrant colors and packed with a combination of flavors. By the time I was in high school, I purchased a small grill set to entertain my interest in cooking. On weekends, I spent a lot of time in the backyard preparing the grill to cook peppercorn steaks, marinated pork bellies, and sweet yam - which are my speciality dishes. To further develop my skill in cooking, I would join my parents in the kitchen, which has been a great learning experience that has allowed me to diversify my skill beyond cooking on the grill. Through my parents, I also perfected the craft of soup-making. Making a pot of soup is actually far more difficult than I had previously imagined. In the past, I relied on online soup recipes and food delivery subscriptions like Spoonful of Comfort if I wanted soup, but under my parent’s guidance, I have learned to make my favorite beef bone marrow soup and a classic lobster consomme that I often make for potlucks and family parties.

My hope is that in university, I would be able to impart my knowledge of cooking to the friends that I will meet and learn from others that have experience in different cultural dishes. Cooking is truly my greatest passion apart from computer science, and though the two are unrelated for the most part, both involve a learning process, patience, and attention to fine details.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Life often feels like standing in the sun-soaked streets of Chinatown, balancing a stack of sun-glossed oranges on a wobbly scale while sniffing the earthy aroma of dried herbs that drifted from a street down. That's how I've learned to navigate my own world, a fusion of academics, sports, and responsibilities. Growing up in Chinatown, my grandma and I ran errands weekly, and while weighing oranges one afternoon, she shared a valuable lesson about how "Balance is the key to success." I never forgot it.

For years, I've practiced the art of hula every Saturday morning, much like weaving gracefully through the chaotic, narrow sidewalks without bumping into the elderly. Every Sunday, Kumon added another pound to my heavy scale. Some days, this hectic routine felt physically demanding and mentally draining, and I relied on caffeine-fueled naps to finish homework, leaving little time for self-care. This didn't stop me; it just slowed me down.

Eventually, I realized that these unhealthy habits weren't sustainable – they were tipping the scales too far. So, I adjusted my routine, replacing the caffeine-powered naps with eight hours of sleep and peeling twenty minutes every day to journal as a way to restore balance and keep me grounded. Over time, I've become methodical, as the repetition of my schedule has made me well-adapted and surprisingly diligent.

Still, the scale tips in one direction depending on the season of life. Some days, I put more weight on studying for an exam or prioritizing volleyball before an important match. My grandma once told me time management isn't about doing as much as you can, but doing each thing with intention, like peeling an orange, splitting my day into even sections. Over time, many of my friends, family members, and teachers have commended me for it, making the little me proud.

Just as I once balanced oranges on a mini Chinatown scale, I've continuously balanced and reflected my lived experiences, transforming them into opportunities for growth, which allowed me to utilize this skill to thrive throughout life.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
"Just hop on the seat, hold tight, and let your hands steadily guide you along the track". Seconds later, the thrill of racing down a narrow path along the Tahoe Rim Trail ended abruptly when I made a crash landing that left me battered up in my hotel room for the rest of the weekend getaway. This happened just about four years ago. And although it was a traumatizing experience that made me reconsider going down steep slopes without absolute confidence, it didn't stop me from biking.

For the record, off-road biking is incredibly challenging, and requires a keen awareness of the environment, speedy reflexes, and a good sense of direction. Unlike the typical bikes that people use as transportation around cities, off-road biking demands a lot more focus and precision because certain trails are unpredictable and even dangerous in mountainous locations. For me, I have developed these skills since my parents first introduced me to the Marin Headlands trail when I was still in middle school. Since then, I spent many weekends traveling with my parents to visit numerous bike trails across California, but by far, the Tahoe Rim Trail is our favorite.

Along these visits, my parents and I have also met an inviting community of avid bikers that are always teaching us something new and showing us some of the best hidden trails around. Often times, I coordinate weekend trips with these seasoned bikers to visit some of the most breathtaking trails, laced with small rivers and creeks and covered in canopy that changes beautifully with the seasons.

Within the last three years, I continue to notice improvements in the way I handle my bike. I owe it to the accessibility of the internet and the generous content of off-road biking videos that teaches me different ways to approach the hurdles that I meet along the road. Now, when I come across challenging obstacles such as steep declines, rapid tides, and heavily vegetated landscapes that make navigation much more intimidating, I know exactly how to avoid dangerous situations like the one that ended my weekend retreat miserably.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Staring down a nearly vertical slope of jagged boulders and thorny shrubs, my will to continue hiking dissipated quickly. Even worse, I dragged along two of my best friends to accompany me on this impulse trip to visit "The Bridge To Nowhere" hidden deep in the San Gabriel mountains. We were clearly unprepared for this hike, and as an experienced hiker that has clocked in hundreds of hiking hours along some of the most challenging hiking courses around California, I should have known better than to carry just a small backpack with saltine crackers and a canister of water.

This hike was immensely difficult but we managed to find our way to the bridge after nearly 7 hours of walking under the beating sun, crossing through waist high rivers, and following a fading trail of asphalt and discontinued train tracks that often led to forked roads. Nonetheless, we had an amazing time socializing along the way, making team efforts to cross the turbulent rivers, and singing our favorite tunes at the top of our lungs. But more importantly, I learned that there is still a lot that I have to learn about hiking, and that my experience can only guide me until the unexpected presents itself. Under most circumstances, I would be able to use the old wooden stick under the sun trick to determine the time of the day, or using the direction of the river flow to approximate the direction that I'm heading towards, but when it came to this hiking trail that tested the limits of my skill in hiking, I would have to argue that luck brought us to the bridge - if the sun had set earlier, we would be in serious trouble.

After this trip, I continued to develop my skill in hiking by regularly going to the gym to keep myself physically fit. I also made it a habit to do online research on hiking trails that I planned to explore, and in the process, discovered many forums that better informed me about hiking routes and equipment that would make my hikes smooth and enjoyable.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
"Good, give me a jab, a short right-hook, and a quick right-uppercut". That's the new combination that I am training to perfect. My boxing coach says that this is the potent combination used by big-name fighters in the boxing and mixed-martial arts industry to win their title fights. At first, I was convinced that this would be easy - I mean, how difficult could it be to learn a three punch combination? But I quickly learned that there was much more to boxing than throwing punches; it involved flexibility, agility, quick reflexes, accuracy, and most importantly, excellent footwork.

Apart from coding, boxing is my greatest skill. Frankly, it's an odd combination of skills, but I have always considered myself to be a boxing enthusiast. I would follow boxing events on social media, watch pay-per-view fights with my friends in college, and attend boxing competitions hosted at the Oracle Arena in Oakland to support my favorite, now-retired fighter, Andre Ward. In fact, I started boxing during my first year of community college because I met Andre Ward at a boxing event where he encouraged me to take boxing lessons as a form of exercise. I took his advice without hesitation, and I am glad I did.

In the past year, I have committed to an intense training program designed to improve my cardiovascular health and to increase the power of my punches. As part of the learning process, I regularly watch my coach perform the combinations and follow exactly as instructed. I always pay attention to the minor details that my coach repeats with every punch, "rotate your arm at the end of the punch, left foot forward, follow through with your hips!". Recently, I have also incorporated a cobra-bag in my training, which helps me to improve my reflexes, timing of punches, and footwork - all of which were skills that I never had from the start.

Over time, I have grown fond of the testosterone-filled atmosphere that keeps me motivated to push myself to my physical limits, and I plan to continue my training beyond college as a lifestyle hobby.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
I've curated the perfect technique to peel an orange.

Start by making a 45-degree incision with a knife near the top. I learned this in February of 2021 when my mom was diagnosed with stage 2 lymphoma in her liver. With this sudden change, I found myself in an unfamiliar place. The bubble I previously lived in, the constant security I found in my parents, had burst. That first cut in the orange marked my first step out of that bubble.

With your thumb, begin to peel the skin off the orange layer by layer. For so long, I had relied on my parents to shoulder much of the familial responsibilities. Now, with their schedules occupied with radiation therapy sessions and endless nights on Google deciphering medical terms, I found myself managing things on my own. The skin of this particular orange was thick, and the new weight of responsibilities was daunting at times; I had to face the reality of this newfound independence. I spent countless nights hovering over a tissue box, feeling isolated, longing for times before the bubble burst. Despite this, I knew there was no choice but to continue peeling. Each layer I peeled revealed a little more of the hidden sweetness, small steps that I was able to take by myself.

Peel the orange into halves, then into slices. Each slice of the orange was like a small victory, and with that, I became more confident with my ability to navigate abrupt situations. One afternoon, as I finished cutting the fruits and washing the dishes, I found myself feeling proud, not because it was flawless, but because I had done it. I no longer depended on my parents to solve things for me. Peeling that orange taught me that independence is not gained in a day—it has to be earned through overcoming discomfort and persevering. While it wasn't easy, once that tougher outer peel was removed, what remained was sweeter and more fulfilling. Shedding my dependence on others, I now embrace independence, letting it seep into every aspect of my life.

Next time, I'll show you the best way to cut an apple.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
I'd always make promises that I don't tend to keep. I tell myself to go study after dinner or practice basketball before it is too late in the day, but I'd always come up with some excuse to not do it. I wanted to change but didn't know how to start. I always think about the person I want to be, but never take the first step towards it. I was frustrated knowing what I wanted but not knowing how to begin.

It slowly began to change as I started to read motivational quotes from famous people. A specific quote by Thomas Edison changed my way of thinking: "Many of life's failures are people who did not realize how close they were to success when they gave up." Reading this only made me realize that I've been giving up on myself too soon on my goals. I decided to start small, like studying for thirty minutes a day, practicing sports for ten. It all seemed too little, but being able to do it every day allowed me to build momentum.

Through sports I was able to find a way to learn discipline and commitment. Every afternoon, I'd go outside to play basketball or football, even when I was tired. I'd often challenge my brother, as a way to push myself. I only tried to be consistent. Over time, I began to see improvements in not only my skill but my mindset. I've learned discipline isn't about perfection, but it's about showing up even when it's hard.

I carried this mindset through school. I stopped waiting until the due dates to complete work and started managing my time better. My grades started to show a slow incline, as well as my confidence. Instead of avoiding challenges, I started to face them as a way to grow.

Getting things done is my best skill that I'm still working on. It has taught me hard work and time will lead to results. I plan to continuously work on this skill as it can help me in not just sports, but school and life.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
"I don't want to live in a world where someone else makes the world a better place better than we do," says the antagonistic voice of Gavin Belson, fictional tech mogul of HBO's beloved show, Silicon Valley. Perhaps it's this leering ambition in natural leaders like Belson that has transformed him into the frontliner of tomorrow's advancements that have inspired so many to follow the same routes and philosophies. He truly is a titan of the tech industry that I look up to.

With an always optimistic attitude and a competitive nature in me, I have spent the last two years reinventing a better future for myself. From my academic performance to my physical and social upkeep, everything had to be faultless. These perfectionistic tendencies have never been a setback, rather a source of drive and progression.

My vigor is the greatest skill I am bringing forward. I have developed a can-do attitude by determination. Same as how our world's chess champions maintain rigorous physical routines and regimens so they could perform well during tournaments, I jog five miles a day and prepare for marathons just to keep my body in a well-enough state. This same determination also sustains my studies and allowed me to achieve competitive grades. Even though it was not a requirement in my past studies to attend in hackathon events nor stream the latest Techcrunch Disrupt, I had always found myself to be in such environments where I could pursue, intuit, and absorb information. In my downtime, I have learned how to code in HTML5, Joomla, CSS, and even basic-level javascript writing.

While I am extremely proud of the work I had put into achieving good grades, I know this will be nothing if I do not have the correct ideologies, therefore I'm continuing trying to learn the moral advocacies of my tech idols as I learn about their achievements. This dedication, adaptability, and natural sense at multitasking without the hiccups are what I believe make me a good candidate for the University of California's Department of Computer Science.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
"One more bowl please".

That line never gets old. I embrace it like my mother would if someone told her she hasn't aged in a decade. For me, my youthful appearance could be better, but my cooking skills are second to none in my household. As if my ancestors from above blessed me with the ability to measure the perfect pinch of seasoning on my kitchen creations, I always found it easy to learn new recipes and add a twist of flavors on my own. That's why "one more bowl please" softly spoken in Cantonese is heard more often than a broken record, especially when I fire up the oven to make my specialty dish: curry chicken wings with roasted carrots and potatoes.

Now, I'm not claiming to be on the same playing field as chef Gordon Ramsay when it comes to the culinary world, but I did learn a lot from watching him on Masterchef where he was nothing short of being a perfectionist and creative genius. It's empowering to watch chefs toss a wok full of food one foot in the air, purposefully blending the flavors and juices into a perfectly crafted dish. After years of learning, starting in high school, I've found the rhythm and motion to toss food around in epic fashion. It really is as impressive as it looks because there were far too many times where the food ejected straight onto the stovetop when the angle or wrist maneuver was off.

More than just the motions of cooking, I've also become quite skilled with the culinary artistry. As I've eaten at a few Michelin restaurants, I learned that visual representation goes hand-in-hand with taste. I prepare every plate like a competition, balancing a symphony of aesthetics, intense flavor profiles, and rich aromas. Even now, I continue to learn and experiment with different herbs, colors, and placement of food, and oftentimes attempt my own unique dishes by clashing flavors of sweet, bitter, salty, rich, and fruity. Cooking is truly a canvas for me to express my skills and creativity. Back to the kitchen I go.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
"Plant your feet firmly on the board, stay balanced, and let your arms guide you along the snow". As easy as that sounded, only seconds after the snowboard instructor released his grip from my jacket, I jetted down the icy slopes of Mammoth Mountain at alarming speeds. I panicked, threw all protocols out the backdoor, and hurled my chest into a guard rail. It knocked the wind out of me for what felt like hours. That's all I remember from this horrible experience three years ago. But apart from the scrapes and bruises, the embarrassment of this Kodak moment, and my sprained elbow, I continued to snowboard.

Snowboarding is a skill that I've developed through persistent training. It isn't an exotic skill like Hawaiian fire juggling or the Cirque du Soleil acrobatics, but it's a skill that is tricky to master. Even just practicing this skill is difficult because it always requires planning ahead and traveling long distances. In the last three years, I've traveled to nearly every snow resort that I could find in California thanks to recommendations from online snowboarding forums. I spent holidays and make weekend trips at these snow resorts with friends and family that share a love for this sport, and along the way, I've met a circle of new friends that have taught me a lot about snowboarding safely while performing cool stunts that I would see in the snowboard X-game competitions on television. These friends are always adventures, always looking for new places for recreational snowboarding, and have helped me improve noticeably.

Since the fiasco at Mammoth Mountain, I've clocked in numerous hours of snowboard training with professional instructors. These training sessions have helped me to adapt to different types of terrain, be it all-mountain, alpine, or powdery slopes, and has grown my confidence. I believe that this self-confidence played a significant role in my development but also the sheer amount of time that I've committed to this activity has sharpened my reflexes, expanded my awareness to the surroundings, and drilled in me an always cautious attitude when going down these slippery slopes.

essays.prompt: What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?
essays.essay:
Standing at five feet tall, I'm already on the shorter side. Combined with inheriting my mother's baby face and my father's lean build, I often appear much younger than I actually am. At the internist's office I came to observe nurses at, I still remember the doctor's confused expression as she questioned if I was the face behind the professional-sounding emails we communicated through. In group projects, it often felt like classmates would talk over me, dismissing my ideas as insignificant. Being treated as if I were a child, even if unintentional, made me doubt myself and my voice.

Over time, I've discovered my greatest skill being my ability to empathize. I've always been one to cry easily while watching a sad movie, or imagine how someone else's pain feels when they've broken a bone. But my sensitivity to how others feel grew most as I learned how it felt to be hurt myself. My experiences gifted me a lens to notice those who go unseen, allowing me to hone my empathy by learning to observe—to read the subtle cues and unspoken dynamics others might miss.

In lab one day, a new student navigating English as her second language was assigned to join our group. As my group members began delegating tasks and gathering supplies, I noticed her lingering on the side, unsure what to do or how to join in. Immediately, all the feelings of being excluded rushed back. With a smile, I invited her to pipette samples with me and tried my best to explain the lab's goal of conducting an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), recognizing the language barrier.

Empathy is a defining component of who I strive to be, but I've learned that its real power lies in how we use it. Applying empathy in my everyday life, even in small ways, allows me to build meaningful bonds with people by understanding them. It's easy to put ourselves first, but true strength lies in putting in the effort to make someone else feel seen, valued, and uplifted, especially when it is most difficult.

essays.promptLabel: How you express your creative side
essays.prompt: Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.
essays.essay:
A cacophony of vexing chirps, whistles, and squawks awoke me from my slumber. This chorus of chirping wonders brought remembrance to my passion: ornithology. A symphony of research, adventure, and curiosity provided my unique bridge, a connection between the matrix of school and the woodlands of nature.

Birdwatching was a relaxing pastime to collect my thoughts and escape the polluted world. I always loved adventure, whether biking through the hills and trails of Coyote Hills or backpacking in the woodlands with my fellow Scouts. But now I had another purpose for going on these adventures–I brought binoculars and a notebook to take notes, draw illustrations, and appreciate mother nature.

Unbeknownst to me, there was an ornithology event at the Science Olympiad, so you can imagine my surprise when I first tried out for my school's team. I just knew I had to partake in this event. I had only been birdwatching for a couple of months before the tryouts, and gathering information on birds from the wild was an arduous process. Many times, new birds would not show face, and their migration patterns were complicated to observe. So I knew I had to do something unique to not only stand out but also to gain more information.

Since each bird species had its unique characteristics, I designed a computer program that used the eBird API and other libraries to scour information from online databases and websites. The cultivation of this data procured a binder that each team is allowed to bring to competitions. Using this binder, my team's interpretation and analytical skills helped us get a podium in the regional competitions in both years that this event took place.

The shiny glint of the sun paralleling that of the medals brought me back to my senses. Sitting now wide awake in Yosemite, away from the world, I can listen unimpeded to the beautiful birds and creatures of nature. My third notebook is open on my lap, binoculars hanging from my neck, and a curious glint in my eye; I continue to feed my passion.

essays.promptLabel: How you prepared for your intended major
essays.prompt: Describe how you have prepared for your intended major (statistics) and what has drawn you to it.
essays.essay:
“I'm planning to study Statistics in college”, I lauded. All I received were blank stares of confusion. My friends, who were all die-hard disciples of engineering, biotech, and computer science, had the likes of Amazon, Google, Apple and Genentech smeared across their foreheads. Hearing my black sheep response was a head-scratcher moment for them. But I knew I was level-headed in my decision. I knew what I wanted and I had a plan for success just like them.

Rewinding back, my passion for statistics was rooted in a popular 1989 Hong Kong film called “God of Gamblers”, starring the legendary Chow Yun-Fat and Andy Lau. As a kid, movie depictions were synonymous with reality, so if actors could do it, so could I. I replayed this film a handful of times, each time amazed with the sheer power of statistics that was used to defeat the casinos. I was fascinated to see the predictive nature of statistics and how it was leveraged to build wealth and notoriety. Of course, this movie and the glorification of mathematics was all scripted. But was it really?

In high school, I came across a documentary on a team of MIT students that used statistics to game the casino, a feat that was once thought impossible. I was once again, fascinated by the complexity of statistics. I want to emphasize that for me, statistics is not intended to help me to become a professional blackjack or poker player. I am just genuinely amazed by statistics for its analytical and predictive abilities. I intend to study statistics to qualify as an analyst or actuary as a future job.

In fact, I've prepared for this major by spending the last two years fine-tuning my skills on RStudio, a program designed for statistical and quantitative analysis on large scale data sourced from the internet. As a personal project, I've also compiled data from the New York Stock Exchange to examine the probability of various market patterns and posted my findings on a personal blog. The combination of both experiences gives me confidence in succeeding in upper division courses.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time. (Standard UC PIQ prompt; inferred from content, not printed in the document.)
essays.essay:
“Yes. He dropped black paint all over his sister then peed himself.” How in the world could a 7 year old cause so much chaos in a summer art program week 1, were my first thoughts entering the summer art program’s building for the second time this week. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t terrified of what this could do once the lead teacher assigned me to stick with him the whole day. I was warned the other volunteers could not control this beast, meaning I was left to put on my big boy pants and finally end this kid’s reign.

As the week progressed, problems arised and I quickly faced these problems. I didn’t understand how to act around this boy since he was a special case, he just did not sit still. Paint was constantly spilled around his desk and he would run up and down the hallways looking to pick on other kids. At first, I assumed this kid was just doing these things out of pure enjoyment. However, the more I followed him around and gently reminded him to focus on his artwork, I realized he had a deeper story than what was presented.

I connected with him deeper than I did with the other students throughout the program. He did not receive attention from his parents, he was neglected. The reality dawned on me, and I spent the rest of my shifts sitting by him and talking to him about pokemon. At the end of the week, he finished all of his projects and went home with an icecream bar.

I didn’t know it was possible to connect with someone much younger than me about something so complicated. Though patience was always built into my skill set, I truly harnessed those same skills to a new degree. By nurturing him, I understood the true definition of patience. It comes with practice, if I had never been exposed to such a situation, I would lack more skill than what I could have. He may not have changed, maybe he did, but he helped me grow.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Last September, I attended XSCI Design Hacks in Silicon Valley, which is a competitive event where software developers and computer engineers collaborate for several days in an effort to create the most innovative computer technologies to help companies resolve existing problems in the real world. At this event, I had the chance to learn from a diverse community of bright minds and engaged with experts in artificial intelligence, computer forensics, and data scientists to name a few. I felt that this was the moment where I could put my coding skills to the test, and despite having only four years of coding experience, I was confident in my abilities to win the $15,000 grand prize for my team.

The event started off in a haste and the chattering of ideas in the auditorium took shape in the form of a competitive environment. I could see the frantic efforts of my team through the illegible notes and rough outlines jotted onto the provided scrap of paper. I, on the other hand, remained calm and collect. I felt good about this project because the task involved integrating virtual reality technology into a software used by an architectural design company and doing so in the C++ programming language - both of which I was competent. Still, I was initially hesitant to voice my suggestions in front of a group of strangers that were probably far more experience and than I. But eventually, I mustered up my confidence and proposed my idea of developing a versatile virtual reality software that is compatible on multiple devices, user-friendly, and efficient for data transferring which resolve many real-world challenges for the architectural design company.

Unfortunately, we placed far below our expectations, but I was content. My team was very receptive of my ideas, and likewise, I kept and open mind about revising my plan with the aid of my team members. I led most of the discussion during this event, asked challenging questions that prompted creative responses, drew schematics to help my team better visualize the end goal, and most importantly, exercised my leadership skills effectively in the process.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
When I became an officer at a youth marketing nonprofit, the organization was positioned for a major change. We moved beyond social media development for small businesses and chased a grander vision of hosting business showcases to promote local businesses to the community. Our first showcase was in my area, where as the Technology Officer, I was responsible for the event's entire technical setup, including sound systems, staging, and power solutions. These technology needs accounted for a large portion of the budget, but were crucial for an engaging experience.

Everything went well until two weeks before the event when our venue withdrew their agreement because they didn't want high school students hosting an event this large. We had to adapt and find a substitute location. When the team struggled to find another venue, I volunteered to take responsibility for this effort. I led the team to contact all the parks and recreation centers near us, cold emailed countless government officials and developed a pitch for the event.

After a few days of silence, one official responded back to our surprise and let us rent a venue that was slightly out of our price range, but we accepted out of desperation. This meant my job wasn't done. I had to reevaluate our technology budget and find ways to cut corners where possible, all while ensuring that the experience would be perfect for our businesses and attendees. I rearranged the vendor tents close to the outlets to save us cords, and replaced a few auditory equipment that were more budget friendly. With late nights, and full collaboration from all the officers, we had everything ready just in time.

The event went much better than expected with businesses bringing in profit and getting their names out there. We also had over 100 attendees despite the last minute switch and this is a reflection of the great communication that my team and I put together to notify businesses in a timely manner. I'm proud to say that I helped make our first business showcase a success.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
In the midst of an internship, sitting 7,000 miles away from home, duty called from my phone at 1:30am. It came in a slew of concerning emails and calls that kept me up through the night. I was frantic as one of my coaches had just left for Texas for two weeks without notifying me, leaving 19 lessons unattended.

As president of Impactful Tennis, I knew it was my responsibility to make sure we continued donating to local charities. Even though I was in Turkey for my internship at Ernst and Young, I acted quickly to resolve this issue.

Rightfully, a few parents demanded reimbursement and an explanation for this abrupt, unprecedented change. But before I did anything else, I immediately blocked off the absent coach's calendar to prevent any more sign-ups.

Afterwards, I called each parent scheduled within the next three days to apologize for any inconvenience. I offered substitute coaches to cover the class, spending hours analyzing overlapping coach schedules to find suitable replacements. For all other lessons, I sent a personalized apology email addressing the issue with honesty – as an organization, we had to own up to our shortcomings. Still, some of the parents weren't fully satisfied, so I offered my own time to coach missing lessons at no charge once I was back home. Fortunately, this proved enough to show our organization's determination to make things right.

Yet this only solved half the issue; now it was time to make organizational changes to learn from our mistake. I sent a spreadsheet of direct contact information for our 17 coaches to the parents, drafted a timesheet to hold everyone accountable to their commitments, and added protocols to manage unexpected schedule changes. I even standardized the process of courtesy calls to coaches one day ahead of their lessons, ensuring everyone was aligned.

Thankfully, the issue subsided and we were able to protect the good reputation of Impactful Tennis. I'm grateful for this experience, because it taught me that leadership is not always straightforward. Now I could finally go to sleep, a little stronger and ready to lead.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
I gained a basic understanding of how a team operates thanks to my experience as captain of my eighth-grade softball team, but slipping into cheer shoes in high school revealed a new rhythm that taught me how a team doesn't just work together, it moves together.

At the age of eight, I competed in gymnastics until sixth grade. My experience in tumbling helped me earn a spot as co-captain of the cheer team towards the end of my freshman year. Although I've never done cheerleading before, I understood how leadership worked and how a team runs by observing my captains in action. I began prioritizing personal connections among the team to help my players bond and stay synced during our performances.

But high school cheerleading often comes with the reputation of constant drama, and unfortunately, this affected my team. When my captains graduated, I became head captain in my sophomore year. I discovered that the freshmen cliques within the team harbored underlying drama from middle school that was never resolved, which led to them bossing each other around. Unfortunately, I discovered this issue the day of our school rally performance, which poorly reflected our coordination and preparation.

Instead of stepping back, I stepped up. I became a big sister to my cheer sisters. In the weeks leading up to our next rally, I introduced restorative practices and team-bonding activities to rebuild trust. I held restorative circles where everyone shared their feelings while listening to each other's side of the story. I also crafted a "speed-dating" stunting activity designed to pair teammates who rarely interacted with each other, pushing them to collaborate in new ways. When the next school rally came, we left a jaw-dropping performance that prompted the students to give a standing ovation.

"Thank you for not giving up on us," my team said, loudly in unison.

What started as cliques evolved into a close family. In guiding my cheer sisters through conflict, I learned that leadership isn't about authority but rather modeling patience to encourage others to do the same, which I will continue to uphold in life.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
When I think about examples of leadership, two familiar faces cross my mind: Martin Luther King Jr. and Steve Jobs - the former, an admirable civil rights activist that led peaceful protests against racial discrimination, and the latter, a visionary that led a team of brilliant engineers to create one of the most successful companies in modern history. That said, replicating their exceptional display of leadership is unrealistic for most.

However, at my community college, I had the chance to exercise my leadership on a smaller scale. Leading even a small group can be painfully challenging especially when a common goal is not defined, which often leads to tension among group members. However, it is in these uncomfortable moments that I am truly able to test my capacity to lead.

Among all the group projects that I've participated in, one stood out the most. It was a research project aiming to study Google's marketing technology. Everyone in the group had a similar idea of what they wanted to do - the one that required the least amount of work. On top of that, there were disagreements about the format, images, and background of the presentation slides. Three days had gone by and everyone did their own research. There was not a hint of team effort because everyone had an excuse not to meet in person to finish the project. Out of pure desperation, I finally decided on a solution: I suggested that everyone should create a small presentation of what they wanted to include, and at the end, I would stitch and refine the presentation into one finished product. Needless to say, the project was far from perfect - it was more of a collage.

In hindsight, I saw this as a form of leadership. Although I failed to take full control of my group members and could not arrange a collective meetup to finish the project together, I took the best route to help everyone accomplish the task to some extent. To me, an effective leader must be able to consider alternative solutions to meet a goal, and that's exactly what I did.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Over the last decade, much of the video game experience has changed for the better. With the integration of mobile gaming, improvements in graphics, and a wider genre of games, video games have become the center for entertainment for most children and adults. Yet, one thing has remained the same: the players are always arguing about something trivial.

For me, this type of negativity is off-putting; it defeats the purpose of a game, which is to have fun. As an always optimistic player that is able to control my emotions under even the worst circumstances, I often find myself being in the position of a leader. By leader, I mean the person that mitigates tension among players and help guide my team to victory.

Take League of Legends for example - a popular multiplayer game where there are various objectives and positions designated to each player. In every matchup, I find myself trapped between players arguing about what resources to collect first or which direction the team should go. In the event where someone intentionally dies or quits the game, almost everyone on the team would engage in an all-out verbal warfare. Needless to say, this type of gaming environment is distasteful and someone level-headed is needed to intervene - that's usually when I step in.

As I have mediated these types of situations countless times before, my leadership experience is plentiful at this point. For me, I find that explaining the roles to each player prior to the game is essential to establish order. Throughout the games, I maintain an active presence in the chat - constantly praising my teammates for the smallest achievements and reassuring them that teamwork is all we need to win. By positively reinforcing the idea of teamwork even under the worst scenarios in the game, I find that I gain respect as a player, which ultimately leads to people listening to my advice and lessening the odds of an argument. In fact, I even earned an "honorable player" badge for my positivity and support of my teammates and that is something I am extremely proud of.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time. (UC PIQ #1; prompt not stated verbatim, standard phrasing)
essays.essay:
The defense was collapsing on me, closing in fast. I knew I had seconds to make the throw. I was in the middle of Wednesday afternoon flag football practice, and as quarterback, the only thought running through my mind was how the entire play relied on this pass. Much to my dismay, the ball sailed past my teammate and straight into the ground. Sighing, we all got back into our positions with minimal exchanging of words.

"You guys are playing for yourselves," my coach said, clear frustration in his tone.

Taking a deep breath, I replayed the countless times we had run the play. It wasn't just about my throw, nor dependent on how well positioned the receiver was. It was about communication–starting with the call and ending with the catch. I realized that as a quarterback, it did not matter how solid my throw was if the receiver was not there to catch it, and vice versa. Being aware of my surroundings and being able to quickly adapt were key, but so was the trust and reliance I put in my teammates.

Right before the next play, I gathered our offensive team together and locked eyes with everyone, ensuring a shared understanding of each of our roles. It was a small, but powerful shift. We were all on the same page, and because of that, everyone was in the right place. My receiver caught the ball, gaining a considerable amount of yards. Continuing the momentum, on the next play, I recognized the shift in defensive position, advising my teammates to shift in response to the defense, should the play not go according to plan. Instead of throwing it, I handed it off to my running back, trusting she would bring it to the end zone.

Though the changes were subtle, the overall outcome was momentous. By learning to build a shared understanding prior to a play, my team was able to play with a level of harmonization, something that I did not just apply on the field, but outside of it, encouraging communication and fostering connection in those around me.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
I've grown into a leadership role I never thought I'd be. I'm the translator for my family. Whenever we go out, whether it's shopping, ordering food, running errands, or talking to neighbors, I'm always the one who is there to help my parents and relatives understand what's going on. At home, I'm translating bills, letters, and other documents. I take this role seriously because they rely on me to guide them through a world where they don't speak the language.

When I was just starting to translate, I didn't understand the value of translating but as I grew older I realized how important it is. I had to explain insurance forms, or medical instructions, even when I wasn't completely sure on how to translate. Whenever I come across a road block, like whenever I have to go to the doctors with them, there are words I don't know how to translate, but I started to use Google Translate to allow me to see how it's said in Chinese, but I would make it simpler so it's easier for my parents to understand. Even though I've faced many challenges, one moment still stands out in my memory.

One of the hardest situations I've faced was when a relative accidentally hit our neighbor's car when backing up. Both sides were equally upset and yelling at one another, and it started to get out of hand. I stopped whatever I was doing, and came outside to help translate between them. I didn't just repeat what each person said but I made sure to speak in a respectful and calm tone so both sides can understand each other. Eventually, they reached an agreement and apologized. That moment showed me that leadership isn't always about being in charge, sometimes it's about creating peace, finding a common ground.

Being the family's translator has taught me how to lead with compassion, responsibility, and composure. I've also learned to be more patient, thoughtful, and clear with my words even when things start to get rough. Through my experiences of translating it has allowed me to grow confidence. What has come upon me is that leadership isn't always having the loudest voice but it's really about helping others be heard. I will carry this with me throughout my lifetime.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
I absolutely love traveling. My parents have always told me that my wanderlust began at a young age as I explored the world through the pages of Nature magazine and Trailer Life. This desire expresses itself through the many backpacking trips I've had at the Grand Canyon National Park and countless weekend trips to Lake Tahoe's Emerald Bay. Of course, my desires are mostly limited to these close-by destinations because the level-minded part of me tells me that I have to save for the future.

Perhaps my love for traveling is also complemented by the leader in me. I always take it upon myself to act as a "tour guide pro tem" - a nickname given to me by my uncle because of how I thoroughly study the destinations beforehand. I have a penchant to figure out an entire travel schedule down to the hour to remove spontaneity out of the equation. This habit, for better or for worse, has earned me the title as a leader when it comes to traveling with friends and families.

A particularly memorable trip that I had two summers ago was in Canada. I set up the entire trip from end to end - visiting Capilano Suspension Bridge around a perfect orange sunset, then a small Koreatown filled with hidden delicacies, followed by riding a ferry to Granville Island on a foggy morning to experience the local markets and local art galleries, and topped off with a visit around my personal favorite Chinatown for the picture-worthy scenery. It's safe to say, this experience was unforgettable.

Of course, plans are often riddled with unexpected. I am no stranger to these scenarios, and I do the best that I can to adapt. In such moments, my leadership qualities are unwavered - rather, I try to use my intuit to solve problems. It's easy to become rattled in these situations, but time and time again when baggage are lost, hotel check-in reservations are unfound, or the weather takes a sharp turn, I always have a backup plan. That is what I feel makes me a great leader.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Sorting through the activities that I invest my time into since starting college, I could recall specific moments where my leadership qualities were demonstrated and proven to be useful. Be it the time that I encouraged my friend to train for a marathon instead of going on a fasting diet to lose weight or the many weekend family getaways where I take the lead in deciding the destination, places to eat, hotels to stay in, and attractions to visit - neither would compare to the challenge of leading a dance group that I formed in college.

The background story is that when I began college in America, I met a group of friends that were passionate dancers like myself. I instantly felt connected through this similar interest, and over time, joined them in using empty school corridors as a dance floor. We continued to make use of the space at school for dancing until we decided to use fitness centers and dancing studios by each chipping in some money. There, we choreographed routines that gained a lot of praise when it was filmed and uploaded to our growing YouTube channel.

Although I certainly am not the most talented in the group, I became somewhat of a de facto leader by taking charge of the pace, choreography of solo parts, and keeping everyone synchronized. The reality is that in these off-hours environments after class and the competitive nature of dancers, there are moments where I have to diffuse petty arguments over menial disagreements like the genre of music, the position of each person, accidental clashing in practice, and just plain gossip. I always have to remind my friends that there is a time and place for arguments, and in circumstances where we are able to meet only once or twice a week, it should be a moment of appreciation and bonding.

I believe that at the University of California, I will have the opportunity to demonstrate my leadership skills, especially at the upper-division course levels where my work ethic will play a significant role in guiding others to work efficiently and effectively.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Outside of school, I am a wilderness lover, an adventure seeker, and a great camp buddy. I love traveling to places with rugged terrain, where trails fork like wires on a cable; or places that have no electricity or cellphone reception, where being tactical, resourceful, and creative is essential; or places that I can simply set up a hammock, where I can enjoy a nice book, dripped coffee, and the ambience of nature. Just writing this bit gives me the urge to plan for my next trip.

But the glory of exploring, sight-seeing, and camping out wouldn't be the same without company. I love traveling with friends. Be it a short road trip to Bagby Hotsprings in Oregon (a personal favorite) or a weekender at the Sequoia Campgrounds in Boulder Creek, I fully relish these opportunities to build close friendships. To my friends, I'm always the leader in the group when we're out and about, but I jokingly call myself the "tour guide" because I'm always there to give everyone a great taste of the outdoors.

A memorable leadership experience was when my friends and I traveled down to the Merced River last summer. Before departing, I sent out a group message with a detailed list of essential items to pack: sunscreen, water, insect-repellant, disposable waste bags, a cooler of food, and matchboxes. I mapped out a few checkpoint points for water rafting, fishing, and sunbathing, and designated a rendezvous in case anyone separated from the group. Once there, I helped with setting up tents in a safe spot away from the river currents which I knew would swell up during the night. I showed my friends how to set up a fishing reel, how to tie knots on a bait, how to use a Bunsen burner, and how to construct a wooden barbeque skewer to toast s'mores, marinated beef, and bacon. Everyone had a blast and it was incredibly satisfying to introduce the campsite to friends who were joining along for the first time - as if I was reliving my first experience at the Merced River through their eyes.
