essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
"Who wants to sit in the front seat?"

My hands sprung up like a suppressed coil. It was the question heard around the world. The forbidden question that my teacher asked that led to a dramatic outcry of elementary school kids competing to sit at the front of the roller coaster.

I didn't get to sit in the front. I swear, my hands reached the invisible horizon of hand-raising first, but still, I wasn't selected. It felt unfair. I wanted to be the "leader". I wanted to be the front of the whole pack. It ruined my field trip and I sat in frustration on the bus trip back.

It's funny how time flies. This memory, although a bit fuzzy like old film casted on a projector, is a reference point to a time when I didn't understand what leadership meant. Over the years, my mentality has changed, and it happened on none other than the volleyball court.

By the time I reached high school, volleyball was the one sport I excelled in. I practiced, played, and formed meaningful relationships on and off the courts. With each game, each win or loss, I've grown further from the little girl that yearned to sit in the front seat. I've come to see that a leader isn't about being the best point scorer; it isn't about jumping the highest; it's not even about winning or losing. What being a leader means to me is making sure everyone is engaged; it means supporting others that are falling behind; it means passing the ball and having faith that every person is just as good.

The leader that I am today will make my future self proud. Putting my fiercely competitive spirit aside, I always make an effort to uplift my friends on and off the courts. I try to turn their bad days to good ones and good days to better ones. I do this by communicating, by setting up the perfect shot for others to drive home the point, and by always listening and observing others. Cheers to myself, I'm all grown up.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
"Yes. He dropped black paint all over his sister then peed himself." How in the world could a 7 year old cause so much chaos in a summer art program week 1, were my first thoughts entering the art academy building for the second time this week. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't terrified of what this could do once the lead teacher assigned me to stick with him the whole day. I was warned the other volunteers could not control this beast, meaning I was left to put on my big boy pants and finally end this kid's reign.

As the week progressed, problems arised and I quickly faced these problems. I didn't understand how to act around this boy since he was a special case, he just did not sit still. Paint was constantly spilled around his desk and he would run up and down the hallways looking to pick on other kids. At first, I assumed this kid was just doing these things out of pure enjoyment. However, the more I followed him around and gently reminded him to focus on his artwork, I realized he had a deeper story than what was presented.

I connected with him deeper than I did with the other students throughout the program. He did not receive attention from his parents, he was neglected. The reality dawned on me, and I spent the rest of my shifts sitting by him and talking to him about Pokemon. At the end of the week, he finished all of his projects and went home with an ice cream bar.

I didn't know it was possible to connect with someone much younger than me about something so complicated. Though patience was always built into my skill set, I truly harnessed those same skills to a new degree. By nurturing him, I understood the true definition of patience. It comes with practice, if I had never been exposed to such a situation, I would lack more skill than what I could have. He may not have changed, maybe he did, but he helped me grow.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
When I think about examples of leadership, two faces appear in my mind: Bill Gates and Albert Einstein - the former, a genius technologist and philanthropist that built a trillion dollar software empire, and the latter, arguably one of the greatest physicist that revolutionized human understanding of the universe through his theories on relativity. These incredible displays of leadership are far beyond my reach, but I strive to be a better leader when opportunities arise.

At my community college, I found opportunities to develop my leadership skills through collaborative projects. At times, I became flustered by the looming deadlines, the absent team members, and the unfinished responsibilities. It was difficult for me to comprehend how some of my peers could approach these projects with such nonchalance, but I was not going to let my group fall apart like they often do in high school. In these moments, my desire to lead was provoked, and so I did.

Of all the group projects that I've encountered, there was one project that was exceptionally challenging to complete. It was a research study on Netflix's business model that involved a lot of data analysis. It was time consuming and nobody in my group was enthusiastic about it - myself included. Early in the project, we had major hiccups. Some group members couldn't meet due to work, others had to take care of their siblings, and I was left stranded in the group messages that often went silent for days. We struggled a lot due to the sheer amount of work involved, but I was determined to do well on this project. To get the job done, I met with each group member, provided a list of resources that I collected in advance, and regularly updated everyone about the progress of the paper through emails and text messages. It was far from a perfect operation, but I managed to get an assembly line running.

In the end, the project was properly executed. I was an effective leader in this situation because I didn't give up on my team, looked for alternative solutions, and got the job done.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
"Sit Rico. Sit down! Why can't you just sit?" I lamented. My 3-month old puppy just sat silently as he stared into my fuming eyes with a confused expression. What started out as an exciting day at the dog park quickly turned into a miserable afternoon of scolding because Rico refused to perform his trick.

Being a leader is tough. I've had my fair share of experiences trying to lead study groups that evolve into a chattering session about sports cars and electronic dance music. But when it comes to leading my puppy, it's an entirely different playing field. For one, Rico cannot speak or presumably understand English - he relies purely on his tail and the occasional whining for communication. Another challenge is that he has a mind of his own when he is outside of the home - he wanders around, sniffing for different scents, and does his business where he finds comfortable. These two things alone have presented challenges that I have to work around as a leader.

In the past year of training Rico, I have become a more effective leader, and I can see a remarkable difference in the way that I interact with my peers. Admittedly, there were many tiring and irritable days that discouraged me from putting my time and effort into the training, but I persevered. Somewhere along this process, I gradually developed the qualities of patience and sensibility as I have come to realize that puppies, and dogs alike, are not humans. They have their unique tendencies, needs, and require time and nurturing to learn. Moreover, to be an effective leader to Rico, I needed to find compromises, and usually that meant rewarding him with a treat or taking him out for a jog every time he cooperated with me.

While it may seem odd at first, I owe my leadership skill to Rico. Understandably, leading a dog is not the same as leading a person or a group, but in training Rico, I have become a more patient, sympathetic, and encouraging individual which I believe are essential qualities of an effective leader.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Building a shed of any sort is not easy work. Neither is planning and leading the start-to-finish process of creating this shed. Having no prior experience certainly does not help in the task's difficulty. Despite knowing that, wanting to stand out, I chose a significant woodworking project for my eagle project, something so large it would cost upwards of 700 dollars.

I created multiple blueprints and went to Dale's Hardware to acquire knowledge and feedback from experienced woodworkers. I also went to Cresco and Lowes to secure a full discount on all tools used for the project and a 20% discount on all materials bought for the project, respectively.

The actual project started, however, once the planning was finished and we were diving into the workdays for the real labor-intensive work. This was problematic since I was recommended not to work on the building process. So, how was I supposed to lead these inexperienced volunteers by example? I organized workdays, assigned tasks based on individual strengths, and fostered a collaborative atmosphere among the young, inexperienced volunteers. By actively encouraging communication, sharing ideas, and providing guidance, I ensured that each team member felt valued and motivated to contribute their best efforts.

As I look back and journal aspects of the project I could have improved on, I realize the overlying impact of the project. I had undertaken something which only a few young people had yet done, and I gave them the necessary introductions to learn and implement skills they may use. These skills are not simply working with hammers, power tools, and cement but also those of teamwork, following directions, and problem-solving.

This transformative journey for everyone involved was a glimpse into the real world. Only sometimes will we be faced with problems that we instantly know or even understand; instead, we will work as a team to solve such problems. Becoming a leader helped me build a shed. More importantly, it helped me build connections and interests in people. The sweat and tears led to the ceremonious placing of the shiny Eagle Rank Emblem on my chest.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
Leadership is a quality that I value. For me, leadership amounts to the ability to speak comfortably in front of an audience and to be able to make calculated decisions for the benefit of others - but more importantly, I believe that leadership involves compassion, responsibility, and an infectious aura of positivity. These are the qualities that I continue to strive towards while studying in community college.

Apart from my experience in leading group projects and coordinating study groups, lending a hand to my peers during the college application process is by far the most stressful task that demonstrated my ability to lead and help others.

Throughout the last two years, I've prepared to transfer into a UC. My aspiration is to learn everything there is to know about business and connect with a community of like-minded peers that would hopefully motivate me through competition and cooperation. That being said, I spent a significant amount of time researching nearly every crevice of the admission process hoping for the secret formula for admission. My attempts to unravel the mystery behind acceptance yielded nothing surprising other than the old adage of "do your best and you will succeed".

Still, my research served a great purpose when I met a small group of friends that were also interested in the transfer opportunity. Within this group, I gained a sense of leadership and promoted a very proactive and goal-oriented environment for everyone. I often encouraged my friends to participate in outdoor activities such as social bonding experiences and organized a trip to attend a business exposition to learn more about start up businesses and financial management.

More recently, I created a comprehensive transfer guide for myself and my friends. It's a Google document that contains all the websites, events, financial aid information, and deadlines for transfer students. I even created a handy pivot table that can filter over 50 universities based on major selection, cost, acceptance rates, GPA range, and location. I am proud to say that my contribution to my groups has been tremendous and I will continue to help others along the way.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
As I opened my Scout book and read the requirements to become an Eagle Scout, my heart raced with excitement. This was my dream. Little did I know that the final step, the Eagle Scout Project, would become a transformative journey, showcasing a Boy Scout's leadership abilities through a community-benefitting project.

Eager to begin, I downloaded the workbook, contacted beneficiaries, and selected my project: building nine wooden pedestals for a local museum and nursery. I immediately designed structures, created a fundraiser, and sent out volunteer forms. Having completed these tasks, I held an optimistic view of a swift completion.

My perspective changed after the result of the first workday. It was chaotic, with tasks being done incorrectly and inefficiently, leaving me in a state of panic as I did not know how to prevent this disaster. Realizing my initial oversight, I reread the project requirements and discovered its true purpose: "Give leadership to others." It was evident that the project had a more significant purpose, requiring me to lead the scouts and guide them through the process.

In the following workday, I embraced my role as a leader. I delegated tasks to scouts and employed the EDGE method taught to me in Boy Scouts, which helps others learn skills efficiently. I thoroughly answered any questions and made the scouts feel a part of the team. I remained calm and carefully planned out all the steps. As a result of this new system, the workday progressed smoothly, and this trend carried on to the proceeding workdays.

The success from this project highlighted my growth as a leader and demonstrated the impact that outstanding leadership can have on a team. Looking back, I realized that the project's primary purpose was to foster leadership skills in a scout. A leader's goal is to inspire passion and motivate others. These invaluable lessons taught to me by the Eagle Scout project have given me essential skills that can be used beyond scouting. I am confident that a leadership role awaits me in the future, and this project's lessons will help me to successfully fulfill that role.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes, or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
In addition to my work as a member of certain neuroscience clubs in high school as mentioned above, where my communication and leadership skills have been tested, I have also put in some good work doing community service. Namely, this was in a Veterans Affairs hospital in the summer of 2018 and a local hospital, from September 2017 up to date.

Spending time doing community service has taught me a lot about how to exercise forming ideas with a group of people on how to do our work efficiently, and how to command those around me while being empathic to everyone's schedules and mindset. At the local hospital, I am an active volunteer for three departments, which are the Medical/Surgical/Orthopedic department, the Emergency department, and Rehabilitation. My duties include helping out nurses with transport of laboratory specimen, attending to patient calls, handling nurse requests, and comforting family members. I have learned that it had never been easy for the hospital staff to actually break bad news to the patients whose health progressed into more challenging situations, and how it is inefficient (and sometimes unethical) to blankly promise actually curing people from certain diseases or guaranteeing a speedy recovery.

The holdover communication and organizational skills I have acquired in my youth (humbly honored a Girl Scouts Ambassador and National Merit Commended Student) have been focal to my experience. There had been a number of high-tense and urgent scenarios that had been thrown around in the day-to-days which really tested out everybody's patience and ability to stay calm, which is to be expected from every staff member but not quite mastered yet by young people such as myself. Whenever I found myself in the middle of brewing arguments with my co-volunteers, I have always tried to take steps into deescalating the tension, pulling aside those who are close to my age and sometimes giving them pep talks. I constantly try to remind myself and others about the good we do, and how we are investing not just into our future but in the general well-being of the patients.

essays.prompt: Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.
essays.essay:
I opened my phone to read the news: "Due to COVID-19, no activities may be held in-person." As my Boy Scout troop's Senior Patrol Leader (SPL), uncertainty clouded my mind. I wondered how I was going to lead my Boy Scout troop as SPL. I admired the older scouts' leadership as SPL in the past, but now I couldn't follow their path. Despite the setback, a spark of determination ignited within me. I stumbled on Zoom and I realized that it held the key to reviving our troop. Leading my troop through these uncharted waters became my mission.

As the SPL, I had the privilege of guiding and supporting the scouts who held important leadership roles within the troop, known as Positions of Responsibility (POR). Adapting each POR's role to match the virtual environment required resourcefulness and quick thinking. I created a Google Drive to document their progress and delegated tasks to help ease the troop into the new setting. For instance, the instructors would create presentations each week for the scouts to learn at the meeting.

Due to our troop's large size, it was split into six patrols, with each patrol consisting of six to eight scouts and a patrol leader. In order to maintain the patrol method and ensure that each scout was able to complete their requirements to rank up, I utilized Zoom's breakout rooms feature. The scouts were able to bond, advance in rank, and learn new skills. The online meetings became a beacon of hope in the darkness caused by the pandemic. Watching the scouts progressing filled me with joy. I was determined to ensure that each scout experienced the beauty of scouting as I had in my earlier years. Furthering our online journey, I organized virtual campouts and service projects, allowing scouts to achieve their camping requirements and contribute to the community.

My role as SPL taught me many lessons in leadership. Embracing the change taught me adaptability and resilience. As a leader, I realized the importance of guaranteeing that every scout felt connected and valued. Our troop's swift transition to the virtual setting was a testament to the unbreakable spirit of scouting. Guiding my troop through uncharted waters helped me realize that leadership transcends physical boundaries. Leadership is the ability to unite, inspire, and navigate the way for others to follow.

essays.essay:
Blogging is one of my favorite hobbies, and Reddit became the perfect environment for just that. Being part of the Reddit community has a cool factor that is hard to describe - like the feeling of being part of an exclusive club.

When I joined Reddit in high school, I quickly learned about the perks that this community provided. It became my portal for endless entertainment, a temporary paradise away from productivity, and a space for me to exercise my creativity and display my comedic abilities. Over the years, Reddit has evolved, and so did I. From a social forum that posted videos of impossible stunts and funny voice overs of politicians, Reddit expanded into the ultimate handbook for success and problem solving.

For me, Reddit became a space for me to develop an audience and a place for me to share my knowledge. In a short amount of time, I gained a lot of attention for my expertise in fixing software issues on the iPhone and was given credit for helping someone resolve a persistent hardware issue on their laptop.

Of course, I had more to offer than just electronics related advice. Often times, I would share my stories of dealing with cyberbullying for people that express concerns about the mental impact that bullying has had on them; it is these genuine exchanges that make Reddit such a tightly-knit community that I am proud to be a part of.

More recently, I provided advice to senior high school students that were inquiring about the community college transfer process. I shared with them my experience as a prospective transfer student, the challenges that I have encountered, the time management skills that I had to develop, and the process of selecting the right courses to fulfill the transfer conditions.

Reflecting on my contributions to the Reddit community - both small and large - I have learned to appreciate the delicate process of communication. I am beginning to realize the impact that I can have on others through a couple taps on my keyboard - and that is such an inspiring thought.

essays.promptLabel: Making community a better place (community garden)
essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
I was 10 years old when the last farm in our city closed down. To my young mind, this simply meant that I could no longer bike around the farm and look at sunflowers, or buy corn from the stand nearby. Five years later, however, I decided to make a change.

Through volunteering at my local senior center, I was entrusted with the task of tending to their community garden thanks to my experience gardening at home. While harvesting mint one day, I noticed we had far more than the kitchen would need. So, I dug up the extra plants and put them in pots. I then set up a stand outside of the senior center with about 100 potted mint plants and a sign that said "Please take one!"

Curious residents, visiting families, and staff members alike stopped to see what my stand was. As people asked questions, I walked them through the basics of mint care, and each person happily left with their own plant. As the day went by, each plant found a new home until there were none left.

My stand became a weekly event where I'd share different plants—from basil to cherry tomatoes and sometimes even flowers—as our senior center community grew more passionate about gardening. Soon, I began teaching different gardening techniques, and my small stand had evolved into people actively helping out in the garden. Many of my "students" would show me pictures of their home gardens, or dishes they made using herbs they grew themselves, and every time I smiled, cherishing how each person discovered, just as I had, the joy of growing their own food.

Watching these small gardens multiply throughout our neighborhood showed me something larger: sustainable urban farming is crucial to feeding local people and to mitigating climate change. Even though our city lost a beloved farm that brought joy to many, watching our community members grow their own plants at home has brought some life back to our community, nurturing both our responsibility to the environment around us and our connections with each other.

essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
I am fortunate to be part of a supportive college community and a Chinese community that shares my language and cultural background, but I find that my role is most defined within the YouTube community.

The YouTube community is enormous. While I do not personally know everyone in this community, I know it is home to one of the most diverse, intelligent, creative, and quirky peoples from all type of ethnic, religious, and professional backgrounds. Specifically, there are two types of people within this large community: content creators and the audience. Content creators produce all types of videos ranging from vlogs, cooking tutorials, education, movie reviews, among many, while the audience simply enjoy the content and show their support or concerns through the comments section.

For me, I am a content creator. I make educational videos specifically on the subject of economics. Initially, I got this idea from a friend that talked about a professor uploading lengthy lectures on YouTube to teach students about biology. This gave me the idea that I could do the same with economics.

Making YouTube videos is hard work. It takes several hours to record a lesson and additional hours to edit the video to include sound effects and graphics, but I enjoy this process because I know it helps students to learn the concepts and ace their exams. I know this because some of my YouTube followers take the time out of their day to let me know that my videos are helpful.

Over the last four years of uploading content on YouTube, I have over 40 videos that I am very proud of. And while my YouTube following is only in the double-digits, compared to other educational channels like Crash Course that have 8.5 million subscribers, I remain optimistic that I have the privilege to extend my help to my small community of followers.

Moving forward at university, I hope to be able to expand my presence on YouTube by taking on a wider range of subjects and inspire others to do the same.

essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
One afternoon I walked into the library, as I walked in I saw leftover lunches on tables littered everywhere. There was a rule about eating in the library: "if you eat in the library, you must clean up after yourself", but some students tend to ignore it. I spent most of my free time in the library because it was relaxing and quiet without distractions. After seeing it messy, I decided I would help clean it if given the opportunity.

Weeks go by, I've noticed flyers going around asking for volunteers at the library. Without hesitation, I took my phone out and scanned the QR code to sign up. I was the first one to arrive so I asked if I could get a head start cleaning. The job was easy but important. It was to wipe down tables, clean shelves, reorganize them alphabetically, and pick up any trash. I was paired up with two other volunteers that arrived late and we quickly got to work. This was my first time volunteering here, but being able to work as a team made it more efficient and fun.

Over time, we could see changes in the library, as it remained clean for a longer period of time, and see students throw their trash away. The library clean up became a monthly event. It was nice knowing that I was a part of something small that was able to help shape a better environment for everyone who shares this place.

Through this experience, I learned that I cared about the environment around me, and those who share them. I learned that small efforts can lead up to big improvements. I've noticed that it isn't only the leaders that make change happen, but it's also from anyone who is willing to notice the small problems and take the first step to fix it. In college, I will spread the word about the value of volunteer work and teach people to be more mindful about their surroundings so that we can keep our schools in a better condition than when we started.

essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
A quick reflection of my past yields a colorful story of excitement, positivity, and gradual maturation. I'm at the awkward stage in my life where the teenager in me is introduced to adulthood; a stage where I begin to set my priorities, envision a brighter future than yesterday, and build lifelong connections. Perhaps it is the healthy upbringing that my parents blessed me with that encouraged me to share this always can-do attitude with those that know me.

I've always tried to be a social person - something that my parents instilled in me at a young age. I enjoy communicating with friends, family, and unfamiliar faces alike. I challenge myself to learn more about others and to practice good judgement of others - never to look down on others that disagree with my values or assess someone based on their clothing or the cars that they drive. To that extent, I make my community a better place by always being friendly and extending my helping hand when needed.

During my time in community college, I had a positive impact on my friends and peers both academically and socially. Granted I live by the idea of "teamwork makes the dream work", I often contributed to group efforts not only to increase productivity, but to nurture the ideal college environment that gets everyone motivated. I've done everything from hiring a private tutor for group study sessions during midterm season and even recorded and broadcasted office hours lectures for those that didn't have the chance to attend.

My efforts to help others do not go unnoticed and my mission to make the college environment a comfortable, collaborative space is not wasted. I've seen struggling peers perform better on exams with the study groups that I organize. I've seen excelling students become more open to helping others and learning further in the process. I've seen the confidence levels rise among my study groups with the addition of a competent private tutor that I pay for with my personal savings. These contributions, I feel, best define the impact that I've had in my community.

essays.prompt: What have you done to make your school or your community a better place?
essays.essay:
As someone who has spent a lot of time in the computer science community, I know all too well how much my colleagues and I can struggle with confidence issues. Being behind a keyboard can seem empowering but transferring this confidence to the outside world can damage job prospects, social lives, and other facets of day-to-day existence. As such, I have become all the more determined to help others in the community overcome this issue.

For coders, developers, programmers, or anyone else who spends a lot of time staring at a screen, online communication is the default. Slack, Skype, Discord, IRC, or whatever program you use, being social online is only ever a few clicks away. You can be as anonymous as you like and it doesn't take long to familiarize yourself with the internet discourse which is so prevalent. As someone who has struggled to transpose online confidence into real world results, I always want to help people who are in a similar position.

I noticed members of the computer science community who struggle with social anxiety and other issues. Due to my past experiences, I've made it my mission to reach out to those in a similar position, including them in social activities and networking sessions. I've helped organize hackathons, for instance, ensuring that these events are approachable, inclusive, and a great conduit for improving confidence. I like to think that I've expanded our community, helping people come out of their shells and enjoy the full benefits of what the world of computer science has to offer.

After overcoming my own confidence issues, I've now expanded my own list of hobbies. Nowadays, I can be found rock climbing, off-road biking, and practicing gymnastics outdoors. At the same time, I've made friends and helped to boost the confidence of others, all through our shared hobby. Where I grew up, the computer science community was small and quite introverted. Now, thanks to my efforts, I'd like to think that we're an outgoing, confident, inclusive group. This, I believe, makes the community a better place.

essays.essay:
The pandemic was a difficult time for many people in my community. I grew sad as I saw local businesses shutting down in front of my eyes. The restaurants that I enjoyed throughout my childhood were closing their doors, and the heart of my community crumbled right in front of me.

I was troubled by this reality and decided to take action. I researched further and realized that most of these struggling businesses lacked an online presence or had websites that were slow and not optimized for success. Fortunately, I knew how to build a great website, and I was convinced that I could help drive more foot traffic to these local businesses if their websites were more modernized and appeared at the top of Google's search results.

Determined, I enlisted the help of a close friend. We created a list of over 200 local businesses and began making calls. The first few calls were discouraging declines, but we persisted and continued to reach out. After days of calling, we received our first resounding "yes!" from a kind restaurant owner who welcomed our help.

The owner was elated to have his first business website. To express his gratitude, he even invited our families to eat at his restaurant for free. We wasted no time building the best possible webpage for our client and received more responses from other businesses that wanted our help. In a short few months, we designed two beautiful websites from scratch. We knew that we were impacting our community by coding these websites since our work could help these establishments overcome the challenges of the pandemic.

Through this experience, I gained more than just web development skills; I discovered my entrepreneurial spirit. This experience exemplified how determination translates into real progress, and I felt more motivated than ever. More importantly, I realized the monumental role that these small businesses play within my community. They serve as the backbone of our community and helping them stay afloat means that my work will have a long-lasting impact on my community for years to come.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
Last summer, I made a big lifestyle change: I paid for a two year subscription at 24 Hour Fitness. My intent was to take advantage of the heated fitness pool and learn to swim. This was a big deal for me, mainly because it was the first time that I had the motivation to workout without being urged by a physical education teacher.

It didn't take long for me to realize that swimming was not my forte - far from it. If I wasn't struggling to stay afloat, I would panic and gasp in mouthfuls of water. And if I wasn't blinded by the seepage of water into my goggles, I would flail my arms and legs in a completely desynchronized manner. I was, in simple terms, a terrible floater.

This experience didn't stop me from trying, but it was frustrating nonetheless. I found myself entangled in new challenges each time that I stepped into the pool; but instead of dwelling on the failures, I focused on the small wins. Learning to float for even five seconds was a win; learning to develop a rhythm in my strokes was a win; learning to finally breathe in with my mouth and exhale with my nose was a win.

All of these small wins were the product of more than just my perseverance, but my willingness to learn. As odd as it sounds, I spent a lot of time watching others in the pool - paying attention to their warm up stretches, to their cadence between each stroke, to their exhaling and inhaling, and to how they used their full range of motion to propel forward.

In hindsight, learning to swim matured me in several ways: it presented me with a challenge, made me doubt myself, taught me to reevaluate difficult situations, test my patience, and made me more optimistic at the end. This experience was not taken lightly as it uplifted me as a student and self-learner. I find myself giving less excuses about not being able to accomplish certain tasks, and rather, put in greater effort to succeed both physically and academically.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
As I sat in front of my French teacher in sophomore year and had a nervous breakdown, I wished he could read my mind.

He couldn't understand why I didn't want to take my AP French exam. "But you're doing so well in class. You're one of my students I thought would get a 4 or 5," he said, his voice brimming with hope. Not many people at my school take AP French, so he was always extremely proud of the few who would, especially those who passed the exam. I knew I was letting him down, but I was so terrified that I might fail.

Whether applying for a job, playing a tennis match, or taking my driver's test, my mind was always more occupied thinking about the possibility of failure. This became an all-or-nothing mindset, where I would rather not try at all than give myself the chance to fail. But by not trying, I was missing out on countless opportunities. Something needed to change.

I began uncovering why I was so scared to fail in the first place. Each morning, I'd sit cross-legged on my bedroom floor, letting my racing thoughts settle through meditation. After a few minutes, I'd jot down my thoughts, noting anything that made me feel stressed. I slowly realized that as someone who puts in the maximum effort into anything I do, failure felt like a personal attack, damaging my self esteem. I wanted my hard work to be "worth it" by succeeding, but what I failed to realize was that the hard work itself was something I should be proud of. As I shifted my mindset from seeing failure as a reflection of my worth to viewing it as a natural part of learning, my fear lost its grip on me.

Looking back, many of the people and opportunities I have in my life today would not exist if I had remained the person I was two years ago. Embracing failure has opened doors I never thought possible, and has taught me that growth, not perfection, is the true measure of success.

essays.promptLabel: Most significant challenge you have faced
essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
“The game on the line, down by two, number 12 goes up for a three. Oh my goodness! Here comes number 3 [me] and blocks the shot,” the commentator screams ecstatically as the buzzer goes off, indicating the end of play. It may not be that cool, but a man can dream.

This moment from my final AAU tournament constantly goes through my dreams, the last game before a life-altering injury. All of my life, starting from when I was six years old and had just moved to America till this point during eighth grade, I had dedicated myself to practicing, learning, and competing. I had nothing else.

I was ready to get back on track after months of being beached at home and physical therapy. I wanted the joy of playing again, and that's when the quarantine struck. It could not have been worse timing. When reality landed another blow, I was on the verge of defeat. Nevertheless, that was when I stumbled upon a new realm. Rather than being knocked out, I found new motivation and solace in the complexity of computer science. The digital world became my new basketball court.

Spending innumerable hours learning new algorithms in Coursera and applying those algorithms on LeetCode helped me utilize the skills I learned through basketball. I discovered that the same determination and perseverance I once channeled on the court could be harnessed in the digital realm of programming. As I immersed myself in coding challenges, I found a unique satisfaction in tackling complex problems and creating elegant solutions. The thrill of witnessing my programs execute flawlessly – after spending an hour debugging – mirrored the excitement of making a game-winning shot.

As I embraced this novel pursuit, my grades soared, and I found myself venturing into coding competitions, fueled by the same competitive spirit that once drove me on the court. Although my injury robbed me of the ability to play basketball competitively, it gifted me with the discovery of a whole new realm of possibilities. While I may have found a new love, I still indulge in my first love.

essays.promptLabel: Most significant challenge you have faced
essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge.
essays.essay:
For a majority of my life, I lived and breathed Chinese tradition thanks to my parents, my formal education, and my environment. As my parents always touted, “being Chinese is a way of life, a part of your identity, and you can never forget that”. These words were profound because it instilled in me a sense of pride, arrogance, and belongingness. Everything from my fashion choices, the foods that I eat, and the way that I carry myself in public were all products of living in China and being surrounded by this incredible culture.

This was of course before I emigrated to America. Life in America didn't just feel like a different time zone, but like a different dimension - and I am hardly exaggerating. My first two years in the United States fell into the typical immigrant story of discrimination both in public and in school. There were countless times where I've encountered people that purposely spoke English in a heavy Chinese accent thinking it would be taken as humor and at school, where I would hear my name thrown into a blender of rhyming words to make a mockery of my very un-American name. It's these exchanges, accumulated over the years, that has made me feel embarrassed to be Chinese. This was my greatest challenge: to rediscover that pride and enthusiasm that I once had being Chinese.

In the years since, I've learned to be reasonable with my expectations. Being born into a culturally uniform society made ethnic discrimination a peculiar experience for me, but I've come to understand that social challenges are a normal part of life that many others deal with. I've learned to cope with my low moments through writing in a personal blog, through exercising in my backyard, through playing video games with people from all over the world, and through experiencing other cultures. I try new foods, explore cultural fashion in my daily wardrobe, socialize indiscriminately, among other things. All these things have reinspired my pride in the Chinese culture and helped me to stay focused and confident in school.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement? (Standard UC PIQ prompt; inferred from content, not printed in the document.)
essays.essay:
In front of me, the word “Defeat” was printed on the screen. Of course, sometimes a few “Victories” were sprinkled in here and there, but the word “defeat” has the sourest taste in my mouth. That taste trickled its way into my life in 2021.

Defeat. I was crushed by my father, who ripped himself out of my life, locked himself into his office, and began working himself to death. Once he tore away, I never shared the same bond with him again and felt like he neglected our crumbling relationship. I longed for someone to lean on like I used to with him. That someone crawled into my life right as my father left mine. That someone was video games.

Defeat. I was crushed, never realizing my losing battle before it was too late. I slipped into an addiction. I failed to see just how consumed I would become with just a push of a button. As the days blurred, I wrapped myself around this “hobby.” Who am I without my games? I never bothered to think about that question. I assumed I already knew the answer: that this is all that I am, and all that I’m worth.

A long awaited victory, September 2022. The facts hit me hard once I experienced Junior year and saw my grades dropping. I was growing up, and if I continued like this I would never find myself. Thus, I took matters into my own hands and enrolled into a leadership program based around game development in UCLA. I then participated in a program for girls to explore game design and connect with the company Electronic Arts. I continued meeting new people who I could rely on and discovered a new me. As a result, my once maladaptive lifestyle turned into a new and burning passion. In these experiences, I discovered that I can accomplish more than I think and that I can create things people can turn to. I found myself. I believe challenges are made to be difficult to trudge over, but it molded me into the someone I’m most proud of.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
After moving from Los Angeles to the Bay Area, I expected the change to be no big deal. But, I found myself slowly becoming more quiet. Back in Los Angeles, I was a very outgoing and talkative kid, but here, I struggled a lot with speaking up in class, and starting conversations. I felt like the problem isn't because I moved but it's because I lost confidence in myself.

My quietness has followed me into classrooms. During group projects, I struggled to share ideas. In Socratic Seminars, my mind filled with thoughts that I couldn't say because I was afraid of what others may say of me. Even when I didn't understand sometimes, I refused to go ask my teacher for help. My grades dropped, not because I didn't care or try, but because I was afraid to speak.

Change started slowly. I challenged myself everyday to speak at least once in class. I found a small group of friends that shared my same interest so I didn't feel like I was the odd one out. Over time, I realized that people don't care to give the time of day to judge me, and some might just be as nervous as me. This changed perspective taught me to reevaluate myself in social situations. Instead of closing off and making others feel uncomfortable, I've pushed myself to be the ice-breaker when I meet someone new. This shift was important for my own growth because I began to recognize that this problem was internal, and that people around me genuinely want to connect.

By junior year, I let these insecurities go. I wasn't afraid to ask teachers for help, voice my thoughts in a group project, speak in seminars. And, I didn't mind being first to present in class.

Learning to find my confidence to speak has changed my outlook in life and I never felt so much freedom in just being able to share my mind. This confidence has led me to new friendships, better relationships with teachers, and helped get me closer to where I was before I moved.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
My lack of proper mentorship has always been a challenge for me - not just in my academic achievements, but also in the grander sense. To be fair, my parents have and continue to be my central source of financial and mental support. They instilled in me the virtues of success, which cycle between the idea of always being prepared, always help others, and always staying positive. However, when it comes to things such as finding where my passion lies, figuring out how to get through high school courses, filling in college applications, writing essays to illustrate my life in four short prompts, my parents' help diminishes - and understandably so.

This was my greatest challenge: the challenge of always being dependent on someone or something. The challenge of accepting responsibilities and growing up. Now, in community college, I've learned that relying on others for success both academically and in life is not feasible. Rather, being that person in the position of supporting others and being relied on is far more rewarding. It wasn't easy to break out of this shell that I call being reliant - I had to make significant adjustments in my life to be a more independent and responsible individual.

During the first month of community college, I fast forwarded into adulthood. If I must confess, I began doing my own laundry; I took out my own trash; I cooked my own breakfast and prepared lunch a day in advance; I balanced my schedule; and I even began to pay for my own phone bills using the Chinese New Year red envelope money that I've stored away for over a decade. For the first time, I felt like I was in charge of my own life, and oddly enough, it felt great.

These steps have directly contributed to my academic achievements. I am not the top student in my class, but the mentality that I possess is on par with some of the most goal-oriented peers that I've worked with. At university, I will have another opportunity to present the best version of myself both academically and socially.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
Sir Isaac Newton famously argued that "an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion…".

Shortly after high school graduation, my friends invited me to use a social application called Discord. It was a social platform designed to connect friends and internet strangers through in-game voice calls - like a Zoom call for online gaming. I was drawn to the idea of staying connected with my buddies and meeting new gaming friends from all over the world. This was precisely when I fell into the pit of addictive gaming. Gradually, games became synonymous with breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Discord felt like a magnetic force, pulling me in like gravity and making me feel guilty if I ignored a request to join a tournament.

My rendition of Newton's first law of motion: I was an unmotivated object staying unmotivated. My mechanical engineering spirit slowly dissipated; my enthusiasm to cook melted away; and my desire to take a step out the door into nature faded like the silhouette of a boat heading towards the sunset.

As easy as it sounds to just step away from the keyboard and get back into the productive state of mind that I carried for most of my life, it was painfully difficult to shift back. My mentality collapsed and I had sleepless nights just pondering about which ability I could have used to win the game that I lost during the day. I was unhealthy, both mentally and physically. I was drained, with eyebags hanging ghastly below my eyes.

Fortunately, I found my way out. I detoxed, not because I wanted to, but because my friends stepped in like knights in shining armor, restoring me to normalcy. They dragged me on road-trips, drove me to grab dinner, sent me content about my favorite car brand, and suggested a library of books to self-learn mechanical engineering. This stimuli set me back in motion, allowed me to stay in motion, and greatly contributed to my growth in self-learning mechanical engineering and as an academic. I was back, better than ever, ready to succeed!

essays.promptLabel: Overcoming self-comparison and fear of mediocrity
essays.prompt: Prompt not labeled in the source document; the essay reflects on overcoming the habit of comparing oneself to others (inferred).
essays.essay:
In starting this prompt, I hope I succeed.

Every time I stare at this blank google doc and see the cursor blink, all I want to do is toss my computer into the trash and set it on fire. It roots from the frustration of being mentally incapable of coming up with anything that I believe is remotely interesting enough to write about, knowing that others have lived bigger, better, more intriguing lives than I have.

The fear of mediocrity is a silent killer and I'm its hostage.

Comparing myself to others has plagued me ever since I received my first letter grade in middle school. It plagued me in class when we wrote creative narratives and had to publicly post them for everyone in class to see, with me examining others, doubting mine, and rewriting everything to the point where I posted mine five minutes before it was due, still not content with how it turned out.

It even plagues me now, in writing this.

Perfection is a hard competitor to race with.

Reading other people's answers to this prompt, I can't help but notice their writing is better, stories are more detailed, vocabulary is higher, and descriptions are more in depth. I can't help it. I'm intimidated. I can't help but compare my hardships to theirs, degrading my struggles, making them look trivial, even when I know for a fact, to me, they're not.

A teacher told our class once, that success can be found anywhere and everywhere, you just have to look.

And it's something I've recently chosen to adopt into my mentality to combat this internal struggle I've let control the stories I choose to tell, whether others are more extravagant than mine. I believe that comparison is a universal flaw that lies within everybody, but I'm choosing to not let it dictate the value of my abilities.

With that being said, in answering this prompt to my heart's content I've succeeded.

And I'm going to celebrate it.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
I am confident that I have the ability to perform well in my selected major of business economics. My understanding of business and general economics stems primarily from my interest in startup businesses. Seeing the success that some of these newly minted and emerging businesses have had in the social media and technology space within the last two decades is envying to say the least. Thinking about the value of businesses and the impact that they have on society gives me an intense feeling of motivation; it gives me hope that someday I could also trail behind these success stories.

Perhaps I am too optimistic about what the future holds for me, but the realization that businesses are actively shaping the world as I speak is inspiring. To further my personal interest in business and to prepare for my intended major, I've started waking up earlier to watch the morning news. I do this to stay informed about the world around me. I believe that a large part of business as a profession and as a field of study revolves around being knowledgeable. Like the economy, businesses sway with the public, and there is no better way to stay informed than the news.

While in community college, I also took advantage of the ease of access to office hours. I connected well with my lecturers and professors, and had conversations about course materials that segued into discussion about businesses and investments. I feel that the time I invested into office hours gave me a far broader perspective of what business economics as a field encompasses. I learned that this field is extremely practical and versatile; that business is not just about startups or aiming for riches; it's about learning to communicate, gaining insight through pattern observation, building social networks, exchanging and molding new ideas, and solving global problems.

Through this lens, I am confident that business economics is the right field for me. I am fully prepared to succeed in upper-division courses and will do my best to apply the concepts in real practice when I have the opportunity.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
In high school, my parents would nudge me with the same question that I dreaded to hear: "Have you decided on what you want to study in college?" The questions would come in a flurry, alternating between my parents as if they had shifts to remind me that I needed to get my life oriented.

It seemed that for a while, my answer would always be a variation of "not yet", and in hindsight, I felt rushed by the time junior year of high school came around. This feeling was stress inducing and I knew that I had to align my passion into one field, but there were many options that muddied my vision.

Fortunately, community college provided the space and time for me to build a vision for my future. I had the opportunity to explore in depth many subjects that appealed to me and this gave me the reassurance that I needed to settle my sight on statistics.

Statistics naturally meddled with my curiosity about the world. I find that this field is misconstrued as impractical for the real world, but I see its implications as vital to many industries. More than just a party trick to calculate the odds of landing red at the casinos or a tool to solve the classic punnett squares in genetics, I see statistics as a powerful tool for preparation, prevention, assessment, and problem solving.

To further my interests in statistics, I attended office hours everyday to fine tune my comprehension of lecture material and to prepare for exams under the guidance of my lecturers. In doing so, I've learned the value of communication with faculty and gained insight into the correlation between statistics and fields such as business economics, computer science, and physical sciences. Moreover, my independent practice of statistics using software such as Capterra and Minitab has accelerated my abilities in algorithm development and mathematical analysis which are useful in simulating business cycles and chance related events. Having exposure to such complex and diverse application of statistics gives me confidence that I can succeed in my upper division courses.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Deciding on a career route was never an easy decision. Fortunately, I grew up in an Asian household where parental expectations were reasonable, but the pressure of performing well in school still lingered in my mind all the time. For most of high school, I assumed that I would end up studying marine biology as I was fascinated by the vastness and mystery of the ocean – or perhaps I would pursue legal studies where I could make a solid living by defending clients' rights. All of these opportunities sounded great at first, but it just made the major selection process more convoluted than necessary.

However, nothing painted a clearer picture in my mind about my career aspirations than my first job experience at State Farm as a representative. There, I grew an interest in business economics but it was far from an interest at first sight. I had to really test my patience, learn the trade, and apply my training each day that I worked on the sales floor, interacting with all types of customers. For me, State Farm started as an entry-level job that would diversify my portfolio for future jobs. Over time, however, my perspective changed significantly as I became more active in the tight-knit working environment at State Farm. Through the weekly conferences held at work, I truly experienced the value of teamwork in solving complicated tasks and gained insight into the many obscure variables that contribute to a healthy and profitable company. At that point, my job no longer felt like a responsibility, it felt like a true hands-on learning experience that I would not be able to replicate in a classroom environment.

Without a doubt, my role at State Farm has set me up for success in even the most challenging upper division courses. State Farm has given me the experience and tools to work effectively under pressure, showed me different ways of managing my time to meet important deadlines, and most importantly, developed my interest in a field that I had never previously considered.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Without a doubt, I intend to study economics at university. My parents, on the other hand, didn't always support this decision because they had uncertainties about what this field entails. They always made meager attempts to steer me into the direction of medicine, but I held firm to my passion. I've had an interest in learning economics since I was in middle school - I wanted to know more about how businesses operated, why stock prices change, and quite frankly, how some people manage to build billion dollar empires while others struggle to stay employed. These were the questions that I wanted to explore, and I plan to do so at university.

In community college, I pursued my interest of economics and prepared for upper-division courses in an odd way: I invested into the stock market. While I understood that the stock market is only a fraction of economics, it was far more insightful than reading scholarly journals and watching documentaries about the Great Depression in community college.

For my initial investment, I started with $200 on a trading platform called Acorns. With little experience but a bit of luck, I actually made a small profit. But as I started doing my research by reading company financial reports, joining investor conference calls, and learning how to analyze stock price patterns, I was able to make smarter decisions that led to greater profits.

Perhaps the best part about investing in the stock market was that it gave me a real-world experience of economics, and it reinforced my decision to study economics. For the first time, I felt like I was no longer limited to learning about economic theories; I was able to put what I have learned into practice and observe real-world economic variables that trigger fluctuations in the stock market. And much like the work that I put into researching stocks, I intend to relay this work ethic towards my studies at university to ensure that I will be fully equipped and successful in my upper-division courses.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
My intended major is Computer Science. I am specifically interested in software and web development because this is a part of computer science that requires a heavy amount of coding - which I have extensive experience in. My passion for coding began four years ago on Codecademy, which is a website designed to teach the rudiments of coding in various languages. I used Codecademy practically every day for a year, learned to code in the Python and HTML5 languages, and later, tested my skills online by joining collaborative projects that focused on building web browser extension programs.

My experience and ambition in this field provide me the confidence to succeed in my upper-division courses, but I continue to prepare myself for the challenges at university by expanding my expertise towards different coding languages and keeping up with the latest coding forums where valuable advice, insights, and discoveries are shared. This type of supportive - yet competitive - atmosphere is exactly what I need to keep myself motivated to practice my craft.

Recently, I have spent my time to develop an online boutique for a friend. In the process, I have encountered various challenges that involve: setting up a secure payment option, finding a credible database for client information, and creating unique graphics to enhance the aesthetics of the site. These are the types of challenges that I find motivating because it pushes me to think about problem-solving strategies, and allows me to gauge the level of my skill in coding.

At university, I plan to use my experience to practice the theories of computer science. Inherently, computer science is an exceptionally difficult field that I see as a never-ending loop of refinements to computer technology, and that is exactly why it appeals to me. My hope is that at university, I will meet like-minded individuals that appreciate the power of coding, and that are willing to collaborate with me on innovative projects that have the potential to improve the user experience for anyone that owns a computer.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
“Which one should we get? JavaScript for Dummies or Objective-C for Dummies?” I remember my best friend asking me this question four years ago in the middle of the computer programming aisle at Barnes and Nobles. At the time, I had a very limited understanding of the computer science, but I soon developed a serious curiosity in this field after attending a computer science workshop hosted at my high school.

In short, my friend and I decided to purchase the JavaScript guide based on recommendations from an online forum of computer programming enthusiasts. My first experience of coding was incredibly challenging to say the least, and admittedly, there were moments where I felt uncertain about whether this was the right path for me. Coding was unlike any academic subject that I had encountered, and for the first time, I felt that I could no longer rely purely on memorization and studying to get by. However, I didn’t give up despite my uncertainties. I continued to self-study throughout community college as a form of preparation for upper-division courses in university by studying computer science concepts on YouTube and Khan Academy, and subscribing to coding bootcamps online for further practice.

Four years of coding experience later, I have gained a proficiency in JavaScript, C++, and Python - all of which are highly versatile languages in computer science. In this time, I realized that learning to code requires more than just intelligence and grit, it demands an open-mindedness to change, a vision of the final product, an awareness to minor details, and most importantly, a capacity for problem solving. In hindsight, everything that I have learned from my experiences with coding has had a very positive impact on me as a student. My passion for computer science has not only kept me academically driven, but it has also given me a sense of direction that I never had in high school and it gives me the type of confidence that I need to succeed in university.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
While studying at my community college, I was enrolled into Introduction to Business, which is a course that uses the theoretical principles of economics to describe the framework of business operations and marketing ploys. Through this course, I came up with the idea of purchasing a vendor's permit at the San Jose flea market to sell the clutter that had built up in my closet over the years. This was my first experience at the flea market and what I consider to be the start of my preparation for university.

At the flea market, I learned that communication is the key to business. Following the advice of my business professor that, "business and economics are intertwined - if you want to make a sale, you have to communicate the value of your supply to generate its demand", I initiated small-talk with prospective customers. By communicating, I gave myself a critical window of opportunity to build demand for my goods through persuasion and recognizing the needs of the customers. Apart from becoming a great salesman, what I gained is the important ability to sustain a meaningful conversation.

At university, I intend to pursue a degree in economics. Specifically, my interest involves studying different business structures, learning about the financial responsibilities to support a business, and most importantly, discovering the powerful influence of economics on business stability. As preparation for the upper-division courses where I will have a chance to gain a better understanding of my interests, I have participated in a study group at my community college where I exchange my ideas and knowledge about subjects spanning financial management, accounting, micro-economics, and a range of mathematics. Being part of this group has not only furthered my communication skills, but it has also given me the pressure to study the material in advance and address any questions with my professors and peers beforehand. Aside from my study group, I have also self-taught myself a comprehensive list of economic terms by reading The Essentials of Economics by Gregory Mankiw, which has given me a much easier time in understanding the course material for various courses.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Growing up, my older relatives had always turned to me when it came to matters of social media, online bank accounts, and online storefront, as if mistaking me to be co-inventor of such innovations. I guess this has always been the case for us folks who grew up in the digital age. Being faced with this question, I ruminate and realized I could count on one hand the innovations that had been brought forward to the U.S. where technology isn't involved. I am and have always been seeking to position myself in places of innovation, which is why it is easy for me to take my main interest and choose it as a major. This is, of course, Computer Science– a field which is always on the constant state of evolution, prompting the world with advancements that were once written off as science fiction.

I even remember the first time I launched DreamWeaver on my Windows Vista laptop when DreamWeaver and Vista were still a thing. We had barely progressed a decade and those two had already been marked 'antiquated'. This small yet seismic shift alarmed me to the fact that we are living in a fast-changing world and pushed me to master the basics first. I have always had a knack for understanding mathematics and algorithms where the rule is simple: one solution either is correct or incorrect. My interest in the field of Computer Science grew further that I took even bolder steps in creating my groundwork.

When my batchmates hyped about their dream careers being glamorized on pop culture which usually involved something in the entertainment industry or government work, I was consumed by the elegance of the idea of what we now know is the Weissman score. My basic-level research on the topic of this lossless data compression technique, which had been quickly turned from fiction to fact, had left such an impact on me that I believe when I'm to be introduced to the more complex and grounded parts of programming, ones with real world applications, I'd be able to easily keep up.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
In the last two years of high school, I was not entirely sure how to move forward and what sort of places my passion would go to. I traipsed my day-to-days thinking that perhaps tourism or hotel management would be suitable - being that I am a person who enjoys travelling and meeting new people. But as I moved on to community college, my heart and mind had been equally set on studying mathematics with an emphasis on economics.

While in community college, I have entertained with the idea of paper trading. Something about these simulated stock portfolios were fascinating, and the novice trader in me wanted to experiment. Paper trading provided a very surface understanding of mathematics and economics such that I had to learn about leveraging, risk management, building long term wealth and generating passive income. I also delve into the microeconomics side of investing by tuning into earnings reports conferences for businesses that I followed and learned to read stock charts at a fundamental level. I have to admit, however, that I did not exactly have the healthiest portfolio by years end, but it only fueled me to understand the underlying principles and overarching factors that contributed to interplay that is economics.

Where paper trading provided a supplemental form of preparation for university, community college provided the more tangible elements. In these two years of college, I've learned more than just rudimentary economics; I've developed a commitment to working hard, staying on top of my course requirements for transfer, and even connected with peers and instructors that genuinely want me to succeed. For the first time in a while, I felt confident in my abilities and I felt the support of my social circle against the weight of college work. Community college gave me a fresh slate and I used all the resources within my reach to prepare well for university. For these reasons, I am fully aware of where I want to be, what I want to study, and how I will succeed as an economics major with a focus on mathematics.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Growing up, I have seen some of my extended family becoming successful working in fund management positions and engineer jobs. The hardworking people that surround me were able to sustain good lives even when set against the competitive nature of Californian business attitudes and the disadvantages of being first generation American immigrants. I have always dreamt of being like that, and there is no shortage of inspiration around me, but I want to build upon my own passions without riding along the coattails of my relatives.

I ultimately decided on economics as my intended major. My closest friends, who have all committed to a computer science tract or recently signed up to coding boot camps, were all confused about what I saw in this field that was so appealing. Perhaps I am among the few in today's technology focused society that recognizes the broader impacts of economics on the infrastructure of every industry, every business, and many social issues. It is this desire that I have to study economics that makes me confident that I would succeed under any circumstances.

To prepare for upper division courses at university, I have strengthened my proficiency in mathematics and economics by enlisting the help of a private tutor. The mentorship that I received prompted me to revisit my learning strategies that I previously had not considered. I started by studying lecture material week in advance to avoid cramming, which in turn resulted in shorter study schedules to free up my day. My tutor had also explained the importance of learning by listening rather than vigorously jotting down half completed lecture notes, which helped me with memorization and long-term retention of the material. I also implemented "visual queues" as my tutor would call them, which is the creative way of attaching mental objects to certain vocabulary or concepts to further improve recall of the material. These experimental steps in learning felt uneasy and took some time to get used to, but since then, I have gained more confidence in myself to succeed and developed a habit of asking for help when needed.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
A watch, as simple as a sweeping dial on an automatic watch may appear, underneath its surface is a complex arrangement of cogs, dial trains, balance wheels, and springs. At the age of 14, I was given one of these incredible pieces of engineering. It was a skeleton automatic watch, where the entire casing was transparent. It was the first time that I received such an expensive present. I was confused, mesmerized, curious, and inspired all at the same time.

Fast forward to present day, I'm a knowledgeable, ambitious, and budding learner of mechanical engineering. I graduated from building Lego figurines of battery-powered motors, steamboat turbines, and sportscar engines to now learning real-world engineering concepts that deal with high-level mathematics, evaluating prosthetic machinery in textbooks, and creative problem solving. Where Legos have manuals for guidance, engineering courses often rely on listening, memorization, intuition, and strategizing.

On an everyday basis, I spend personal time outside of school to learn mechanical engineering. In the last three years, I've developed the tenacity and discipline to spend half an hour each day learning virtual mechanical engineering tools with real-world applications such as AutoCAD and Autodesk Modflow. These tools enable me to design illustrations of ideas that come to mind, such as a crank-operated motor or a basic 4-cylinder car engine that I'm currently attempting to assemble. It's amazing to see these simulations come to life on a virtual screen and it's even more interesting when it fails, because it prompts me to dig deeper to figure out the source of the mechanical failure. Moreover, these are tools that real professionals use at their jobs, be it a car mechanic, an aerospace engineer, or an architect.

Ultimately, the combination of learning mechanical engineering in school and applying them on practical applications outside of school is self-affirmation that this is the field I want to be in. I will continue to use these skills, knowledge, and motivation to forward my progress in learning mechanical engineering at university and I am confident and well-equipped to manage the challenges that come with upper-division courses.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
