An elderly woman I met at the gym once told me: "mental preparation always beats physical preparation." I had no reason to doubt this sweet lady who, at her age and frail frame, could still curl twice the weight in dumbbells that I can.

In preparing for future upper-division courses at university, I've designed a personal studying regiment that simply works. Instead of using the brute force, cram-study strategy that netted nothing good in the past, I decided to take a different train in community college.

I set up my mental groundwork by first creating self-discipline. I've committed to a "sprint schedule", which I learned from books on personal growth, time management, and productivity. These books taught me the value of "setting and not forgetting" because all too often, I set goals that wither away with time - like ink on an old receipt.

When I set sprint goals, I set them with the intention to fulfill. I chuck in rewards as a bonus. If I study 45 minutes a day, 8 days ahead of my exam, I'll buy that way too expensive coffee grind from Devout. If I go to office hours twice this week, I'll splurge on an Uber Eats delivery.

These incremental goals have changed the way that I think as a learner. I quickly learned that the size of the reward wasn't the driver of good habits; it was my new appreciation for small wins that helped me to build a great mentality and better grades.

The mental training of incorporating sprints into my daily routine has had a wonderful impact on my progress. The depth of knowledge that I have for economics is blossoming as a result of these small wins and I feel empowered to do more.

The trade-off here is fatigue. Sprints are hard to maintain, so I recently added meditation into my routine. The serenity of momentarily pausing time, clearing my mind, and controlling each breath helps me to unwind.

For me, the moral of the story is to listen to the elderly. They usually know a thing or two about life.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Our society is currently experiencing exponential growth in computer technology, unlike anything else in human history. I have grown up in the shadow of this huge boom and I am fascinated by the machines which watch over us, which govern our lives, and which make the impossible, possible. I wanted to study computer science; I want to understand and contribute to the rapid development of our society and I have geared my life towards this field.

Fortunately, I am in the position where my elected major and my personal passions perfectly align. After seeing the ways in which computer sciences has become a foundational part of everyday life, I am not only delighted to study computer science, but I am also pleased that I can apply what I have learned into practice. Whether it's taking part in competitive hackathons, learning how to program a friend's smart refrigerator, or investigating the technology behind self-driving cars through tech forums, every day is a new opportunity to prepare and better myself.

In recent years, community college has contributed to my growth in computer science and has given me a new perspective on how to be successful. I have studied computer science and put the theories into practice; I have learned multiple coding languages in the last two years; I have developed websites for friends in the retail business space; and I have explored the changes in this field as it progresses. Moreover, my curiosity, my love of reading tech-related articles, my applications of coding in a personal mobile application that I am developing has all contributed to my certainty in this field. And even with the time I commit to growing as a computer scientist, I still maintain a healthy balance between academics and my social and physical lifestyle.

I hope that transferring to the University of California will be one of the most important steps in my personal journey. As someone who works incredibly hard, I hope to take advantage of everything the institution has to offer and hope that I have prepared myself more than adequately. I am ready.

essays.prompt: Please describe how you have prepared for your intended major, including your readiness to succeed in your upper-division courses once you enroll at the university.
essays.essay:
Deciding on a career path was not easy. Fortunately, I was raised in a household where parental expectations were fair, but the pressure of being a first-generation college student hovered over me like a dark cloud. Throughout high school, I was indecisive and my interests wavered like a kid at an ice cream shop. Sometimes, I envisioned myself going down the nursing route where I could treat patients and work with doctors to save lives. Other days, I fancied the idea of becoming a software engineer because that's the new normal.

In recent years, I've settled down on business administration and economics as my college majors. A big factor in this decision was that I started a small business on Etsy and Pinterest to showcase my hobby of scrapbooking and designing calendars. At this time, my products are free to access because I'm still testing the waters and learning the business model. I find that the greatest challenge of commercializing do-it-yourself products is building a returning audience and creating an attractive listing that draws in attention. The competition on these e-commerce platforms are also higher than ever, with many people doing it as a full-time job and a team of staff managing some of the most successful operations. This is why I chose business administration and economics: to learn how to manage a business, maintain fluid operations, and gain experience in marketing strategies.

Although I still don't make any money on Etsy and Pinterest, I still spend a lot of time on it each day.

Unlike the past where I had to find reasons to like a field, I simply gravitated towards business administration and economics through my experiences. More importantly, this business experience sets up a nice foundation for me to learn business and economics first hand, and provides a great frame of reference for me to utilize what I learn in college. Moreover, I gained what feels like years of learning experience while managing this small business and this gives me all the confidence I need to succeed in upper division courses for this major.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
I've always been a shy kid, but I figured I'd grow out of it one day.

But I don't know if I ever will.

Embarrassment causes my back to profusely sweat, cheeks to grow hot, and heart to race, with an urge to firmly tug on each finger thinking it'll relieve the tension I feel as my stomach drops with every breath I take. All I can process in those moments is that this is the end, and from there it's an infinite cycle of escalation.

Social anxiety is my challenge.

High school is an obstacle in itself, but for me it's terrifying. Chinese class in particular was an absolute horror show. It involved the public speaking of a language I hardly knew in front of an audience of fluent speakers. When the teacher called on students to recite sentences, all I did was repeat what I would have to say over and over in my head and hope she'd pick someone else. You can probably already guess that I messed up a lot. It was brutal.

With that being said, I worked even harder to prepare for class each day to minimize my mistakes, and in the long run I proceeded to take the class year after year. I found myself becoming a better student in all my classes through applying the same work ethic.

The fear of humiliation is still a very present part of my life, but I've learned a few tricks to cope. I've learned how to laugh things off even when it's the last thing I want to do, as well as reassure my mind through saying to myself that the world isn't over, that I'm in a safe environment to fall down, and get back up again, especially with the support I receive from my close friends and family.

Though it's a pain to endure, my social anxiety has provided me with a work ethic that I'll take with me to college, and genuine relationships I'll cherish forever. There are still days where it feels like the world is falling apart, but regardless I won't let it stop me from pursuing my goals.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
I once found joy in the captivating world of video games such as Fortnite, Spider-man, and Minecraft, playing for hours. I would get lost in the fantasies brought by the game, neglecting more important aspects of my life such as my family and school.

My addiction reached a point where I resorted to lying about completing necessary chores and homework. On certain days when I was alone, I would play for six hours at a time, ignoring basic needs like using the restroom or going outside to play. Sometimes, I would intentionally ask my parents to cook a smaller serving so that I could quickly return to gaming. I constantly suppressed my hunger and fatigue in order to convince myself that I was fine.

My body and mind were facing the consequences of my poor decisions. In school I would be thinking about new items I could unlock, ignoring my teachers and failing to answer basic questions. As I looked around, I noticed the progress my friends were making in their studies and involvement in extracurriculars. While they were seeking new opportunities to expand their knowledge, I remained at the same place, focusing only on video games. I felt deeply saddened as I would not be able to experience the same things as my friends. My friends participated in the AMC math competition and were discussing their scores. I could not join in the conversation since I did not take the exam.

My relationships were drifting, signaling the requirement for a transformation in my life. I slowly started to stop giving in to the temptation of video games. Every day I played less and less. I could see a considerable difference in my life as I distanced myself from the games. I devoted my newfound time into Computer Science, family, and school. As a result, my academic achievements started to grow and reach new heights. Throughout this struggle, I learned the value of discipline, setting priorities, and the impact of perseverance. The determination and resilience I gained from this experience has helped me go to the gym, and I am sure that it will have positive benefits in the future.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
Silence. Not a word out of anyone's mouth, it was like taking a penalty in the World Cup final – and missing. My worst fear was there, blanking out during a presentation. Experiences like those are what created my fear of public speaking. This fear didn't just affect my confidence but also my grades, especially in presentations and projects involving collaboration.

This led me to join my high school's Speech and Debate team in Public Forum. We mainly compete in local tournaments with lay judges. To really appeal to the judge, we related the debate topics to their lives and built a story around them. This helped us sound less monotonous and speak with emotion. Through this, I was able to form a genuine connection with the judges, which made the experience far less nerve-racking.

To further refine my public speaking, I took the opportunity through 4H to compete at County Activity Day, where my partner and I gave a presentation on a topic of our choice. We chose bread, a narrow but fun challenge. The preparation process was unusual as I've never presented an abstract concept like this, but it was entertaining. We appealed to the judges by bringing in bread from different cultures, all while making funny remarks throughout. All of this improved my impromptu skills and helped me feel more comfortable speaking to an audience. In the end, we won gold at the district and county levels, and silver at states.

Overcoming my fear of public speaking made me more confident and changed the way I approach challenges. What once felt like a wave of anxiety became something I looked forward to. However, confidence didn't come overnight; it developed through discomfort and accepting mistakes as an opportunity. Every debate round and 4H presentation taught me to embrace mistakes, adapt under pressure, and connect with my audience as people and not judges. Now, when I stand in front of a crowd, I don't see it as a penalty kick that I might miss. I see it as a chance to share a story worth hearing.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
As I slowly ascended towards the sky for what felt like an eternity, I felt disoriented and light-headed. My eyes were tightly shut and my sweaty hands were gripped onto the safety harness. All I could hear was the "click-clack" noise from beneath the roller coaster, and before I was prepared, I was catapulted into a series of loops and turns that took the voice right out of my mouth. I was mortified as I gasped for air, but my friends were having the time of their lives.

It's quite embarrassing to admit that I have acrophobia, or the fear of heights, despite boasting to my friends about my adventurous lifestyle. I hike on a weekly basis, but I frequently encounter situations where I have to decide whether I would climb a small hill to reach my destination or look for a different path that doesn't require climbing - I always pick the latter.

But on this trip to Six Flags in Magic Mountain, I decided against my own will to stay away from heights. My desire to try what appeared to be a children's ride led to the worst several minutes of my entire night, but strangely enough, I felt happy that I did it. It's difficult to explain the mixed sensation of fear while being tossed in all directions, and at the same time, feeling a sense of relief that I was alive to see the moment unfold.

Since then, I have taken incremental steps to overcome acrophobia by trying indoor rock climbing at Diablo Rock Gym and indoor skydiving at iFLY - both of which I was hesitant at first, but grown fond of.

What I gained from this experience is the confidence to face challenges head on and try new things. I am no longer limited by my fears, and continue to preach this attitude towards academics. I am not afraid to take courses out of my comfort zone, and I am no longer hesitant to take my concerns to my professors. I feel absolute control of my life and I hope to keep it that way.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
It was a brisk summer morning. My friends and I had set up camp by the Tenaya Lake to appreciate its mountainous backdrop. This was my first camping experience and I was incredibly excited. I wanted to explore the campsite, collect boulders for a fire pit, roast marshmallows as I see in movies, and most of all, I wanted to swim.

The problem was that I didn't know how to swim, but I couldn't resist seeing my friends having a great time while I sat in a tent. In a haste, I changed into my shorts and darted for the water. Everything was fine at first. I had a great time in shallow waters and was even pleasantly surprised by a pack of fish swimming inches from my face, but before I had time to react, my foot left the pebbly shore. I was in deep waters - actually, I was in deep trouble. In that instant, I got nervous and knees locked up from the cold water. I was sinking, and the last thing I remember was two of my friends scrambling to help me.

This was my first experience of drowning, but instead of instilling fear in me, it actually encouraged me to learn how to swim. I took advantage of the pools at 24 Hour Fitness where I learned to swim comfortably in the 4 feet pool. I wish I could say that I could scuba dive at this point, but frankly, I have much more to learn. As of now, I am learning how to tread water. It looked easy from the online tutorials, but it is deceptively hard and strenuous when I do not have proper form.

The lesson I learned from this experience is to never overestimate my abilities. I apply this principle to my academics where I maintain a healthy level of self-confidence, but also keeping an open mind about learning. I admit that I was arrogant, but had I not experienced this with the right group of people, the outcome may be far worse in a different situation.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
While most kids fear monsters, my greatest fear has always been tests. Since elementary school, I've dealt with incapacitating test anxiety. I'd sit down for a spelling test and faint from anxiety. Math tests in middle school would make me run to the bathroom ill. By the time I reached high school, where the testing stakes became even higher, my test anxiety increased exponentially.

More than normal feelings of nervousness or anxiousness, it is a diagnosis I wrestle with daily. Test anxiety caused me to miss a number of tests that I had no option to re-take. It's caused me to receive abysmal scores on standardized and state tests, which has had repercussions in the classes I'm allowed to take. My test anxiety has been the greatest challenge of my life. In a school system so reliant on testing, it has completely affected my ability to achieve academically.

By the time I took the PSATs, I couldn't even move my hand to write my name. I knew something had to change. I reached out for help. My mom knew I had been struggling but didn't understand the extent of my illness. Together, we contacted my school counselor, who told us how to find a therapist.

With my doctors, I worked to mitigate the effects of my test anxiety on a medical and psychological level. I began taking beta-blockers that helped slow my heart rate, thus tricking my body into being less anxious. Alongside that, I spent months working through the reasons my brain interpreted testing as such a threat. I learned to appreciate my intrinsic value instead of relying on external factors like test scores. And rather than viewing tests as chances to fail, I began to understand them as opportunities to showcase my growth.

Now, after two long years of effort, I can take any test with ease. Since learning how to manage my disorder, I've successfully taken my driver's test, SATs and ACTs, and all seven of my AP exams. I'm looking forward to all the tests I'll take in college.

essays.prompt: Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?
essays.essay:
As I sat in front of my French teacher in sophomore year and had a nervous breakdown, I wished he could read my mind.

"But you're doing so well in class. You're one of my students I thought would get a 4 or 5," he said, his voice brimming with hope. Not many people at my school take AP French, so he was always extremely proud of the few who would, especially those who passed the exam. I knew I was letting him down, but I just didn't know how to explain how terrified I was that I might fail.

Whether applying for a job, playing a tennis match, or taking my driver's test, my mind was always more occupied thinking about the possibility of failure. This grew into an all-or-nothing mindset, where I would rather not try at all than give myself the chance to fail. But by not trying, I was already missing out on so many opportunities. I knew something needed to change.

I began uncovering why I was so scared to fail in the first place. Each morning, I'd sit cross-legged on my bedroom floor, letting my racing thoughts settle through meditation. After a few minutes, I'd jot down my thoughts, noting anything that made me feel stressed. I slowly realized that as someone who puts in the maximum effort into anything I do, failure felt like a personal attack, damaging my self esteem. I wanted my hard work to be "worth it" by succeeding, but what I failed to realize was that the hard work itself was something I should be proud of. As I shifted my mindset from seeing failure as a reflection of my worth to viewing it as a natural part of learning, my fear lost its grip on me.

Looking back, many of the people and opportunities I have in my life today would not exist if I had remained the person I was two years ago. Embracing failure has opened doors I never thought possible, and has shown me that growth, not perfection, is the true measure of success.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
All around us, the world is dominated by big voices, people who can present themselves positively and effectively elaborate on their opinions. Many of our most successful politicians carve their paths to the top through their charisma and articulate language. Unfortunately, while many of them possess a strong voice, many of them don’t possess that same strength in listening. While their job is to represent the people, there is a large disconnect between their perspective and the perspectives of their citizens. Even in Congress, civilized debate has transformed into a shouting battle, where both parties attempt to push their ideas, but neither side is willing to listen.

In contrast, a leader with an open ear, an open mind, and an open heart is exactly what I bring to the table. I believe that everyone has a unique story to share. From the most flamboyant billionaires to the people living on the streets, every single person possesses their own unique set of skills, perspective, and knowledge that can be useful to learn from. Because of this, I make it my priority to listen to and understand the human behind each team member I work with. In recognizing each person’s strengths and weaknesses, I’m able to build a positive environment in which every person is able to reach their maximum potential.

For example, when it comes to group projects, I always make sure to know the personalities of those I’m working with and create a transparent and inclusive environment that is conducive to productivity. Rather than dishing out assignments and deadlines, I make sure everyone is able to contribute in a way that matches their strengths and skills. Furthermore, by creating such a transparent atmosphere, group members are able to understand each other’s situations and help each other out like an actual team, allowing everyone to be both productive and pleased.

With all the divisiveness that is taking place in the country today, it is more necessary than ever to have open-minded leaders such as myself to help bring this campus and this nation together.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
Stepping foot in public has been like opening a floodgate to questions and comments about the one thing that I’ve been looked down upon my entire life for - my height. Standing out because I was 4'9" wasn’t something I was proud of; I was picked last for sports, not taken seriously, and often used as a human arm rest. My mom warned me life was going to be hard if I didn’t drink my milk. However, people aren’t aware that my appearance is a deception and what makes me extraordinary is that I’ve outgrown myself. People should be asking me how a person so “big” can fit into a girl so tiny. I have a huge personality, dreams, goals, and a plethora of talent. My achievements earned me such a high standing that I do know what the weather is like up there, yet, my head is never in the clouds because my distance from the ground makes me down to earth.

My only oddity is that my anatomy has grown out of proportion. It’s hard to believe that with such short arms, I can extend them long enough to touch hearts with my art and performances. I have been devoted to helping people and educating myself ever since I was young, but who knew that my brain and heart would become so gigantic? Despite how big my brain is, I keep my head as small as my body because I value letting others know that I’ll never overlook them.

Although I haven’t hit as many significant growth spurts as the average person, I grow with ambition every day, considering every moment a step closer to success. Being able to pursue my passions at a university will allow me to continue maturing into a person who will one day be looked up to by many. The reader of my response cannot see the facade that has been the subject of many people’s first impressions of me. Instead, they will observe that even though I can’t reach the top shelf, I can still reach my goals in life.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
The eyes eat before the stomach. When we are given a plate of food, the presentation of the meal can influence our expectations of how it will taste. The human instinct to judge by appearance doesn’t stop at food though. It affects how we view people too.

Looking younger than my age has followed me like a shadow, shaping every interaction I have. Standing at five feet tall, I already was on the shorter side. Inheriting my mother’s baby face and my father’s lean build didn’t make my situation any better. I dreaded seeing the confused looks as people questioned if I was the face behind the professional-sounding emails we communicated through. In group projects, it often felt like classmates would talk over me or dismiss my ideas as insignificant. Being treated as if I were a child, even if unintentional, made me question my own capabilities and wonder if I was truly unimportant. I became afraid to put myself out there, fearing being unjustly judged.

However, in my silence, I gained a strength. I have honed my empathy by learning to observe—to read the subtle cues and unspoken dynamics others might miss. Being overlooked myself has given me a lens to notice those who go unseen, an increasingly valuable skill in our world filled with distractions and snap judgments. I take pride in my ability to consider others’ perspectives, even if they don’t speak out. Once invisible, empathizing with others motivates me to ensure that everyone is given the fair chance to be heard. I strive to be the one who turns to the “quiet” student and asks for their ideas and thoughts, or who reaches out to someone standing alone to include them and make them feel seen. I believe that observing and recognizing people’s unique contributions is the first step to creating an environment wholeheartedly dedicated to fostering support and understanding between each other. It’s easy to put ourselves first, but true strength lies in putting in the effort to make someone else feel seen, valued, and uplifted, especially when it is most difficult.

essays.promptLabel: What makes you a strong candidate (PIQ)
essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
In the summer of last year, I received a text message from my uncle who was an ambitious entrepreneur trying to break into the heavily saturated milk tea industry. He asked me what I thought would be a unique topping to add into milk tea. My first thought: fruit puree.

This year, my uncle is on track to have his second grand opening of his milk tea brand in a nearby city. He took my advice and worked out a formula for a peach, mango, and blueberry puree as a topping and added a twist of foamed cheese on top for a unique blend of flavors. Over the last three months, I helped out at the milk tea shop on the weekends, mainly looking into new ways to jazz up his product line and created spreadsheets for him to determine which flavors had the best sales. Although I only volunteered to help him, this experience was the first hands on experience that I had with business operations.

I believe that having this first hand experience in the day-to-day operations of a business, albeit a small one, makes me a great candidate for the University of California to consider. While I was able to help my uncle with his initial launch with an innovative product, I think this speaks volumes about what I can offer if given the educational resources that could help me develop as a student and as a thinker. Frankly, the fruit puree idea was only a spur of the moment type of suggestion, but this made me realize that one small window of opportunity can lead to significant changes in my life, and that's why at the University of California, I will see it as my duty to try new things as it can be an opener for great opportunities.

My hope is that the positive energy that I always carry will inspire confidence from the board of admissions to give me an opportunity to prove that I am a capable student.

essays.promptLabel: What makes you a strong candidate (PIQ)
essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
I have thought a lot about this question. In fact, completing this application has forced me to examine myself in greater detail. What do I offer that makes me stand out? Time and time again, I would type out stereotypical qualities highlight my passion, my hard work, my experience. And while these responses are genuine representations of who I am, it lacks that "wow factor" that I'm subconsciously looking for.

Perhaps I am overcomplicating the purpose of this question. To be quite frank, I do not have any quirky skills or interest tricks under my sleeve that sets me apart from the hundreds of thousands of applicants. It's hard to be the odd one out; but I do believe that I would be an excellent candidate for admission into the University of California because of what I am not. I am not an individual that uses grades as a measure of my success. I am not an individual that focuses solely on academics. I am not the typical student that uses the word procrastination as a joke.

I am however, a person that is honest with myself and others. I am a person that constantly reevaluated my own work for improvements. I am a person that loves to communicate my ideas and listen to others for advice. I am a person that is dependable when a family member, friends, or newly met peers need a helping hand. I am a person that learns through watching and listening. I believe that the combination of these qualities is what makes me a great candidate and a decent person to get to know more about.

These qualities, coupled with my passion for computer science and my experience in coding are some of my best qualities. I truly hope that this honest self-examination makes me stand out as an individual that deserves the opportunity to study at the greatest education platform that is the University of California. My intention is to take what I learn into the professional workforce and proudly represent the university that believes in me.

essays.promptLabel: What makes you a strong candidate (PIQ)
essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
I believe my curiosity and positive attitude are my strongest attributes that make me stand out as a strong applicant. I am a person that always desire to try new things, travel, and take on big challenges. I'm never afraid of unfamiliarity and obstacles because that's what makes life interesting. Frankly, I think a big part of this do-it-all attitude stems from me being bored all the time. I have a habit of finding new things to do, whether it's searching for new travel destinations to feed my passion for snowboarding or discovering new home improvement projects for my family to enjoy. As long as it's new to me, I'm always up for the challenge.

I think as a student, actively engaging in different things is critical for success and adaptation. I anticipate university to hurl major obstacles in my direction, from exams to term papers to research projects, but my attitude will always be positive because every one of these challenges is a new opportunity to learn. My hope is that at university, I will blend myself into a group of new friends that are also as curious, adventurous, and driven as I am. The friends that I have met at my community college have all been very supportive of this lifestyle that I lead. They travel with me to new places just to get the perfect photo for our social media profile pictures, they teach me how to cook foods from different cultures, they put me on to watching sports like boxing and soccer, and I'm grateful for these experiences.

Above all, I think being always curious has built dexterity in my character which will play a role in my success at university. I've failed so many times by trying new things like making a pizza, sticking to a diet plan, building my own website, all of which didn't pan out the way I imagined. But from these experiences, I've become a hardened individual that isn't afraid to fail, that won't let bad news ruin my day, and I'm fully ready to give university my best shot.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admission to the University of California?
essays.essay:
I've been raised in a suburban bubble my whole entire life, with hills rolling behind my house and conformity being the coolest thing to do. A stroll in the school halls resembles walking through a herd of sheep, same shirt, same shoes, same mentality about success, that it only comes at the top floor of a business or in a doctor's white lab coat.

It's easy to get lost in what you think you want and what everybody else wants.

When I go to college I'm determined to uncover my genuine interests and aspirations that weren't passed down to me from my environment or my fellow classmates in school. I don't want to experience conformity, but instead individuality.

There are dozens of whims I wish to indulge.

I want to try different jobs, maybe a barista or at a register. I want to learn new things, like how to sew or how to cook something other than a pop-tart. I want to participate in different courses, perhaps biology or economics. I want to become more independent, through buying my own groceries or doing my own laundry. I want to drink coffee because I actually have to study late and not because I want to fit in.

I stand out as a candidate because I'm open to change and growth.

I plan on experiencing as much as I can throughout college, to help me morph into a person I'm proud of with passions I'm confident in. As a student I'm going to utilize all the resources the University has to offer, from the wide selection of classes to the well-educated staff to the diverse clubs scattered across campus. As a person I welcome the inevitable mistakes, seeing it as an opportunity to grow, getting to know my strengths and weaknesses.

I seek to reach out and explore as many opportunities within my grasp. I seek to put effort in every class I take, every word I write, every whim I succeed in, every setback I face, seeing it as a chance to develop as a student, and an individual.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
"Checkmate!" Those were the words my dad said after playing an intense match of chess when I was eight—the first time I ever challenged him as a new player. However, my competitiveness pushed me never to give up; so at family gatherings, I sat beside him studying the board, where I noticed how strategically and meticulously everyone moved their pieces, learning that progress is earned move by move.

As I watched more games, I learned about "zugzwang," a position where you must move even though any move will worsen your situation. I've encountered this in life, as Math 3 became my greatest zugzwang: averaging low B's in every test. I often found myself stuck, drowning in numbers, and my confidence was exponentially decreasing. I was embarrassed to ask for help, feeling like everyone around me understood something I didn't. But chess had already taught me that freezing never solves anything. So I began treating math like a match I refused to lose. I broke down problems step-by-step and attended office hours to review my mistakes, just like I reviewed lost games with my dad, with an open mind to feedback. Slowly, linear patterns emerged. My confidence grew, and I began averaging A's on tests. For the first time, I felt capable of accomplishing anything. I even started to be open to out-of-the-box ideas during group activities, and it worked.

At sixteen, after years of practice, I rechallenged my dad again. When I finally said "Checkmate," it wasn't the victory that mattered–it was realizing how far I'd come from the kid who once froze at the sight of a math problem.

This is the mindset I will bring to the UC community. I ask questions, collaborate, and keep going even when the next step feels foreign. I've learned that growth comes from taking risks through trial and error, testing different outcomes to see what works. Whether I'm facing a tough exam or a moment of uncertainty, I will do what chess taught me: be assertive, reflect on errors, and make the best move that helps me thrive–one step at a time.

essays.prompt: Beyond what has already been shared in your application, what do you believe makes you stand out as a strong candidate for admissions to the University of California?
essays.essay:
In writing this essay, I deeply reflected on some of my greatest attributes that would make me an outstanding candidate for admission to the University of California. However, there was one issue: I found myself inadvertently filtering only the best qualities that make me an ideal candidate while ignoring the qualities that truly define who I am. Keeping that in mind, my honest answer is that I am indecisive. My parents would also wholeheartedly agree that they raised a child that always seems to have a shifting mind. I change my mind all the time on just about everything. Even in answering these prompts about who I am, I changed my mind about the topic more times than probably should have.

However, I'm slowly beginning to change my mind again - about how I choose to label myself. I remember reading an old Forbes article titled, "Jeff Bezos On How To Change Your Mind", which weighed in on the importance of being open-minded. This was the same day that I started my job at State Farm and I remember reading the article three times - not only because Jeff Bezos is a great example to follow, but mainly because he recognized the better side of being "indecisive".

This article, while insignificant at first, prompted me to reevaluate how I describe myself.

Given this opportunity to revisit the prompt, I consider myself to be open-minded rather than indecisive. I firmly believe that being open-minded makes me more than just the ideal candidate for admission - it makes me an ideal learner. For starters, I genuinely appreciate the constructive feedback from peer reviews and I especially love collaborative projects that involve long discussions and intermingling of ideas and opinions. It's an exciting experience to work with others because it often allows me to think beyond what I know - after all, I know that being self-reliant in school has its limitations on my intellectual growth. But above all, I believe that being open-minded has given me the perfect balance of optimism and confidence that I need to succeed in college.

essays.prompt: Letter of continued interest submitted after being waitlisted at UCLA (no formal prompt printed in the document; the letter reaffirms interest and updates the school on recent accomplishments).
essays.essay:
Besides the allure of the city, when I lived in Los Angeles, it was the beginning of a dream. Arriving as a young child from India, UCLA was the first college I had ever heard about. Despite my young age, I was entranced, telling my parents, “This is where I will study one day.” Unfortunately, we had to move away from Los Angeles, but that dream never left me—lingering in the back of my mind, a constant reminder of the exciting journey in front of me. Now, as I reminisce, I realize that LA wasn’t just a brief chapter in my life but the foundation of a lifelong journey.

Since submitting my application, I’ve been fully immersed in the field of robotics. I am currently developing an open-source software robot pathfinding algorithm, a project that embodies the principles of Samueli Computer Science. This project reflects my passion for computer science and showcases UCLA’s emphasis on innovative and impactful solutions. I noticed that many FTC teams globally struggled with reliable robot navigation, prompting me to create BeepBeep. This library incorporates efficient PID and motion-profiling algorithms, ensuring smooth and precise trajectory following. Through BeepBeep, I also demonstrated my communication and teamwork skills by collaborating with another FTC team, essential traits at UCLA. While this algorithm is not publicly released to all teams, it is implemented by a team that advanced to the international level. This experience has reinforced my dedication to making meaningful contributions to the field and has prepared me to thrive in UCLA’s innovative environment.

My experience with the BeepBeep project has spearheaded my own team’s success, allowing us to perform at a state level. One of my proudest moments has been leading my FTC team to build the highest-scoring robot in our region, earning the highest ranking and winning first place in the Inspire award—an award that showcases greatness in all aspects including programming, robot design, and outreach just to name a few. These achievements not only reflect my dedication but also fuel my desire to continue pursuing computer science and software engineering.

Looking ahead, my goal is to translate my passion into a professional career in Computer Science. UCLA is the ideal school for my journey, offering not only a rich academic environment but also entrepreneurial opportunities and alumni connections. Already planning for my future, I am in the process of acquiring the Amazon Web Services Cloud Practitioner certification, a crucial step for software engineers to gain essential knowledge applicable in professional environments. My proactivity prepares me for the academic rigor of UCLA and allows me to excel professionally.

I am truly thankful for the opportunity, allowing me to imagine myself as a Bruin. My commitment to UCLA is certain, and two months ago in February, I drove eight hours to visit my future school. Looking at the campus gave me momentary flashbacks from when I was five years old. I can envision myself watching the USC rivalry game (go Bruins!) with my friends already at the school, studying in the Engineering VI building, and accomplishing my dream of starting a business. This fall, I hope to join the UCLA community and return back to my true home.

essays.promptLabel: Two things that undo each other
essays.prompt: Exponents and square roots, pencils and erasers, beta decay and electron capture. Name two things that undo each other and explain why both are necessary. (~550 words)
essays.essay:
In California rain is like a blessing. Even as an atheist, I would be on my knees and thank the gods for bringing such refreshing weather to where I live. But just in a couple of days, the clouds would clear and poof, the water was gone like it was never even there all thanks to the amazing phenomenon known as evaporation. In all honesty, I am sick of this simple weather Californians are used to. Sure it may be of great pleasure to those who desire to live here, but I cannot stand the repeated cycle of sunshine to cloudy skies. Nothing in between. Yet the occasional rain is always of great pleasure to me. Of course, rain doesn't last forever (not unless you are stationed in Seattle) and evaporation will happily take place.

Well, imagine a world where evaporation does not occur. How would the planet look? By doing some very simple research the answer is clear. Without evaporation, we'd have no clouds. Without clouds, we'd have no rain. Finally, with no rain, the consequences begin to snowball. First goes our water vapor then our earthly flora, and at some point, all life will die. We'd have no plants, no animals, no life on our planet Earth. Our once green and blue world will turn into a desert with an ocean somewhere in the mess. Not a very pretty sight in my opinion. However, with evaporation present in our everlasting cycle of water, we can flourish as a society and a world. Oftentimes the water that is processed can be from thousands of years ago. We'd be drinking our ancestor's water. However, the idea of drinking water from another person who has passed it through their body is a much more unsettling fact I'd like to not think of. That is, in simple terms, why we are still alive today, but of course, there is more depth to it with other factors influencing the direction of society. Without either of those phenomena present, we'd be nothing but bare lands. Human life would cease to exist. There would be no University of Chicago to attend.

Even with the known process of rain and evaporation, the facts of where our water originates from, and how the world would be today if water was stripped away, the odds of a climate change catastrophe such as that are low. Whenever it rains in California, it's a blessing. The little droplets of water crashing onto the grass of my dying yard remind me of the duality of the world. For a few days, water stays in puddles or gets soaked up by all the soil, then once the sun comes out the water fades like it was never there in the first place. However, its effect on my world is apparent. The dry grass suddenly has little beads of yellow sprouting from who knows where. The outside world is pungent with the smell of fresh rain. The air around me is cold, yet comforting like there was just a pleasant presence just around. Yes, something was there once, but now it's gone. That is the most important principle of life. There will always be something a part of your life, and someday it could leave out of your control. Change is the everlasting cycle of life.

essays.prompt: How does the University of Chicago, as you know it now, satisfy your desire for a particular kind of learning, community, and future? Please address with some specificity your own wishes and how they relate to UChicago.
essays.essay:
Hogwarts. That is all I could think of when I first laid eyes upon UChicago’s Harper Library. Like discovering my house on the official Harry Potter Fan Club website, the grand and brightly lit hall constructed with mahogany wood called to me, enticing me to find my place amongst itself. As my college counselor continued on with their lecture, I daydreamed about the campus and wondered if UChicago could turn me into a wizard of medicine.

It did for Roger W. Sperry, an exceptional psychobiologist who won a Nobel Prize for uncovering the distinct functions of each hemisphere in the human brain. Upon hearing this fact in my 6th grade science class, I was utterly confused. The proposal of such an abstract ideology intrigued me, continuing to plague my mind for years until I finally conducted research on Sperry. Granted, my research was quite unintentional as I found my answer in a “Life at UChicago” video. In the video, a university student explained that life at UChicago was unique. She claimed that the institution’s students constantly questioned the world, turning even the smallest conversations into deep discussions.

At UChicago, Sperry found himself amongst the sea of culture created by these brilliant minds. The education he received was not only supplemented by the constant circulation of ideas, but rather synonymous with it. Harboring these values, Sperry was granted the opportunity to discover greatness for the benefit of society. This is the education I seek. A rigorous academic course amplified by the people of UChicago. A style of scholarship that has been propelling my capabilities even before I had heard of Sperry’s work. From making vinegar and baking soda volcanos in grade school to running Interact food drives in high school, I have found that collaboration often creates the best results.

Before this discovery, I wrestled to find fulfillment in my work. In my history classes, I’d struggle to understand the mistakes I made on tests and volunteering as a single individual felt pointless. By honing my craft of forming interpersonal relationships, I have come to understand the profoundness of learning, contributing, and working with people, a resource that can only be enriched by the unique facet of UChicago’s population. It is a culture that has been formed through selectivity in the prompts I answer currently, the rigorous nature of UChicago academic programs, and the beloved Hyde Park neighborhood - which houses the Museum of Science and Industry (Something I’ve been eyeing for a while now).

Each factor filters and compresses the school like creating shapes from PlayDoh. The beautiful art that manipulates itself cycles back to the sorting hat in my mind. The further I learn about the UChicago lifestyle, the more inclined I am to devotion. In my research, I have continued to find endless career supplemental programs that intrigue me. Particularly, the Pritzker’s School of Medicine’s student-led programs, such as the Asian Pacific American Medical Students Association (APAMSA) and Geriatrics Interest Group (GIG), offer me the ability to connect with fellow students of medicine, and spark my own deep discussions. APAMSA will deepen my understanding on the power of healing and grant me the opportunity to meet inspiring people. On the other hand, GIG will offer insight into the geriatrics field, a rather undeveloped branch of medicine that I believe needs to focus more on quality of life studies.

As a student who yearns to master the magic of medicine, I have decided that there is no better place to do so than at UChicago. Its diverse population alongside its rigorous academic course and clubs inspire me, egging me to discover more of its beauty. While I know UChicago cannot teach me healing spells like Hogwarts, I look forward to every moment I spend on campus, as it will be magical.

essays.prompt: Why did you apply to each of the academic programs listed on your application? This personal statement should provide additional information not already referenced in your application. (500 words)
essays.essay:
In trying to answer this question, I tried for hours to reflect on the things that really push me forward - not just in the academic department but also in what drives me, as a human being, with dreams of somehow trying to make our world a better place to live in.

In choosing a major, I have never had any doubt in my mind that Neuroscience would always be the way for me to go. With my interest in biology and psychology, coupled with the fact that it truly is an interesting time for women to be working in both healthcare and research, there never were anything else that came close to this option. In a way, I am very excited to see how much I can challenge myself in the understanding of the human biological condition and, in turn, be challenged by the University of Cincinnati's very promising courses and timely, fruitful lectures.

As for applying to minor in Medicinal Sciences, it had been an easier choice. Coming from California where healthcare laws and medicinal application had always been in the news, prompting numerous debates both outside and inside the classroom set-up, I have always seen my current and future self as someone whose endeavors must always be in service of advancing our understanding of what works in curing many diseases, alleviating growing discomforts, and wanting to make things easier for people to have access to proper treatment.

When speaking about my readiness to success in the field, I always turn back into my recent experiences. I believe I have laid good leadership groundwork as a Research Officer in the Neuroscience Club at my high school and as a specialist in the fields of neuroscience even as a high school student. As I delved deeper into the medical community through my research, I recognized the prevalence of problem-solving in every situation. I also know (and feel) that I have never truly shined brighter than when I am in a proper research environment, trying to understand nerve and brain functions.

As I shadowed two family physicians, I realized how problem-solving has played a role in finding the cause of every symptom. Specifically, in one situation, a patient came in with shoulder and back pain. While he believed the source of the issue came from his COPD, the physician was suspicious of this judgment. The physician was able to implement his problem-solving skills to diagnose the pain with ease, and he concluded that the pain was muscular in origin since the pain was more associated with soreness and achiness, as opposed to a tightness, which is the type of pain associated with COPD.

While being a physician requires a strong background in science, it also requires a sense of analytical thinking. When I saw this action first-hand, I found my passion for medicine more cemented, and I would very much like to dedicate the rest of my academic and future professional pursuits into it by being an undergraduate at the University of Cincinnati.

essays.promptLabel: Most meaningful commitment outside the classroom
essays.prompt: Please provide more details on your most meaningful commitment outside of the classroom while in high school and explain why it was meaningful. This could be related to an extracurricular activity, work, volunteering, an academic activity, family responsibility, or any other non-classroom activity. (250 words)
essays.essay:
Taking out the trash. Vacuuming the car. Mowing the lawn. These were the chores I dreaded most in high school.

The garbage reeked in the winter and the smell lingered onto my clothes; the car’s tight cracks between the seats collected dirt and crumbs I could never reach, which drove me crazy; and that old mower that hasn’t retired, always kicked grass and dirt on my skin, leaving me itchy. For a long time, I saw these chores as punishment and my patience grew thinner by the day. But I knew my parents always had good intentions, and I eventually realized that they were simply teaching me to show up, even when I didn’t want to.

These chores taught me countless life skills, but the two that stood out are accountability and hard work. I learned accountability the week I skipped taking out the trash, only to be greeted impolitely with more than double the stench the next time around. I learned hard work every time I had to mow the lawn, no matter how thick the summer air was and how much grass stuck to my legs, the job needed to be done.

Now, I’m committed to my chores. It’s become a routine and my way of giving back to my parents for all they’ve poured into me. Being able to take a little weight off their heavy shoulders is the least I can do while shaping myself to be a more responsible individual.

essays.promptLabel: A book that impacted you (middle-to-high-school transition)
essays.prompt: The transition from middle to high school is a key time for students as they reach new levels of both academic and personal discovery. Please share a book (novel, non-fiction, etc.) that had a serious impact on you during this time. Please focus more on why this book made an impact on you and less on the plot/theme of the book itself (we are not looking for a book report). (200-350 words)
essays.essay:
Money makes the world go around. It is related to everything we do. Ever since I was a kid, I’ve had a rigid view of money: you make money, you spend money, and you save money for when you retire.

When I got my first bank account during my 8th-grade summer, my dad wanted me to read a book. It was called “Rich Dad Poor Dad” by Robert Kiyosaki. Throughout the summer, I read this book, learning a new lesson every chapter, shifting the way I viewed money and society as a whole.

It continued to pique my interest in the field of finance, but most importantly, it helped me decide which sector I want to pursue in finance: private equity. When I was younger, I wanted to be a stockbroker or in corporate finance, but this book made me think about “how can I buy this company?” instead of “how can I work for this company?” Those words changed my life for the better.

What stood out most wasn’t just the idea of making money work for me; it was realizing that my life didn’t have to follow a traditional script. I even began looking at companies differently, asking myself what made them valuable and how someone could grow or restructure them. That curiosity pushed me to read more, explore online business models, and even have deeper conversations with my dad about his own financial experiences.

This led me to get an internship at Global SVF, a student venture firm. There, I had the opportunity to put my skills in action. While it wasn’t fully investing in companies, as that requires a higher level of education that I plan on pursuing in the future, I got to allocate certain amounts of money to nonprofit organizations and see them use this money to create a real impact. That pushed my love for this field even further.

One thing that I can confidently say is that this book didn’t just teach me about money; it helped pave a path for me, one that I plan on pursuing.

essays.prompt: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from UIUC and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them.
essays.essay:
Taking part in UIUC’s winning and dedicated mindset will only positively translate to my career. Formula One has transcended beyond its entertainment value in my life. I have grown to understand the mechanics behind the cars and the vitality of computer engineering in them.

After fulfilling my dream of participating in the collegiate version of F1, I will venture into the real world. Initially, joining or creating a start-up focused on enabling robots to navigate complex, realistic environments effortlessly is the vision.

The university's robust ecosystem of research centers, entrepreneurial support, and diverse network of like-minded individuals will provide me with the resources and mentorship needed to realize this dream.

This specialization process also originates from UIUC’s in-depth machine learning catalogue. Once specialized, I dream of working in an F1 garage, winning with the Mercedes logo on my shirt.

essays.prompt: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from UIUC and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them. (150 words)
essays.essay:
Since I was in the third grade, I looked up to Bill Gates because of his intellect and entrepreneurial skills. I’ve had a plan to create a revolutionary application that will benefit the globe in college with my two best friends. And while this may seem like an impossible task, with my resilience and resourcefulness, I can achieve my dream at UIUC.

At the Grainger College of Engineering, courses like Software Engineering and Cloud Networking will teach me skills that are vital to application development, bolstering my current experience with cloud technology and programming languages. Through student organizations such as Founders Illinois Entrepreneurs, I will have the opportunity to nurture my basic ideas into practical applications that will be crucial in paving my path toward starting my own business. At UIUC, I can connect with students through the various programs and advance my technical knowledge through the sophisticated curriculum.

essays.prompt: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from UIUC and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them. (150 words)
essays.essay: After UIUC, I plan to start in Chicago as a private equity or investment banking analyst, then move into a leadership role where I can contribute to scaling growth at companies. Finance at UIUC is the right major that will prepare me for this industry because it trains the exact skills that I need as an analyst – valuation, financial modeling, acquisitions, and general market analysis. This will help me underwrite deals and share investment ideas with reason and numbers. Beyond the core classes, I’ll be able to learn about early-stage investments, growth equity, and specialized skills for deal structuring, all of which I’m keenly interested to learn more about. These courses, paired with student investment organizations and Chicago’s strong ties to the financial hub will give me the experience and network I need to break into the private equity space.

essays.prompt: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from UIUC and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them. (150 words, Undeclared Engineering)
essays.essay:
You can't have a game without purpose. So what purpose does a game serve if you are face to face with a blank screen? Engineering is the solution that I hope to use to bring life onto the screen.

From software engineering to graphic development, the possibilities are broad. Game development has room for both coding and artistic creativity, which is the greatest pair since root beer and vanilla ice cream. I hope that UIUC's phenomenal engineering program will provide me with the skills I need to paint a path towards a career in game development, and more importantly, give greater purpose and impact to the development skills I have honed over the years.

My ultimate goal is to become a lead in developing a game from scratch and I believe UIUC will be the rocket fuel to help me reach the stars.

essays.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else.
essays.essay:
Why did I have to finish the first assignment so quickly?

I interned at Photon Commerce under the mentorship of the Engineering Lead. I had finished my onboarding task relatively fast and was ready to go on to bigger and better things—or so I thought.

My first project was creating a complete documentation of open-source data labeling platforms that use advanced regular expressions to annotate financial documents properly. While she was always willing to assist in any way possible, I wanted to prove my mettle.

After the installation process, the instructions fell out, and I was left alone. After stalling two weeks of precious time, I went to my final resort—my mentor. I told her my problem. Her reaction was completely opposite of what I had expected.

Why would she purposefully give me a flawed task?

To help me understand. Often, I may need to look beyond myself.

essays.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else. (150 words)
essays.essay:
During the summer after Freshman year, I joined a social media startup called Revoteen. Writing efficient code and deploying it to the cloud was an astonishing experience. I delved deeper into the inner workings of JavaScript and learned about frameworks such as Next.js. In fact, working at Revoteen is the reason JavaScript is my favorite language today.

I learned the process of shipping code to production and wrote effective tests to ensure that the code was not erroneous. It brought me joy each time I saw the “Deploy Successful” message as I knew that my feature contributed to the success of the application.

Revoteen’s charismatic work environment, coupled with their desire to develop creative solutions was the reason I became so attached to the company. Each day, I was ecstatic to work on a feature. I was determined to fix any bug or error that stood in my way. It taught me essential skills that will undoubtedly help me in my career as a programmer.

essays.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else. (150 words)
essays.essay:
The Technology Student Association, not to be confused with the airport TSA, holds a national competition each year where students compete to develop technical skills by creating applications to solve real-world challenges.

During the pandemic, my friends and I identified the problem of online lectures, which made it hard for students to focus for extended periods of time. We worked day and night to develop an application that converts audio recordings into transcribed summaries and keywords that are automatically linked to suggested YouTube videos and websites.

We faced many challenges along the way and gained more experience utilizing Flask and applying NLP computational logic. The thrill of adding features, seeing it compile on the first try, and resolving GitHub merge conflicts one at a time made me fall in love with programming again. Our hard work was worth it in the end when we placed 9th in the nation.

essays.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else. (150 words)
essays.essay: This past summer, I interned at Global SVF, a student venture firm, and witnessed firsthand how a small investment can have a significant impact. As part of a five-person analyst team, I conducted a SWOT analysis of the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship (NFTE) to assess its financial and business metrics, determining whether it was a suitable investment opportunity for Global SVF. We summarized our findings in a business proposal and created a pitch deck to support our recommendation to invest in NFTE. The panel of executives at Global SVF was impressed with our depth of research into the NPO, and after successfully defending our proposition, our proposal was approved. This experience not only sparked my passion for finance but also gave me a tangible understanding of how proper deployment of capital can transform organizations, ultimately inspiring me to pursue a career in private equity where I can drive meaningful impact.

essays.prompt: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else. (150 words)
essays.essay:
My experiences at UCLA's Game Development program opened my eyes to a new digital world of possibilities and a spark in the field of engineering.

Before day one of the program, I had only touched the surface of software engineering and robotics. Once I had entered my first lecture, a flood of excitement carried my once little interests into a fixation. I had learned more about the development of games in those 9 days than I had over several years. After the program, I spent the rest of my summer learning JavaScript and HTML Style CSS by developing my very own video game.

I hope by plunging into the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's engineering programs, I can intertwine this new passion with a future career in the field of game development and AI.

essays.prompt: Everyone belongs to many different communities and/or groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interest, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong, and describe that community and your place within it. (minimum 100 words/maximum 300 words)
essays.essay:
I was ecstatic when I was accepted into the Science Olympiad team. Ecstatic, but only for a moment. All my hard work preparing for tryouts and competing against 120 people had worked out at that moment. But once the initial euphoria depleted, all that remained was panic.

Panic - I had made it in front of 90 other students. Ninety students who could have done better. Panic - what if I let my team down?

But once the team met for its first meeting, the panic dissipated. This community was supportive, and the seniors empathized with my feelings. I cherished every moment; we studied, went on tangents, and returned to studying. I remember conversations on pendulums and leap seconds going to discussions about people who are born in leap years, I remember working on anagrams at 11 P.M. with light music playing and storytelling. These otherwise insignificant occasions meant everything to me. We’d laugh about physics and cry about codebusters, but it was always perfect.

Until these partners graduated, the countless hours spent grinding with them were invaluable. Each partner graduating to their bright future was bittersweet; they had become true friends. But it was our time to step up.

As those years passed, my friend and I assumed the new leadership roles in this new team. My friend, the president, took upon the role model position and set an example. I became the relatable senior: the person others approach for questions without feeling judged. I helped in ways my previous partners helped me by being a mentor and, more importantly, a friend.

Together, we worked to maintain the collaborative and welcoming spirit that defines our community. Science Olympiad, where fun and stress collide to form everlasting connections. Connections that I will continue to cherish and hope the new members also cherish.

essays.prompt: Everyone belongs to many different communities and/or groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interest, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong, and describe that community and your place within it. (minimum 100 words/maximum 300 words)
essays.essay:
"Can I get a nine? Nine! Can I get a two? Two! Can I get a five? Five! We're dialed!" That is one of the team chants that we start every high school varsity tennis meet with, with the digits representing our area code and our team mimicking dialing it on imaginary cell phones. Kids, coaches and parents laugh when they see the puzzled looks of our opponents.

The team is all about having fun, but also being competitive, with us winning the league two years ago. We support each other and 'fair play' has been drilled into us by our coach from day one.

The community has expanded tennis beyond high school. For example, one of my volunteer activities, Impactful Tennis, consists of some of my club and high school tennis friends providing tennis lessons with the proceeds going to a good cause. This past summer, I was the team leader and we raised $4500 for Meals on Wheels.

Being part of the team has helped me grow as a person. For instance, each team member gets a nickname based on our behavior and personalities. They called me "The Conversationalist" during my freshman year, jokingly, because I did not say much. Now, I am "The Conversationalist" because I have become the chatty guy. I was very happy to be voted as Team Captain last year, not so much for the title, but because it showed that the team trusts me.

Although this year will be the last year of varsity tennis, I fully intend to stay engaged. I'm very optimistic about the chances of that happening. We even have an extensive group text consisting of current and former team members with the former team members celebrating big rivalry wins from all across the country.

essays.prompt: Everyone belongs to many different communities and/or groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interest, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong, and describe that community and your place within it. (300 words)
essays.essay:
From the moment I played my first note, middle C, I immediately connected with the piano. I had discovered a small branch leading to a special community. Driven by my curiosity to explore this branch further, I developed my skills as a pianist through weekly lessons, recitals, and exams.

As I met diverse pianists over the years, I grew increasingly excited, realizing I was now a part of this vibrant and melodious community. We shared a distinct language that only other musicians could understand in this realm. Every time I listened to classical music, I could hear another pianist from this community echoing their emotions to me. I felt the urge to replicate these sentiments, hoping to propel them forward.

The first time I experienced a true connection to this community was during an event when a volunteer requested assistance reading piano notes. A surge of euphoria coursed through me as I rushed to her side, passionately explaining the notes. The radiant comprehension in her eyes mirrored the same luminous grin that once graced my face when I started learning. During this moment, it felt like we had transcended into the musical realm, where the black and white keys allowed us to communicate beyond words. This wholesome interaction reassured me of the power of music to connect individuals from completely different backgrounds.

The piano has linked me with a family distinct from mine who have been a valuable source of learning and inspiration, fueling my desire to create music through the impromptu style. They allowed me to express my inner thoughts and emotions through the eighty-eight key wonder. I aspire to pass the knowledge I've gained to young pianists who also want to learn. I hope that I can bring them into this community–this family.

essays.prompt: Upload a document or artifact that represents something significant about your life to show your learning in action. Describe how your artifact demonstrates your learning in action. (approximately 250 words)
essays.essay:
Despite playing the piano for 9 years, I'm really not that good. Based on my crazy hair, people think I'm Mozart, but looks can be deceiving. When I sit down to practice, I may struggle to make sense of what feels like an endless sea of notes, dynamics, and tempos. No prodigy here.

Despite not being a natural talent, I stuck with it. During hard moments, when I just wouldn't be able to nail a piece, I would tell myself that I can do it, reflecting back on pieces that I once thought were impossible but easy now. I don't tell myself: "this is easy, there won't be any pain" (we refer to piano as "pain-o" in our family) because I can't lie to myself. Instead I say: "this WON'T be easy, but I've overcome before so I will this time also". What really helps that internal dialogue is to realize WHY I want to master my current challenge. It is not to become a virtuoso, but it is so that I can enjoy playing more.

It also doesn't help that I have hyperhidrosis. When I'm nervous, my hands sweat severely, resulting in a very slippery set of keys. As soon as you tell yourself "don't be nervous" you get really nervous. Instead, I tell myself to be ok having sweaty hands. Worst thing that can happen is that I won't receive an award. Big deal. Move on.

I just like playing piano and I persevered.

essays.prompt: Upload an artifact that represents something significant about your life and shows how you've put learning into action. This could be related to something inside or outside of the classroom (like an extracurricular accomplishment you're particularly proud of). The goal is to give you the chance to showcase a unique aspect of yourself.
essays.essay: “Cars go vroom!” That was one of the first things I said as a baby. Since then, my love for cars hasn’t changed. I love everything about cars, from the way they look to the way they sound. My grandma got me a set of Hot Wheels from India, and those became my most prized possession. My favorite of this sentimental set is the Lamborghini Huracan LP 620-2 Super Trofeo. When I brought them to the U.S, I couldn’t just let them sit there and collect dust, so I built this garage. This garage allowed me to implement everything I’ve learned about cars into this one piece. From the way the garage opens to how cars get loaded onto a trailer, I wanted to put all that into action with this piece. This was the greatest representation of my creativity and ability to engineer something out of imagination in the 5th grade.

essays.prompt: Choose a current event or issue in your community and discuss the business implications. Propose a solution that incorporates business principles or practices. The review panel will look for creativity, drawing connections, and originality. Your response should be limited to approximately 500 words.
essays.essay:
As a kid, I spent most of my time outside, playing with friends. Every day on my short but fun scooter commute to our hangout spot, cars would zoom past me, going in excess of the speed limit. It was extremely frightening for my 8-year-old self. My friends had the same experiences, but with their bikes, feeling the sharp cold air and engine noises zoom past us. My friends and I brought this to our parents' attention, and it was the star topic for every gathering. Every event, parents would talk for hours, complaining about all the people speeding, and that those drivers are putting the kids' lives at risk. Everyone knew about the good-old speed bump, but that was not only inconvenient for the drivers who actually followed the speed limit, it often damaged cars’ suspensions.

To solve this issue, I think neighborhoods should implement speed bumps filled with non-Newtonian fluid. These speed bumps, which have already been implemented in many places in Europe, contain a liquid that hardens when sufficient impact is felt. This liquid is covered by a hard-wearing plastic tube that is flexible, so that the speed bump doesn’t break.
