With this solution, I can vary the quantity and chemical makeup of the fluid so that I can personalize it towards the speed limit of every community, and this will provide the resistance required to slow these drivers down.

My target audience would be neighborhood HOAs and the government. This business would operate under a B2G and B2B model, where I would offer installation and maintenance contracts for residential streets and school zones. Initially, I would focus on a pilot program that would be in local neighborhoods. By partnering with HOAs, I could install these speed bumps and collect data on average vehicle speed after implementation. This data would show the effectiveness of this product, which I would pitch to city governments and traffic safety boards to secure bigger contracts.

The revenue generation would come from 3 main streams. Firstly, the price of the product and installation fees that I would charge to HOAs and local governments. Secondly, communities would pay quarterly fees for fluid replacement, maintenance, cleaning, and monitoring to make sure everything is working smoothly. Thirdly, I would sell the data I get from these speed bumps to local planners or insurers, or really anyone who wants it to improve neighborhood safety.

The value proposition of this product is based on the basis of balancing safety, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. Traditional speed bumps often frustrate drivers, increase vehicle wear, and can even lead to noise complaints, costing cities in repairs and reputation. In contrast, these speed bumps made from non-Newtonian fluid reward safe driving and keep drivers accountable. This represents a modern approach that aligns with the recent growing demand for smart infrastructure in communities. In the long term, scaling this concept could involve licensing the technology to road construction companies to turn this small startup into a nationwide safety innovation.

essays.promptLabel: Business solution to a community issue
essays.prompt: Choose a current event or issue in your community and discuss the business implications. Propose a solution that incorporates business principles or practices. The review panel will look for creativity, drawing connections, and originality. (approximately 500 words)
essays.essay:
COMMUNITY HOUSEKEEPING

Our neighborhood is peaceful and quiet. Not much happens on the outside but its inhabitants are a different story.

In my family, we're all busy. My brother and I are inundated with school work and after-school commitments while my parents work all day, a common story of families like ours. House chores are the icing on the cake, except not as enticing as the real thing. Quite the opposite, actually.

A short while ago, when our neighbors were visiting us, the adults vented about the never-ending daily housework. There was so much energy around this conversation, I could not help but listen. Like us, our neighbors struggled to find time to do it all, as they put it. Some had cleaning services that were too expensive, infrequent, or inconsistent. This was clearly a source of stress for many, at least for my focus of working parents and kids in my neighborhood. It was easy to see there was a common need and problem to solve. The business opportunity was there as these families were happy to buy back time for more important things in life. To solve this need, I came up with a solution: Community Housekeeping!

Community Housekeeping is a routine housekeeping service for groups of families that live in close proximity, like what you get in a hotel but designed for neighborhoods. When ten or more neighbors are on board, community housekeeping services are made available for a neighborhood. Households that are part of this program can pick one or two plans – basic or premium – and each come with a predetermined set of services.

Housekeeping services, as the name suggests, help with maintaining the house through routine cleanings and provide key benefits such as giving subscribers more time back to do things they actually enjoy and provide access to help when needed. Maybe the best way to define this offering is the ability to purchase relief and peace of mind, perfect not only for my family but others like us.

Community Housekeeping runs on a website and app, where choosing a plan and entering a six month contract is simple. The onboard experience should be no longer than your average chore around the home, 5 minutes tops. The business model relies on a subscription format for consistent revenue to feed the operating costs, and then advertising revenue as the platform and services grow. Over time, upgrades are made available to subscribers as new products roll out to add additional income.

For the business, geographic concentration and community-based offering is key to keep the costs down and profits high. Customer service, ensuring high quality service and trust are the cornerstones of the offering.

Facebook, Nextdoor and Instagram communities and advertising will help introduce and grow "Community Housekeeping" services along with neighbors telling each other. My street is the best candidate to start to offer this much-needed peace of mind service with a goal to spread the relief from one neighborhood to the next.

essays.prompt: Everyone belongs to many different communities and/or groups defined by (among other things) shared geography, religion, ethnicity, income, cuisine, interest, race, ideology, or intellectual heritage. Choose one of the communities to which you belong, and describe that community and your place within it.
essays.essay:
For my first birthday, I was photographed wearing a light pink and blue Hanbok. Seated on my dad's lap, I stared into the camera lens with a squint of confusion, and then came the bright flash - "Hana, dul, seht!" That was my first invitation to my Korean heritage.

Born and raised in a little town, I had little exposure to my Korean roots. My parents, being first and second generation Korean Americans, never had a slow moment in their busy lives to celebrate all the Korean traditions and holidays due to work. At home, it was just me and my halmeoni, the best grandmother I could ask for.

My grandmother is the link that infused me into the Korean community. She held many beliefs and laid the moral foundations that guided me into my teenage years. When she spoke, I could listen to her for days because I held so much respect for everything she's taught me. It's these days that I learned to hold great pride as a member of the Korean community.

I see myself as a tourist in my Korean community. Sometimes I feel tightly connected with my Korean community, making my grandmother proud; other times, I take small excursions where my grandmother reels me right back in. Though I broke a few rules here and there, my grandmother is the red string that ties me back to my roots.

I am forever grateful for her persistence in dressing me up in that Hanbok for all those years, and I can't wait to one day take her back to Korea, where she was taught the traditions of being a daughter under our family name. She truly is my "Seoulmate," and she is the reason that I have a place within the Korean community.

essays.promptLabel: Leaders and citizens who challenge the present
essays.prompt: At the University of Michigan, we are focused on developing leaders and citizens who will challenge the present and enrich the future. In your essay, share with us how you are prepared to contribute to these goals. This could include the people, places, experiences or aspirations that have shaped your journey and future plans. (300 words)
essays.essay:
Our world is riddled with many major issues. From climate concerns to economic disparities to the emergence of global health problems, there are simply more problems than we can tend to. But that’s also a problem because not all issues are represented equally, and that needs to change.

This problem motivated me to join Youth4Change, an organization dedicated to bringing awareness to issues, big or small, around the world. Unlike many nonprofits that focus on a single cause, our local branch brings awareness to a new topic each month, from rare types of cancers to global urbanization issues. Not only do we promote these causes through fundraisers, but we also leverage podcasts, public events, and social media for broad coverage. This mixed media approach gives us the best chance to solve problems, both niche and systemic.

This experience helped shape my belief that leadership isn’t about taking care of the biggest causes, but making sure that no issues are overlooked. I hope to bring the same relief to the Michigan community, whether it’s through collaborating on passion projects or joining initiatives like the Ginsberg Center. I hope to bring light to causes that may be ignored otherwise.

During my time at Michigan, I hope to one day start my own organization similar to Youth4Change. But even more, I hope to unite students not with a desire to solve one cause but a mission to solve problems that are worldwide and of all sizes. I want to bring people together from unique backgrounds and cultures, each with their own opinion on issues, to create a community of real impact. My goal is to address pressing problems while creating leaders who see the world's problems as an opportunity to make it better.

essays.prompt: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate College or School (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (minimum 100 words/maximum 550 words)
essays.essay:
The influence of computer science in the world is immense. Progress in the last century has altered how we think and conduct our daily routines and lives. Artificial intelligence, data science, machine learning, quantum, and algorithmic all stem from this ever-encompassing field of computer science. Besides these technical uses of this field, I love to see the combination of the digital and the elemental.

Our sweet, beautiful Earth is littered with forests and mountains but sophisticated with the man-made creations of asphalt. Spiraling lanes of asphalt, twisting around acres of land throughout the globe—23 thrilling Formula 1 races rotated amongst 34 countries featuring hundreds of thousands of fans and 20 machines built to near perfection.

The College of Engineering and the University of Michigan understand the beauty of sophisticated machinery through the number 1 American Formula SAE team. The idea of joining the Red Bull of the collegiate circuit makes me nervous but also excited.

The emphasis on practical experiences, hands-on learning, and knowledge in sophisticated branches of computer science are all present in the education provided. Besides the diverse range of machine learning and artificial intelligence courses provided at this College and the opportunity to work on industrial-grade robots, is the University of Michigan’s compelling dedication to education.

During the fiscal year of 2021, $1.7 billion was spent. It is truly an absurd number; however, the respect towards technology at this university is highlighted. Compelling and intricate research into the algorithmic aspects of efficiently controlling autonomy in higher-end robots could be implemented in their leading racecar.

Besides racing, the Wolverine loves collaboration. Breaking barriers at full speed sounds exhilarating. Racing is a lifestyle, and it is not the lifestyle of the Bay Area. Michigan's passion for sports is evident through the electric football and basketball environments I have had the luxury of experiencing during March Madness. This constant learning loop with adrenaline will only fuel my eagerness for Computer Science, and such energy can perfectly be found in this community.

The variety of hands-on curriculum offered here goes back to the collaboration and diversity I have yet to experience. As a high schooler in my hometown, I have had the experience of working with only a limited amount of people. Broadening this network through courses that mandate working together and learning from others mirrors having two drivers on the same F1 team. A dream duo is a young driver that feeds off of the knowledge and expertise of a veteran driver.

This opportunity, knowledge, and guidance will lead me to my ultimate goal: working in an F1 garage as the lead engineer in the aerodynamics division, winning with the Mercedes logo on my shirt.

essays.prompt: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate College or School (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (550 words)
essays.essay:
What stands out to me about the University of Michigan, Ross is the way classroom teachings can be applied to real-world finance. The culture at Ross isn’t just studying cases or gaining knowledge; it's actually running funds, evaluating companies, and getting a taste of what it's like working in business alongside my peers and industry professionals. The flexibility in coursework allows me to pair general business courses with interdisciplinary options like finance, technology, and entrepreneurship. Looking past the academics offered by every school, Ross’s ambitious community and strong alumni network in high finance and banking will help me find my people who will challenge me to achieve my dreams.

The dream that I hope to achieve after attending Ross and some job experience is launching my own private equity firm that uses modern technology to streamline processes and increase automation. Currently, many PE firms rely too much on Leveraged buyouts, undervalue ESG and impact; they value companies in a very rigid and exclusive manner, and fail to integrate technology at an advanced level. Those are all problems I hope to solve with my firm.

Even though Ross’s collaborative community and ambitious culture provide me with the foundation, it’s the curriculum and organizations that will help me reimagine what my modern private equity firm could look like.

Courses like FIN 427 will teach me how to integrate technology into this firm by applying Python to data-driven investment models. To build on this technical information and foundation, FIN 428 will help deepen my understanding of developing financial infrastructure, which is crucial for modern investing. Both of these courses will help bring automation, efficiency, market analysis, and innovation to my private equity firm. Furthermore, FIN 418 will allow me to explore global capital flows, market microstructure, and strategic portfolio allocation, helping me find value in companies so I can identify and capitalize on opportunities. This strategic thinking bridges perfectly toward entrepreneurial investing approaches, which I will strengthen in FIN 425. Here, I will connect the analytical skills and strategies with the actual human side of investing, where I would examine venture capital, deal structuring, and exit strategies that balance social and financial returns. Together, these courses will provide me with the intellectual knowledge to start this firm.

Just the knowledge isn’t enough; I have to put this knowledge into action so I can learn the ins and outs of a private equity firm and develop those tangible skills needed to run a successful firm. That's where the Wolverine Venture Fund and the Social Venture Fund will come into play. They will give me firsthand experience sourcing deals, conducting due diligence, and presenting to investment committees. I’m eager to join the Michigan Private Equity and Venture Capital Club, which will sharpen my technical modeling and strategic thinking through LBO competitions and consulting projects with local firms. These opportunities ensure I graduate not just with classroom knowledge, but with the confidence and practical expertise to build a forward-thinking PE firm.

Ultimately, Ross offers more than just a degree in Business Administration; it provides the interdisciplinary mindset, hands-on practice, and forward-looking vision I need to reimagine private equity. By blending rigorous technical skills with ethical, transparent practices, I will be prepared not only to enter banking but to eventually launch a transformative PE firm.

essays.prompt: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate College or School (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (550 words)
essays.essay:
Though my father is Christian, and my mother's side follows Buddhism, I find myself as someone who hasn't had the time to explore or take religion in depth. However, there is one Bible I am willing to follow, and that is the "Bible for Machine Learning," also known as Elements of Statistical Learning. Reading this 700-page passage of knowledge reflected the interests I've been searching for. This is my following.

The overall summary of the book consists of the main topics about how statistics can be applied to many different fields of work, from agriculture to economics and even to medicine. I was met with so many options and possibilities as to what statistics can bring to the table. Let there be light, he said, light in my room so I can read this gem from the core of mathematics. Not only did this ignite my interest in statistics, but it fueled the flame for me to explore mathematics as a career. Exploring data science and the digital field has always been an ever-present enjoyment in my life. Not only did it brew a new hobby, but it polished skills I had left in the dust from a long time ago. As a result of finding my new beliefs, the process of game development came to a new light. What was once a structural process of a step-by-step project changed to a new realm of possibilities and probabilities. Though the hobby does not directly contribute to finding the cure for cancer or solving poverty, I believe I may tie statistics with the development of video games to find solutions to certain dilemmas. Some may say it was a fall from grace, but I see it as an opportunity to present the facts that are hidden behind the screen.

I hope that by journeying to the University of Michigan, I may learn the theories of statistics that apply to situations that intertwine with real life. Elements of Statistical Learning provides theories corroborated by professors, and I desire to gain knowledge of what goes behind the lists of data. Not only am I looking forward to advancing in data visualization and Bayesian statistics provided by the Statistics curriculum, but there is a social portion that I hope to take part in: the seminars. University of Michigan's colors are blue and a specific yellow, known as maize. Blue is widely known as not only the color of sadness but also means imagination and wisdom. Maize represents bravery and sociability. Not only do these colors represent the school, but I believe they represent every individual under their roof. Seminars represent people for who they are. I hope that by partaking in the seminars hosted by the statistics department, not only will I network with different minds, but I will also represent the vibrant colors bolded in the University of Michigan's logo.

I may not be following my mother's path, nor my father's, but there is a path laid out for me. By following this path, I hope to see blue complimented by maize that leads me to the gates of Statistics. It may as well be my land of milk and honey.

essays.prompt: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate College or School (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (minimum 100 words/maximum 550 words)
essays.essay:
I am an aspiring business major with a specific interest in Finance and Entrepreneurship. The emphasis that Ross School of Business puts on learning by doing, social impact and its holistic, general management approach to teaching business is why I'm interested in Michigan Ross.

My interest in Finance is partially shaped by what I experienced this past summer. When I went to visit my grandmother in Turkey I was in for a surprise. Before arriving, I was dreaming of the incredible street food I could eat without worrying about my budget. In past years, my money has gone a long way in Turkey because of the purchasing power of the US Dollar. That was not the case this year. Everything was so much more expensive. It was sad to see how people, including my extended family in Turkey, were now poorer given the devaluing Turkish Lira year over year. I know that the Turkish Fed losing full independence and keeping interest rates artificially low had an effect and was a common topic of conversation there. I want to learn deeply about why this happens and how it can be prevented. I look forward to the Currency Markets - FIN 412 class taught by Prof Pasquariello to do so. I'm particularly interested in going beyond the numbers and finding out about the effects of economic and fiscal policies on business, international trade and people's lives. In turn, I will contribute by bringing to life what I have seen and lived with real examples, perhaps as part of a study abroad through the Global Initiatives Office.

My other area of interest is the intersection of social impact and entrepreneurship. During kindergarten, my teacher asked us to pick two words that are very important to us. I recently found a picture of me surrounded with the words I chose way back when: "believe" and "help". I found that picture right after I completed an internship with a startup that is creating a medical gel that prevents severe wounds in cancer patients. Part of the internship included work on a social impact project that helps a cooperative of Somalian growers of myrrh resin, the gel's key ingredient. At Ross, I will look for similar opportunities to make a difference. I already know I want to participate in the Zell Lurie Institute activities. Its Product Innovation Program is particularly interesting, including its current focus on climate tech. I saw the impact of recent climate change on the Somalian growers firsthand and it is profound. I would love to create ideas and build connections that will lead to a product launch.

Finally, I'm excited about the variety of clubs that the University of Michigan has to offer. Given my American, Dutch and Turkish family background and upbringing, I'm specifically interested in joining the International Center Student Council, where I will connect with and help others, should I be lucky enough to be part of Ross Business School.

essays.promptLabel: Why this school/college and major (Computer Science)
essays.prompt: Describe the unique qualities that attract you to the specific undergraduate College or School (including preferred admission and dual degree programs) to which you are applying at the University of Michigan. How would that curriculum support your interests? (550 words)
essays.essay:
There is no doubt that I love computer science. Creating web applications from scratch, setting up authentication methods, and "SSHing" into cloud servers are just a few of the things I adore about programming. I want to utilize these skills that I have acquired to start a business that will revolutionize the globe. This goal of mine may seem like a complete dream, but I believe my time at the University of Michigan will make this into a reality.

I believe that the University of Michigan's computer science program will help me advance my knowledge of various concepts. Courses such as Design and Analysis of Algorithms and Advanced Database Systems will teach me how to query large data but also develop efficient algorithms that analyze this data. I can strengthen my knowledge in dynamic programming, greedy, and searching which will assist me in creating fast and reliable applications. Additionally, delving into machine learning courses such as Natural Language Processing will help me implement increasingly popular concepts into my applications to significantly enhance their quality. In a world where artificial intelligence is becoming widely used, we must adapt and also integrate these new tools. This university's focused computer science program will help me utilize these ideas to achieve my dream of developing a product that will change the world.

At the University of Michigan I hope to join student groups in order to build connections and expand my knowledge. The Michigan Hackers group stood out to me as an excellent way to develop the necessary skills to create projects that use new technologies. Having already participated in a multitude of hackathons throughout high school, this group will further strengthen my knowledge in these fields while also fostering creativity and innovation. The Michigan EcoData group also caught my attention with its main mission to help the environment through technological inventions. As a member of Beyond Terra, which has a similar mission to preserve biodiversity through technological advancements, I worked with a team to construct and program a seeddrone. This seeddrone was filled with many seeds, and using a pathfinding algorithm, it would fly around a park to drop these seeds so that they could grow to become trees. The EcoData group can help me continue my passion for helping the environment while also increasing my skills in computer science.

Finally, I find core values to be extremely important. I have a certain moral compass that I like to follow, and the University of Michigan's values align with mine. This university's emphasis on honesty and integrity stood out to me as my dad has been instilling these ideals to me since I was a little kid. He always tells me to do the right thing even when no one is watching. Additionally, the importance of achievement and service resonated strongly with me. I have completed over 300 hours of community service through Boy Scout camps, tutoring services, and city organizations. If I were accepted to this university, I will participate in events that benefit the college and city, and I will put in my best work to ensure that everyone is satisfied.

I truly believe that my undevoted passion towards computer science coupled with the University of Michigan's vast resources and initiatives can help me become a better programmer, thinker, and person.

essays.school: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
essays.prompt: Discuss an academic topic that you're excited to explore and learn more about in college. Why does this topic interest you? Topics could be a specific course of study, research interests, or any other area related to your academic experience in college.
essays.essay:
In the summer of 7th grade, my dad introduced me to trading stocks. He gave me a small budget to play around with, and that lit a spark that's fueled my passion since. I started as a novice learning to execute trades with the "buy" or "sell" button, but I eventually became more strategic with my picks. I spent hours interpreting earnings reports, reading investor guides, and watching global news to make predictions about how stocks might react.

One learning moment was when I traded Alphabet stock, which beat its earnings but still plummeted several points in the after-hours. It was humbling, but made me want to understand the why even more. This taught me the volatility involved in day trading, along with the risk of strategies like lending shares and borrowing against an asset. Eventually, I switched to a safer, long-term strategy, investing my money into mutual funds that compounded over time while earning dividends.

At UNC, the Applied Investment Management course will allow me to gain hands-on experience in managing a portion of the university's endowment, where decisions carry real consequences. Being part of this selective group and collaborating on research, conducting valuations, and presenting to professionals mirrors the environment I hope to work in. I'm not a student who learns best just by taking notes and sitting in lectures; I'm a learner through trial and error, and AIM's approach enables me to experiment and learn from my decisions, the method of learning where I thrive.

essays.school: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
essays.prompt: Discuss one of your personal qualities and share a story, anecdote, or memory of how it helped you make a positive impact on a community. This could be your current community or another community you have engaged.
essays.essay:
4:1 – that's the ratio of Starbucks to local coffee shops in a suburb of my city. Coffee shops are my go-to place to cure procrastination, but getting a seat at Starbucks is a game of musical chairs. The local coffee shops on the other hand are empty most days and they struggle to compete with the coffee giants – I wanted to help change that.

I began this effort when I joined a local youth marketing association, where I used my analytical problem solving to help local businesses grow through social media. My first consultation was with a local rolled ice cream shop. On our first call, I crunched the numbers and discovered an alarmingly high customer acquisition cost at $4. It may not seem much, but this meant that the business would be operating off debt in no time.

Partnering with the owner, we cut costs immediately. We sourced ingredients locally for a better price, trimmed down the menu to reduce inventory costs, and optimized advertisements on Instagram, Yelp, and Facebook using a new happy-hour deal and holiday sales to attract customers. These simple, but decisive measures, helped the business turn profit within months, and they were able to reinvest their earnings into renovations.

Looking back, I'm proud to drive by the shop each time, reminding myself that I was able to use my problem solving skills to help keep a business going in my beloved community.

essays.promptLabel: Non-negotiable factor in your college search
essays.prompt: Everyone has different priorities when considering their higher education options and building their college or university list. Tell us about your "non-negotiable" factor(s) when searching for your future college home. (150 words)
essays.essay: With a 14-2 record as of the past season, and as a former athlete myself, a strong sports scene is a non-negotiable for whatever college I decide to go to. As a kid I have always been into sports from cricket, to tennis, soccer, and pickleball. Sports have been my way to get outside, get some exercise, but most importantly meet new people. Some of my closest friends have come from playing these sports, and I believe Notre Dame's football team will only continue that. Being in the stands in a Notre Dame vs. USC football game is the perfect place for me to not only have the time of my life, but find a community that is just as passionate as I am about sports. Oh and by the way, having a Chipotle nearby is a must as it's my go-to option when I'm hungry, especially after playing sports.

essays.promptLabel: A compliment you are proud of receiving
essays.prompt: What compliment are you most proud of receiving, and why does it mean so much to you? (50-100 words)
essays.essay: “Have a good one.” “You too.” Those 2 words, “you too,” are a compliment I receive often, but it is what I'm most proud of. It means a lot because it shows that the positivity or effort I put out into the world is being reflected back. It's small enough to the point where anyone can give me this compliment, but it's just the thought that keeps motivating me to do more good in the world. Even in a small exchange, being acknowledged in that way reminds me that my actions, no matter how small, affect others positively, and that's something I'm proud of.

essays.prompt: What is distinctive about your personal experiences and development (e.g., family support, culture, disability, personal background, community)? Why are these experiences important to you and how will you enrich the Notre Dame community? (50-100 words)
essays.essay: When I first came to America, I was the new kid in a small neighborhood in a new city. There I met my friend, at the time just a random person who quickly became a defining part of my journey. He introduced me to all of his friends, welcomed me in, and made me feel like I belonged. At Notre Dame I want to be the person to introduce the new kid and make them feel included just like my friend did for me. I hope to carry that same mindset forward, helping build an environment where everyone feels welcomed, valued, and at home.

essays.promptLabel: How you foster service to others
essays.prompt: Notre Dame's undergraduate experience is characterized by a collective sense of care for every person. How do you foster service to others in your community? (50-100 words)
essays.essay: I foster service to others in my community through free access to financial literacy. As a part of Youth Finance USA I have had the opportunity to teach 100s of students whether it's from an online workshop, or in person lessons, basic financial topics like budgeting, credit vs. debit, and investing. There I have been able to not just teach them lessons but skills that can help them throughout their lifetime.

essays.prompt: Wharton prepares its students to make an impact by applying business methods and economic theory to real-world problems, including economic, political, and social issues. Please reflect on a current issue of importance to you and share how you hope a Wharton education would help you to explore it.
essays.essay:
AI adoption is growing by the day, and to many, it's the future of technology. Especially in the world of finance, AI has a significant influence on human decision-making, enabling trades and the automatic building of investment portfolios. However, I've seen firsthand the limitations of AI, and overreliance can lead to the regression of human skills that were once developed through years of hands-on experience, experimentation, and failure.

Last year, I built my own AI model to predict stock movements based on social media sentiments. It was a passion project, and I became very curious about AI's accuracy. I learned after months of training that the model had an accuracy rate of 38%, great for beginners, but not enough to make a living from.

At Wharton, I want to explore these limitations further by researching fintech alongside other brilliant minds immersed in the AI world. I will participate in organizations focused on finance and investing, which will sharpen my skills to become a future leader. Through Penn, I will be able to develop qualities that help me adapt to a competitive workforce and engage with others in a collaborative environment.

essays.prompt: How will you explore your intellectual and academic interests at the University of Pennsylvania? Please answer this question given the specific undergraduate school to which you are applying. (300-450 words)
essays.essay:
In choosing a major, I have never had any doubt in my mind that Neuroscience would always be the way for me to go. I'm very excited to see how much I can challenge myself in the understanding of the sciences and be challenged by the Penn LSM Program.

When speaking about my readiness to success in the field, I always turn back into my experiences. I started being the representative for the Society for Neuroscience Speaker Events at my high school in 2016 and have been promoting awareness for neuroscience as a field and a possible career path at our school. In this post, I reached out to many students who were academically brilliant but weren't sure just yet which field they wanted to major in after graduating high school. It seems daunting to a 12 year old when being asked where they see themselves when they finally join the work force as we were all just discovering who we are as people. But with a good team, we found and fostered candidates that were equally dedicated to biology and psychology. We then started taking several steps by strategically placing ourselves in activities such as attending neuroscience-related conventions where we hobnobbed with professionals in Southern California and received grounded advice in career choices.

As I delved deeper into the medical community through my research, I recognized the prevalence of problem-solving in every situation. As I shadowed two family physicians, I realized how problem-solving has played a role in finding the cause of every symptom.

Specifically, in one situation, a patient came in with shoulder and back pain. While he believed the source of the issue came from his COPD, the physician was suspicious of this judgment. The physician was able to implement his problem-solving skills to diagnose the pain with ease, and he concluded that the pain was muscular in origin since the pain was more associated with soreness and achiness, as opposed to a tightness, which is the type of pain associated with COPD.

While being a physician requires a strong background in science, it also requires a sense of analytical thinking, and confidence in your own procedures and conclusions.

Taking advantage of the state of the art facilities offered at Penn, I'll be able to do advanced research with other aspiring physicians like me, giving us students front-row access to technological advantage that are not easy to come by. Also thoroughly impressed with the encouraged networking within alumni and undergraduates, it is easy to see not just the many possible career paths, but also the good impact I could bring forward to the larger discussion of American healthcare policies with the education I'm looking to obtain.

essays.prompt: At Penn, learning and growth happen outside of the classroom, too. How will you explore the community at Penn? Consider how this community will help shape your perspective and identity, and how your identity and perspective will help shape this community. (150-200 words)
essays.essay:
I'm really excited about forming tight bonds with fellow students and perhaps some of the esteemed faculty at Penn. As I have always been in neuroscience clubs in high school, I'll seek out a club in Penn that caters to this specific area where I can be more encouraged and guided by my seniors. Through this type of activity, my leadership skills and preparedness for the work force will be honed more.

As an incoming freshman, I actually see myself taking in the Locust Walk and the history that has been made there, as well as socializing outside my block. Be it through shared passions in the medical and biological field, my fondness for creative art, self-expression through fashion, and practicing classical song and dance, I'm looking into growing my social skills and start networking at a young age. I'm also looking forward into finding more about myself through physical activities. As I've seen, Penn has gyms available to students who'd like to maintain their bodies in tiptop shape, plenty of good places to run, and several courts. I already find myself thinking about the friendships I can develop, working out while exploring exciting ideas with the friends I'll make.

essays.prompt: How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn. (150-200 words)
essays.essay:
Born to a Turkish mother and Dutch father in America, I've always been surrounded by different cultures. Instead of choosing one side, I've learned to bridge these cultures to form an identity that's uniquely mine. This perspective shaped my response when the devastating Turkey-Syria earthquakes struck. I rallied my school's support in a fundraiser to aid the children I taught English to in that area - uniting communities of people to help make a difference. Yet, this effort wasn't just about the donation, it was about encouraging the feeling of empathy for others, turning international headlines into a shared experience.

Through Penn's unique community offerings, I look to continue fostering connections. The Greenfield Intercultural Center will provide a hub to have passionate global discussions and bond over topics from politics to Pokémon cards. The Intercultural Leadership Program within ISSS will enable me to unite international students with those raised in the US. Additionally, as Penn shapes my identity as a connector, I'll use what I've learned to host my own community gatherings - from informal cultural exchanges to international potlucks. Above all, whether through a community service event or a shared meal, I hope to do what I do best: bring people together.

essays.prompt: How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn.
essays.essay:
I would start by exploring the Penn community through the Garden Club at Stouffer College House. This is the right starting point as I'll meet others who love doing garden work as much as I do.

At Penn, I'd like to bring this passion forward by promoting the idea of expanding beyond flowers and into the world of planting fruits and vegetables. Here at our 4-H garden, we have revamped our garden from just flowers, dead and alive, to a whole array of fruits and vegetables that we plan on donating. Even though it's a lengthier process, knowing it's for a good cause is what pushes us to make sure everything gets watered consistently, and gives us all the more reason to feel proud when we donate our produce to the community.

At Penn, I hope to be refined rather than changed. I want to carry all my passion, values, and beliefs, but also thrive in the spontaneity of joining new organizations to expand my mind. I truly look forward to blending in at Penn, but also standing out as a contributor.

essays.promptLabel: Huntsman Program - business and international studies
essays.prompt: The Huntsman Program supports the development of globally-minded scholars who become engaged citizens, creative innovators, and ethical leaders in the public, private, and non-profit sectors in the United States and internationally. What draws you to a dual-degree in business and international studies, and how would you use what you learn to make a contribution to a global issue where business and international affairs intersect? (400-650 words)
essays.essay:
My parents sold to me a grand vision of my future; a future replete with white coats and stethoscopes. For a while, I bought into this idea because it made sense. Like any good physician, I loved digging into details, solving puzzles, and did well under pressure. Yet, I ventured into a shoe reselling business that inspired me to do more with entrepreneurship. I even tried to sell this idea back to my parents - "business is a soft skill," they'd say. So, doctor it was.

Heeding their advice, I stashed entrepreneurial spirit to the backlogs and instead, went all in on biology. The summer before sophomore year, I interviewed and accepted an internship at a science-based incubation lab in Istanbul called Technopark.

At Technopark, beyond assisting the setup of a new research facility, I was given the opportunity to develop my own hand cream formula and worked with teams across the globe. The following summer, I was invited back to work closely with the incubation team. There, I researched exosomes and their role in healing wounds in topical solutions, visited production lines where artificial diamonds were made, and saw water transporting drones in its developmental phases.

This incredible exposure to the world of startups and international organizations inadvertently led me back to business. I sat in financial board meetings, listened to supply chains discuss strategies to reduce overhead costs and grow globally, and observed negotiations between manufacturers and startups. It was a lot to take in, but this internship enabled me to see that the development of new technologies are not always rooted in the name of science, but in the opportunity to grow a profitable business.

In junior year, I've made decisions. I'm committed to trading my white coats and stethoscopes for a future in business. My parents may be right that business is a soft skill, but I've come to realize that it requires the same resilience, creativity, and passion as any medical practice, and my internship experience was the final stone that needed to be turned for me to chase this passion with confidence.

essays.prompt: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!) (150-200 words)
essays.essay:
To my teacher,

As my preschool teacher, you taught me how to speak English when I only knew a mix of Turkish and Dutch. With daily Belarussian and piano trivia, you made sure I was always learning something new and discovering something about the world. When I felt left out because of how I talked, you encouraged me to make new friends. You taught me how to explore.

A few years later, I came to you for piano lessons and I was in for a surprise. Instead of the sweet teacher I remembered, I was met with a strict teacher. Sometimes I cried. Yet, there were moments where the cold exterior would melt away and I would see my gentle preschool teacher again, still making sure I was on the right path. I was never your most talented student, but you stuck through with me. In turn, I learned that dedication and discipline can best any talent.

Today, the foundation you laid in me is finally bearing its fruits. I just graduated from piano and soon I will be in college. But no matter what, I'll never forget what you've done for me.

Thank you.

essays.prompt: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!)
essays.essay:
Dear Mr. [Teacher],

Even though you've transferred schools, you're still my favorite teacher at my high school! Your upbeat personality and enthusiasm made every class feel special. Your class was the only class where I could truly be myself – where I could freely express myself without repercussions and have the time of my life. I have so many fond memories, but one of my favorites was when my group did a presentation on burritos. I've never seen a group pull this off, but you let us make a burrito in class. This was the first presentation I went to without fear, had a good laugh, and actually enjoyed every minute of it.

As a nervous freshman coming into your class, I was hesitant to interact with adults. You were the first adult at my high school where I felt comfortable talking freely, without fear of judgement. Your Speech and Debate class was transformative in building my confidence and shaping who I am today. It helped me conquer my fear of public speaking and really gave me room to mature. You even inspired me to join the Speech and Debate Club, which led me to achieve success I could never imagine. I hope you come back to visit, so I can personally thank you for what you've done in my life.

Sincerely,

essays.prompt: Wharton prepares its students to make an impact by applying business methods and economic theory to real-world problems, including economic, political, and social issues. Please reflect on a current issue of importance to you and share how you hope a Wharton education would help you to explore it. (150-200 words)
essays.essay:
My nonprofit Overstress began as a medium to address the adverse mental health effects of COVID. Rather than tackle this issue traditionally, my cofounder and I imbued a more creative process. As a tennis player, I saw upcycling as an opportunity to repurpose discarded tennis balls. Immediately, I scoured my area and called local landscape companies, leveraging wood chippers and eventually reaching out to another nonprofit: Recycleballs. With their help, we successfully converted hundreds of used tennis balls into a fluffy substance to create squishy stress balls.

This experience opened me to the issue of waste across the world, and how upcycling can be used as a medium to tackle issues like global warming while contributing to a circular economy. Working with Kobac General Trading in Somalia, my interest in upcycling has only increased as they have revealed the extensive waste that comes with trading companies. I've learned that companies often produce a surprising amount of waste, and with a Wharton education, I could implement my upcycling initiatives on a global scale. In turn, not only will companies be able to increase their revenues, but the many negative externalities that come with waste can be addressed directly - creating a cleaner world.

essays.prompt: The University of Rochester benefactor, entrepreneur, photography pioneer and philanthropist George Eastman said, "The progress of the world depends almost entirely upon education." With that statement in mind, how will you use your University of Rochester experience to foster positive change in order to make the world, your community and those around you "ever better?" (essay or research response of 250 words)
essays.essay:
I would agree that education provides the building blocks for progress, but more important is the individual attitudes and aspirations that help to realize such changes.

I would like to be building upon my interest in psychology and neuroscience, namely my experience at UC Santa Cruz where I learned about the migration and differentiation of different neurons as they related to specific neurological conditions such as ALS and Autism. There'd been quite a debacle, as of late, on what exactly causes these conditions, some being more grounded in actual science and some unfortunately being complete hokum.

With Rochester's commitment to good methodologies and state-of-the-art laboratories, I could find my future self furthering the scientific explorations I've already tried in the past - such as the examinations and sectioning of mice brains in conducting PCR and Gel Electrophoresis. Within these competitive learning conditions, I'd like to further understand the physiological truth behind such neurological deviances, and compliment them with actual biological work; and in the process become an advocate of the scientific truth about such conditions.

Of course, comfort is also a cornerstone of the modern day America. In a country where healthcare is not easily affordable and is in a constant debate as to whether being properly or not properly supported, I would like to dedicate my future research into finding substantial data that may one day alleviate rare illnesses that didn't get proper funding, staffing, and support and at least finding affordable alternatives to costly treatments.

essays.prompt: How did you learn about Rochester's Combined Degree Program and what relevant experiences or insight have led to your interest in applying to this particular program? Describe how Rochester's facilities, faculty, peers and research will meet your academic and personal ambitions. Describe your confidence to succeed in the challenging profession(s) you want to enter as a Rochester graduate. (500 words)
essays.essay:
Fostering an atmosphere where diversity, future-orientedness, and liberalism are encouraged, I find myself in adoration with the progressive approach Rochester has with education. Even with the campus being geographically distant from where I'm from, the name itself had always rang bells - with people always speaking highly of the culture of both the institution and New York itself.

I found my love for medicine and science at an early age, and I want a program that exhibits as much commitment to medicine as I do. Through my exhaustive search to find the perfect university for me to further my interest in the brain and cognitive sciences, I found Rochester's Combined Degree Program to be a perfect fit for a girl like me who isn't a stranger to taking on big challenges.

I am confident that at Rochester, I will accomplish more than just good grades, but I will make it my duty to stay involved in extracurricular activities offered in and out of campus. Even in high school, I've never limited myself to the scope of getting good grades. I held positions as a research officer in the Neuroscience Club at my high school, as a student representative and panel speaker for the Society for Neuroscience, and as a volunteer at a local hospital as well as a Veterans Affairs hospital. More recently, I've had the amazing opportunity of shadowing a child psychiatrist which has given me a thorough exploration into the hectic, yet exciting, world of a physician. Juggling all of these tasks over the last three years, I still appropriated my spare time to practice Indian classical dance and singing for 10 years for which I have received a Bachelor of Dance from the Art Society of Mumbai and a Carnatic Chamber Concert Competition Recognition award.

Now, when asked why I am confident in my abilities as a medical school prospect, I turn to these past accomplishments and employ my organization skills, inquisitiveness, and level-headedness to reassure myself that I can succeed at anything I put my heart and mind into. My commitment to the medical profession has really distinguished itself from the many academic interests that I carry, and my past extracurricular involvements are more than just an indication of my zeal, but also a reminder of all the milestones that I had to overcome to date.

I believe that with the help of Rochester's state of the art facilities, I'll be able to progress with other aspiring physicians like me - giving us students front row access to technological advantages that are not easy to come by. I am thoroughly impressed with the encouraged networking within Rochester - as with the campus' and alumni's connections to many companies, research centers, and healthcare facilities - it is easy to see the career paths that I could invest my time into and the impact that I could humbly bring forward to the world around me with the education I can obtain as a Rochesterian.

essays.prompt: USF supplemental (prompt not stated in document; inferred): Reflect on how you would embody the university's Jesuit values in your chosen field. Prompt inferred.
essays.essay:
My desire to become a Nurse was deeply rooted in the many times I spent at hospitals because cancer ran through my family. I've seen how hardworking nurses work to ensure the best hospitality, nourishing patients by making them feel comfortable and seen.

Some of the many responsibilities of a Jesuit-educated, BSN professional registered nurse are upholding values such as advocating for marginalized communities and promoting equity, not as a trend, but as a responsibility, and volunteering with groups of people who believe in justice through daily actions. By exploring different environments and meeting new people, I am open to any beliefs and backgrounds, making ethical decisions that include the common good.

Additionally, I would embody a cura personalis—the idea that who you are matters more than what you produce. This trait would foster good self-awareness and reflection habits that will guide me through the challenging obstacles of being a nurse, driven by "The More." Through Magis, I will strive to transform hardships into opportunities for success and grow into the best version of myself–not pressure and perfectionism. Lastly, as a Jesuit-educated nurse, I'll utilize my knowledge on global awareness and cultural understanding to empathize with various patients.

essays.prompt: What skills do you find most useful in adapting to changing environments? (250 words)
essays.essay:
When I began my internship at Ernst and Young in Istanbul, I had no idea I would be debating on who the tennis GOAT is. Rather, I was busy rehearsing “ö" and “ç" sounds and doing everything in my power to fit in with my native Turkish peers. Then I met an older colleague, whom I learned was once a top 1200 ranked tennis player. Soon, walks to the lunch center and momentary breaks were filled with eager exchanges about the rise of Jannik Sinner. I finally felt my passions speaking louder than any of my mispronounced words.

For the remainder of my internship, instead of memorizing pronunciations I focused on seeking connections; while topics like travel, politics, and history were great conversation starters, fascinations in eccentric interests like anime cosplay and pokemon cards became the cornerstones for friendships.

Just as important as any of my presentations or audits, my EY internship taught me how common interests are the strongest connectors. I know that as humans we have more that unites than separates us, and I’m determined to prove it. When I find myself in a new environment, I know I can rely on these experiences to find a new friend. The ability to communicate, empathize with others, and remain flexible has proved invaluable. Change can be scary, but learning how to make connections and understand other perspectives are what inspire me to grow.
